> # 0021. Stage HAQP-1 qualification around Phase 1 authorization
> 
> - **Status:** accepted
> - **Date:** 2026-08-08
> - **Deciders:** Brian
> - **Related:** ADR-0020; M17 (AM-17.2, AM-17.4); M24;
>   `docs/execution/m17-5-adversarial-findings.md` F-28
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-5b8872b927651c18c78c -->

<a id="source-2e271f75fd428eb3cb1b"></a>

Classification: `context`. Original lines 9–41; text SHA-256: `a6f5cf4a93602802a3b68ac927293246dfe6ce510abe362fc9c780fcccd4c727`.

<!-- source-block:source-2e271f75fd428eb3cb1b -->
> ## Context
> 
> ADR-0020 requires, in §3, that qualification predeclare **at least 64 semantic
> mutants** and achieve a **100% kill rate**, with one survivor blocking
> eligibility. M17.5's exit criterion inherits that requirement.
> 
> M17.5 finding **F-28** established that the requirement is currently
> unsatisfiable, and not through any defect in the packet. The 65 declared mutants
> name **35 distinct killing tests**. Measured 2026-08-03:
> 
> | killing tests | state |
> |---|---|
> | 27 | did not exist — they were strings in `packet.json` and nothing else |
> | 8 | exist, `#[ignore]`d under the AM-17.2 Phase 1 quarantine |
> | **0** | **runnable** |
> 
> Twenty of the 27 have since been written (`conformance/tests/milestones/m18–m23`)
> and all pass, but they remain quarantined: they are Phase 1 exit gates, and
> AM-17.2 exists because F-02 found Phase 1 gates pre-greened while Phase 1 was
> unauthorized. The remaining seven have no subject to test — there is no `lim fmt`
> command, no benchmark baseline, and no M24 aggregate gate.
> 
> Lifting the quarantine requires Phase 1 authorization. Phase 1 authorization
> comes from M17.6's GO/NO-GO, which is sequenced **after** M17.5. So M17.5 cannot
> complete, and no amount of M17.5 work changes that.
> 
> The underlying cause is simpler than the mechanics suggest: **ADR-0020 §3
> assumed the suite it mutates already exists.** For every other evidence kind
> that assumption holds — fuzz, crash, generated, canaries and reviews all run
> against artifacts Phase 0 produces. For mutants it does not. A suite that has
> not been written cannot be mutation-tested, and predeclaring the tests a future
> milestone will write is exactly what an inventory is for.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-2e271f75fd428eb3cb1b -->

<a id="source-2148f4c9e99db739c8eb"></a>

Classification: `normative-clause`. Original lines 42–45; text SHA-256: `4674aa54119fcfc71e0277eebdfb9688cde3b92076da94c1a89ad68fe6307d11`.

<!-- source-block:source-2148f4c9e99db739c8eb -->
> ## Decision
> 
> HAQP-1 SHALL be evaluated in **two stages**, gated on Phase 1 authorization.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-2148f4c9e99db739c8eb -->

<a id="source-ef0b6e49c5c561b1f76b"></a>

Classification: `mixed-clause`. Original lines 46–63; text SHA-256: `2741659a78d94950781adeaccd9c060506195f19921f1548c79b6b6df2733352`.

<!-- source-block:source-ef0b6e49c5c561b1f76b -->
> ### HAQP-1a — provable before Phase 1
> 
> Everything ADR-0020 requires **except** the mutant clauses of §3:
> 
> - §1 fixed clean tree and two execution lanes
> - §2 bidirectional traceability
> - §3's **gate canaries** — every ratification gate keeps its disposable canary.
>   Canaries run against the packet's own gates, not against Phase 1 tests, so
>   they are provable now and remain in 1a.
> - §4 generated, metamorphic and fuzz evidence
> - §5 oracle and fault independence
> - §6 two independent adversarial reviews
> - §7 bounded campaign and residual risk
> 
> Satisfying HAQP-1a makes the packet eligible for M17.6's GO/NO-GO. It does
> **not** ratify the Phase 1 suite, and it does not claim the suite detects seeded
> defects.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-ef0b6e49c5c561b1f76b -->

<a id="source-e9c295f4f14956dde4d3"></a>

Classification: `mixed-clause`. Original lines 64–79; text SHA-256: `df941151b0a171f09d46844762437df2493b654356bb2e02ffde4560ee796f75`.

<!-- source-block:source-e9c295f4f14956dde4d3 -->
> ### HAQP-1b — the mutation requirement, deferred to M24
> 
> These §3 clauses defer verbatim, with no threshold weakened:
> 
> - at least 64 semantic mutants across critical surfaces, with the declared
>   operator set
> - at least eight mutants per critical surface family; no operator supplying more
>   than a quarter of the denominator
> - 100% kill of applicable, non-duplicate, non-equivalent mutants; one survivor
>   blocks
> - equivalent/duplicate dispositions naming the mutant, showing the proof, and
>   carrying concurring verification in both adversarial-pass records
> 
> HAQP-1b runs at **M24**, when M18–M23 have written their tests and the gates are
> legitimately un-ignored. Phase 1 suite ratification requires **both** stages.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-e9c295f4f14956dde4d3 -->

<a id="source-9704129039889f88f55e"></a>

Classification: `mixed-clause`. Original lines 80–88; text SHA-256: `74b4c9d66f7483a092516b427fe070b4289b2ca39ff2a4349fc460f4a4b23f92`.

<!-- source-block:source-9704129039889f88f55e -->
> ### What this does not permit
> 
> - It does not un-ignore any Phase 1 gate. AM-17.2 stands.
> - It does not lower the mutation bar. Every threshold in §3 survives intact into
>   1b; only its evaluation point moves.
> - It does not let a stage-1a packet claim mutant kills. The packet records
>   `qualification_stage`, and `verify_qualified_repo` rejects a 1a packet whose
>   mutants claim `killed` and a 1b packet whose mutants do not.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-9704129039889f88f55e -->

<a id="source-7a2dd6f4632eacb730ee"></a>

Classification: `mixed-clause`. Original lines 89–137; text SHA-256: `fae2c7a443530346a9c280afe26bad5d3dbb82c571d10de1771c7fd301ea1a02`.

<!-- source-block:source-7a2dd6f4632eacb730ee -->
> ## Consequences
> 
> - M17.5 becomes completable: its exit criterion is HAQP-1a (AM-17.4).
> - Phase 1 ratification gains a second, later gate at M24 rather than losing one.
>   The suite is qualified against the tests that actually exist at each point.
> - The mutation evidence, when it arrives, will be stronger than it would have
>   been now: it will measure the real Phase 1 suite rather than a suite of
>   predeclared names.
> - A reader of a `complete` packet must check which stage completed. The stage is
>   a required field precisely so that check cannot be skipped.
> - **RESOLVED (M17.5 F-33, closed 2026-09-03):** this previously disclosed that
>   36 of the 65 declared mutants were anchored to declarations — function
>   signatures and enum variants — which no operator can mutate, leaving 29
>   against a floor of 64, and deferred the repair to 1b.
> 
>   The disclosure did not survive contact with §6. A blind reviewer rediscovered
>   it on 2026-09-02 at six coordinates and returned six verified defects, and a
>   finding can only be cleared by a commit that changes the code at its
>   coordinate — there is no "resolved by disclosure" path, by design. A defect
>   that is documented but not fixed still fails the gate, which is the correct
>   behaviour and the reason the disclosure was the wrong instrument.
> 
>   The plan was re-anchored instead: every declared mutant now names a line where
>   its declared operator can genuinely be applied, 17 operators were corrected
>   where the original 5×13 grid had assigned an operator to a family whose code
>   cannot exhibit it (F-06's finding, in the specific), no two mutants share an
>   anchor, and the heaviest operator supplies 12.3% against §3's 25% cap.
>   Dispositions remain `predeclared`: re-anchoring makes the declarations TRUE,
>   it does not claim a kill, so it is 1a work and 1b's evaluation is untouched.
> 
> - **RESOLVED by definition (M17.5 A05, AM-17.7 → AM-17.8, closed 2026-09-04):**
>   AM-17.7 scoped §5's "exhaustive registered crash boundaries" to ILRP and
>   disclosed that the runtime's other ~30 fsynced durable transitions were out of
>   scope. That was a disclosure without a criterion. AM-17.8 supplies one: a
>   registrable crash boundary is a point where a crash leaves state that recovery
>   must *reconcile*. ILRP's eight protocol steps qualify. A single checksummed log
>   append does not — it either landed or it did not, and recovery is the
>   longest-checksummed-prefix rule `store/log.rs` documents and
>   `prop_torn_tail_truncates_cleanly` proves. The registry stays at eight because
>   eight is the count of reconciliation points, not because the rest were
>   deferred. `packet.crash_boundary_scope` carries the criterion and
>   `verify_crash_boundary_scope` still pins every transition to a declared surface.
> 
> - **Disclosed limitation:** between M17.6 and M24, Phase 1 proceeds on a suite
>   whose defect-detection power has been argued but not measured. That is a real
>   risk and it is accepted deliberately, because the alternative — building
>   Phase 1 first so the suite can be mutated, then qualifying — inverts ADR-0020's
>   purpose entirely.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-7a2dd6f4632eacb730ee -->

<a id="source-2d0460fcce6e96dc53f6"></a>

Classification: `context`. Original lines 138–153; text SHA-256: `7ff2507df91bcd1fd089c26ba2c9f3e491b333d64ca05cd91ed70cde406e2e47`.

<!-- source-block:source-2d0460fcce6e96dc53f6 -->
> ## Alternatives considered
> 
> - **Re-target the 65 mutants at surfaces whose tests are active today**
>   (`liminal-format` unit tests, the law canaries, the fuzz regression corpus).
>   Makes §3 satisfiable immediately, and the campaign has already measured those
>   surfaces. Rejected as the primary answer because it narrows the claim from
>   "the Phase 1 suite detects seeded defects" to "the Phase 1 substrate does",
>   which is a weaker statement than ADR-0020 wrote down and would be recorded
>   under the same name. Nothing prevents doing this additionally within 1a as
>   supporting evidence, provided it is not labelled as satisfying §3.
> - **Authorize Phase 1 first and qualify at exit.** Removes the circularity, and
>   inverts the point of the profile: Phase 1 would be built before the suite
>   judging it was trusted, which is F-02 at full scale.
> - **Lift AM-17.2 for the qualification run only.** Deliberately repeating F-02.
>   The gate F-28 added exists specifically to refuse this, and removing it to
>   pass would be tuning the measure.
<!-- /source-block:source-2d0460fcce6e96dc53f6 -->

<!-- source-block:source-d458f0d7e36c453c085c -->
> # Execution protocol — the executor rulebook
> 
> This directory contains **execution-grade work orders**: every decision is pre-made,
> so any executor — a junior developer or an AI agent — implements mechanically. The
> work orders `M01.md`–`M12.md` cover Phase -1 in full mechanical detail;
> `M13.md`–`M17.md` cover Phase 0; `phases.md` holds the Phase 0–12 work breakdown;
> `template.md` is the mandatory skeleton for every future order. This file is the
> contract the executor operates under.
> 
> Spec citations: "v4 §N" = `spec/v4/liminal_master_architecture_plan_v4.md`;
> "R4 §N" = `spec/v4/liminal_architecture_revision_4.md`. The spec is canonical;
> the work orders are its mechanical projection.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-d458f0d7e36c453c085c -->

<a id="source-42bfb60ceb9a572d1646"></a>

Classification: `mixed-clause`. Original lines 14–37; text SHA-256: `b5d155d5ebeba32663374f7ecf52a5614f2211e5bb55e26336abd33deb79c7d0`.

<!-- source-block:source-42bfb60ceb9a572d1646 -->
> ## 1. Definition of done
> 
> A milestone is done when, and only when:
> 
> 1. Every test named in the work order's **Exit gate** table either (a) was authored
>    `#[ignore = "Phase N M<n>: …"]` at the preceding phase gate and flips to
>    passing, or (b) — when the preceding gate did not name it — is **created
>    un-ignored and born passing** in the exact file the work order specifies.
>    Creating a new ignored exit-gate test during milestone execution is forbidden;
>    Phase 0+ backlog stubs are authored only at the preceding gate per `phases.md`.
> 2. Assertions are **UNWEAKENED**. The assertion text in each test's doc comment and
>    in the work order is the contract. Weakening — loosening a comparison, deleting
>    an assert, shrinking a matrix, converting byte-equality to substring, adding
>    retries, widening a timeout to hide a hang — is a **spec change**: stop, write an
>    ADR, get it accepted before the change lands. `retries = 0` in
>    `.config/nextest.toml` is itself a frozen assertion.
> 3. `just ci` passes end to end (fmt-check, clippy `-Dwarnings`, nextest ci profile,
>    doctests, rustdoc `-Dwarnings`, cargo-deny).
> 4. `just gates` shows exactly the delta the work order predicts (which ignored
>    counts decrease, by how much). Any other delta is a finding, recorded in the
>    order's **Discovered gaps**.
> 5. Every previously passing test still passes. There are no known-flaky exemptions;
>    a flaky crash test is a finding, never retried away.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-42bfb60ceb9a572d1646 -->

<a id="source-5dbf013eebfb973af8e4"></a>

Classification: `mixed-clause`. Original lines 38–62; text SHA-256: `9db0ef2a8a12a92a09607ad037f9076db1a8a9c48d54b506ac4c3313e01fd10b`.

<!-- source-block:source-5dbf013eebfb973af8e4 -->
> ## 2. API-freeze rule
> 
> The scaffold's public signatures — everything in each work order's **Frozen
> surfaces** list — are frozen. The executor implements `todo!()` bodies; the executor
> does not rename, re-parameterize, re-home, or "improve" frozen items.
> 
> **Amendment procedure** (the only path when a frozen signature cannot work or a
> needed item does not exist):
> 
> 1. Stop implementing the affected step.
> 2. Write the amendment into the work order's **Amendments** section as
>    `AM-<milestone>.<n>`: what changes, why the frozen shape cannot work, which call
>    sites are affected.
> 3. Record the amendment in the active phase ledger. Phase -1 used the historical
>    `docs/adr/0008-phase-minus-1-execution-amendments.md`; Phase 0+ uses the
>    mutable `docs/execution/phase<n>-amendments.md` ledger and ratifies or reverts
>    every row in one immutable ADR at that phase's final gate. Entry format:
>    `AM-<m>.<n> (M<nn>): <one sentence>`.
> 4. Only then edit code.
> 
> Purely **additive** items (new modules, new pub fns, new trait impls on existing
> types, new constants, struct fields added with `#[serde(default)]`) are
> pre-authorized when the work order lists them; list any others in Amendments anyway
> for the audit trail. Every AM is ratified or reverted at the active phase gate.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-5dbf013eebfb973af8e4 -->

<a id="source-9f33f809bd92d1d276ee"></a>

Classification: `mixed-clause`. Original lines 63–75; text SHA-256: `579f19dcb7e4735af1da7593a107e191462ae0be66aa147f30f6a20b9f76657c`.

<!-- source-block:source-9f33f809bd92d1d276ee -->
> ## 3. Ambiguity procedure
> 
> If a work order under-specifies anything — a field's serialization, an ordering, an
> error path, an env var, a filename — the executor **STOPS** on that step and records
> the gap in the order's **Discovered gaps** section: what is ambiguous, the candidate
> readings, which step is blocked. Continue only with later steps that provably do not
> depend on the gap; otherwise halt the milestone and surface the gap.
> 
> **Never improvise semantics.** This project is a falsification laboratory: an
> improvised semantic silently becomes the thing under test, and the experiment stops
> measuring the spec. An invented behavior that happens to pass poisons every
> downstream conclusion.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-9f33f809bd92d1d276ee -->

<a id="source-312e6d6e6945c7b92c85"></a>

Classification: `mixed-clause`. Original lines 76–86; text SHA-256: `49c101c33497f8e67935b8ee4e79526d2e0593df63511ddb0386f164536a4acc`.

<!-- source-block:source-312e6d6e6945c7b92c85 -->
> ## 4. The mechanical loop
> 
> 1. Read the work order top to bottom before touching any file.
> 2. Implement steps strictly in listed order. Do not reorder, batch, or "get ahead".
> 3. After each step, run that step's listed command and compare against the listed
>    expected output.
> 4. Flip (or create) exactly the tests the step lists — no others.
> 5. After the last step: `just ci`, then `just gates`; verify the predicted delta.
> 6. Update the order's checkboxes (`- [ ]` → `- [x]`) as each step's command passes.
>    The checkbox edit belongs in that step's commit.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-312e6d6e6945c7b92c85 -->

<a id="source-a5abd8b119a8c97ae952"></a>

Classification: `mixed-clause`. Original lines 87–113; text SHA-256: `8cdea0e125447374f61c9e175255d8438d1fde1c0878b054e4a2cdd9e79addc8`.

<!-- source-block:source-a5abd8b119a8c97ae952 -->
> ## 5. Standing prohibitions
> 
> Mirror of `docs/implementation-plan.md` §4 — violating one is an ADR-level event:
> 
> 1. `CompiledJurisdictionPlan`, indexed dispatch, generated policy code (v4 §125).
> 2. Any CRDT or OT implementation (R4 §11.7).
> 3. Real parser, CST, or rope — the M3 ~50-line toy grammar is the entire Phase -1
>    surface (v4 §9, Law 14).
> 4. Agenda subsystem or vocabulary (`no_agenda_symbols` greps for it) (R4 §9).
> 5. Sync, cloud, or Git-as-sync (v4 §88).
> 6. Real editors or the Liminal Document Protocol (v4 §58).
> 7. Persistent socket daemon — `liminald` stays exec-and-exit.
> 8. Production store work (speed, GC, generality) — the toy store exists to be
>    crashed and read with eyes (ADR-0007).
> 9. Performance work, salsa, benchmark gates (Law 14, v4 §116).
> 10. `FacetId` or any third primitive (v4 §7.2, Law 1).
> 11. Rich UI, badges, notifications (R4 §3).
> 12. Schemas, macros, transforms, plugins, AI, HTML backend (phase-gated).
> 13. Overlay GC or archival tooling (Law 3I).
> 14. **Held-out-corpus ban:** never open, read, tune against, or hash-update
>     anything under a locked `heldout/` corpus version. Drift is caught by
>     `verify_heldout_manifest`; the fix for drift is a new corpus version, never an
>     edit (v4 §7.4).
> 
> Plus the **test-weakening ban** (§1.2) and: never delete or rename an `#[ignore]`d
> backlog test — the ignored set is the backlog; it shrinks only by passing.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-a5abd8b119a8c97ae952 -->

<a id="source-fbd8deab77ac1793ce16"></a>

Classification: `mixed-clause`. Original lines 114–125; text SHA-256: `fe7b5ed0b3593ac0afed373b9629e5390ec7f5afeec72f7ca13994415afacea9`.

<!-- source-block:source-fbd8deab77ac1793ce16 -->
> ## 6. Commit conventions
> 
> - One commit per work-order step: `M<nn>.<step> <area>: <imperative summary>` —
>   e.g. `M02.4 liminal-daemon: FsExecutor verify/apply for WriteFile`.
> - The step's code, its tests, and its checkbox flip land in the same commit. Never
>   mix steps.
> - Amendments commit separately, **before** the code that needs them:
>   `M<nn> amendment AM-<m>.<n>: <summary>` (includes the work-order Amendments entry
>   and the active phase-ledger entry; ADR-0008 is used only for Phase -1 history).
> - Commit bodies cite spec sections (`v4 §7.8`, `R4 §10`) for anything semantically
>   load-bearing.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-fbd8deab77ac1793ce16 -->

<a id="source-49371b0fe52b13f3da5a"></a>

Classification: `mixed-clause`. Original lines 126–166; text SHA-256: `059412558a7222ace221bd980bf86a80f15d95d53e7e71fdee9dad8126a2f381`.

<!-- source-block:source-49371b0fe52b13f3da5a -->
> ## 7. Executor tiers
> 
> Every work-order step carries a tier tag `[T1]`–`[T4]`. A tier describes the
> **level of responsibility the step demands** — not which model or person
> executes it. Anyone may execute above a step's tier; never below. The tag is a
> floor of care.
> 
> - **T1 — mission critical; human-grade / extreme rigor.** An error here can
>   pass the tests and still poison the architecture, or the step's output IS
>   constitutional. The executor must bring the project's highest scrutiny, and
>   the result gets an independent second look before it lands. T1 steps include:
>   the ILRP driver core, the auto-apply conjunction, freezing any constitutive
>   golden, the corpus-lock ceremony, the M12 audit and go/no-go, and Phase-gate
>   work-order authoring.
> - **T2 — implementation-level judgment.** The algorithm is fully specified, but
>   realizing it well requires real engineering decisions: data-structure and
>   error-path choices, edge handling, invariant-preserving refactors. Mistakes
>   are usually caught by the oracles, but poor judgment degrades the experiment.
> - **T3 — minor implementation details only.** The shape is fully given; the
>   executor writes idiomatic Rust filling small gaps (naming, small helpers,
>   test scaffolding). No semantic choices exist to make.
> - **T4 — mechanical.** Pure transcription and task execution: code or config
>   given verbatim in the order, file moves, ignore-flips, checkbox close-outs,
>   running listed commands.
> 
> **Blanket rules (override any step tag):**
> 
> 1. Accepting any golden under `conformance/golden/` — and any `cargo insta
>    review` acceptance of a NEW snapshot — is a **T1 act**: a golden is spec.
> 2. The escalation triggers are tier-independent: an ambiguity (§3), a red
>    `crash_*` test, any assertion edit, any new Amendment, or any Discovered gap
>    promotes the moment to **T1** no matter what the surrounding step is tagged.
> 3. A lower-tier executor who cannot complete a step WITHOUT exceeding its tier
>    (i.e. a "T4" step turns out to require a decision) has, by definition, found
>    a Discovered gap — stop and record it (§3).
> 
> Delegation guidance: T4 and T3 are safely delegable to cheaper/faster agents
> prompted with this protocol (§3 verbatim). T2 is delegable to a strong mid-tier
> executor with a T1-level review of the diff. T1 is never delegated below the
> project's most capable executor, and its artifacts get human sign-off.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-49371b0fe52b13f3da5a -->

<a id="source-ad34c4de980c163ce0a8"></a>

Classification: `mixed-clause`. Original lines 167–189; text SHA-256: `2511fd39d024f9cd9bbf0e245390cd717a6323447ca4e457fe244de511c1ecef`.

<!-- source-block:source-ad34c4de980c163ce0a8 -->
> ## 8. Shared conventions all orders rely on
> 
> - **Aux namespaces:** every aux-namespace constant lives in
>   `liminal_graph::store::ns` (`ILRP_INTENT`, `JUR_ALIAS`, `JUR_PLAN`,
>   `JUR_DECISION`, `JUR_REPAIR`, `JUR_OVERLAY`, `JUR_OVERLAY_LOG`, `JUR_RECONCILE`,
>   `SYS_BLOB`, `SYS_UNAVAILABLE`, `SYS_CLOCK`, `SYS_EPOCH`). Introduced at M02/M03;
>   no namespace string literal appears at a call site.
> - **Milestone tests:** Phase -1 milestone tests live in
>   `conformance/tests/milestones/m<nn>.rs` under a `milestones/main.rs` that
>   declares the modules. Phase 0+ gates shared across a phase sequence live in
>   `conformance/tests/phase<n>.rs`, are authored ignored at the preceding gate,
>   and are assigned to exact work orders there. Crash tests are named `crash_*`
>   anywhere (routed into the serialized nextest crash group).
> - **Name aliases:** where `docs/implementation-plan.md` uses a shorthand test name,
>   the work order states the alias once (e.g. `capture_never_rejected` ≡ the gate
>   test `no_edit_is_rejected`); tests are never duplicated to satisfy both names.

> ## Pre-made decisions
> 
> - **D01.1 — firing mechanism = hidden `liminald __fire <point> [count]` subcommand**
>   (AM-1.1). `liminald exec` does not exist at M1 and Cargo cannot build a
>   `#[cfg(test)]` binary. A separate helper bin would construct the injector through
>   a second code path, weakening the proof; `__fire` exercises the exact production
>   `EnvCrashInjector::from_env()` path.
> - **D01.2 — test location = `crates/liminal-daemon/tests/crash.rs`** because
>   `CARGO_BIN_EXE_liminald` is only injected for the crate that owns the `[[bin]]`.
> - **D01.3 — test names carry the `crash_` prefix** (AM-1.2) so the nextest
>   serialized crash group matches; the implementation-plan shorthand
>   `fault_abort_exits_with_sigabrt` ≡ `crash_fault_abort_exits_with_sigabrt`.
> - **D01.4 — `const SIGABRT: i32 = 6`** in the test file with a comment: Phase -1
>   targets Unix dev machines (Linux/macOS); Windows crash semantics are a Phase 2
>   concern with the real-daemon SIGKILL handshake.
>

> ## Algorithms
> 
> `__fire` handler: resolve `point` via
> `CrashPoint::all().into_iter().find(|p| p.name() == point)` (else
> `anyhow::bail!("unknown crash point: {point}")`); build
> `EnvCrashInjector::from_env()`; loop `count` times (default 1) calling
> `crash_if_armed(p)` (import `liminal_jurisdiction::CrashInjector as _`); exit 0,
> no output on success.

<!-- source-block:source-ecf9474dbb34c1d1f668 -->
> ## Pre-made decisions
> 
> - **D02.1 — every durable state change is its own aux-commit, and `run` is
>   resumable via ONE internal `advance` fn shared verbatim with `recover_all`.**
>   Run and resume become a single audited code path; there is no separate "resume
>   interpreter" to drift.
> - **D02.2 — the intent record is KEPT at `state = committed`** — it is the durable
>   history behind `lim repairs`. Deletion is forbidden.
> - **D02.3 — `FsExecutor` lives in `crates/liminal-daemon/src/executor.rs`**:
>   `liminal-jurisdiction` stays Holder-agnostic interpretive semantics; the file
>   executor is a Holder adapter and the daemon is the assembly crate.
> - **D02.4 — staged-file sweep lives in `ToyWorkspace::open`, policy = delete all**
>   (`StagedWrite::abandon()` on every `scan_staged` hit). Safe: staged bytes are
>   never the sole copy of anything — `WriteFile.contents` lives durably in the
>   intent record; third-party bytes only ever live in the target, which the sweep
>   never touches. Trivially idempotent.
> - **D02.5 — `Graph` steps short-circuit in the step loop**: verify is treated as
>   `Prestate` and "apply" is a synthesized no-op ack
>   (`observed_poststate = expected_poststate`) because graph ops land atomically at
>   Finalize. No Graph steps exist in the M2 scenario; the branch exists for M4.
> - **D02.6 — binary location: conformance gains `[[bin]] lim-toy`** (AM-2.4), a
>   ~20-line argv shim (`lim-toy exec <root> <scenario>` / `lim-toy recover <root>`,
>   no clap) delegating to `liminal_daemon::runner::{exec, recover}`.
>   `CARGO_BIN_EXE_*` is only injected for targets owned by the compiling crate;
>   path-guessing `target/debug/liminald` breaks under `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`; per-case
>   `cargo run` is slow and non-hermetic. Consequence: ALL exec/recover semantics
>   live in the daemon library — `liminald`'s `main.rs` and `lim_toy.rs` are both
>   transport shims and cannot drift.
> - **D02.7 — one injector per concern**: `runner::exec` builds one
>   `EnvCrashInjector::from_env()` and moves it into the scenario driver;
>   `ToyWorkspace::open` builds its own for the recovery driver. Safety invariant
>   (documented at both construction sites): `exec` requires a fresh root, so
>   open-time recovery finds zero nonterminal intents and fires zero boundaries —
>   occurrence counting never spans the two instances.
> - **D02.8 — aux key/value asymmetry is deliberate**: the aux key uses the prefixed
>   Display form (`repair:<uuid>`, self-describing in NDJSON) while ids INSIDE the
>   JSON are bare UUIDs (`#[serde(transparent)]`). Do not "fix" this.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-ecf9474dbb34c1d1f668 -->

> ## Data schemas
> 
> Namespace constant: `liminal_graph::store::ns::ILRP_INTENT = "ilrp.intent"`
> (AM-2.3 creates the `ns` module; `liminal_jurisdiction::ilrp` re-exports it as
> `AUX_NS_INTENT` for local readability). Key = `RepairId` Display
> (`repair:<uuid>`), produced by `plan.id.to_string()`, parsed by
> `key.parse::<RepairId>()`. Value = `serde_json::to_value(&RepairIntent)` — the
> derived serde shapes ARE the schema; no hand-rolled DTO. Every aux update rewrites
> the whole value.
> 
> Field-for-field example (enum variants kebab-case where declared; struct fields
> snake_case; `state` ∈ `"prepared" | "applying" | "external-applied" | "finalizing"
> | "committed" | "needs-review" | "aborted"`; `contents` is a JSON byte array —
> frozen `Vec<u8>`, accepted as less grep-able):
> 
> ```json
> {
>   "plan": {
>     "id": "01890a5d-ac96-774b-bcce-b302099a8057",

>       "components": {
>         "path:notes.md": {
>           "file-content": { "path": "notes.md", "hash": "6a4f…(64 hex)" }
>         }
>       }
>     },
>     "steps": {
>       "01890a5d-…-8059": {
>         "id": "01890a5d-…-8059",
>         "subject": { "node": "01890a5d-…-8061" },
>         "operation": { "write-file": { "path": "notes.md", "contents": [84, 104] } },
>         "expected_prestate":  { "file-content": { "path": "notes.md", "hash": "6a4f…" } },
>         "expected_poststate": { "file-content": { "path": "notes.md", "hash": "9b1e…" } },
>         "idempotency_key": "01890a5d-…-8062"
>       }
>     },
>     "dependencies": [],
>     "inverse": null
>   },
>   "state": "prepared",
>   "evidence": { "structurally-disjoint": { "description": "single-step file promotion; durable file unchanged since buffer base" } },
>   "acks": {}
> }
> ```

<a id="source-c25ab9169ceea66fcee1"></a>

Classification: `mixed-clause`. Original lines 118–131; text SHA-256: `d105a74151ec1b37a7c0f44ed109bfd565c033438e8a28edc4b33a7e9d64c3bb`.

<!-- source-block:source-c25ab9169ceea66fcee1 -->
> ### A. `IlrpDriver::prepare`
> 
> 1. `topo_order(&plan)?` — validates DAG/unknown-step up front; discard the order.
> 2. `key = plan.id.to_string()`; if `store.get_aux(ILRP_INTENT, &key)?` is `Some`,
>    return `Err(IlrpError::Store(StoreError::Conflict(format!("intent exists: {key}"))))`.
> 3. `intent = RepairIntent { plan, state: Prepared, evidence, acks: BTreeMap::new() }`.
> 4. One transaction: `put_aux(ILRP_INTENT, &key, to_value(&intent))`; commit with
>    `meta("ilrp:prepare", Origin::Human)` where
>    `meta(p, o) = TxnMeta { actor: None, origin: o, at: Timestamp::now(), provenance: Some(p.into()), inverse: None }`.
> 5. `self.crash.crash_if_armed(CrashPoint::BeforeIntentCommit);`
> 6. Commit.
> 7. `self.crash.crash_if_armed(CrashPoint::AfterIntentCommit);`
> 8. Return `Ok(repair_id)` (captured before the move).
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-c25ab9169ceea66fcee1 -->

<!-- source-block:source-8ef38d9f96d94126957f -->
> ### B. `IlrpDriver::run` + internal `advance` (D02.1)
> 
> `run(repair)`: load intent (`None` → `NotFound`; malformed → `Corrupt` — never
> guess); terminal → `Ok(state)` (idempotent re-run); else
> `advance(repair, intent, Origin::Human)`.
> 
> `advance(id, mut intent, origin)` — `commit_intent(note)` = assert
> `may_transition_to` where state changes (violation → `IllegalTransition`), then one
> txn putting the whole intent with provenance `"ilrp:<note>"`:
> 
> 1. `order = topo_order(&intent.plan)?`.
> 2. **Prepared:** `state = Applying`; `commit_intent("state:applying")`. *(No fault
>    point — the R4 §10 transition boundary is separately covered by
>    `state=applying` record is separately reachable by recovery.)*
> 3. **Applying:** for each `step_id` in `order`:
>    a. Acked already → skip. *(Completed durable evidence is never re-audited by the
>    in-flight saga; a post-ack foreign edit is a NEW foreign-edit event for the
>    M3+/M5 checker/overlay machinery, not a rewind of this step — v4 §7.8 step 3.)*
>    b. If `operation` is `Graph(_)` → D02.5 short-circuit.
>    c. Else `match self.executor.verify(m)?`:
>       - **Prestate** → `ack = self.executor.apply(m)`: `Err(Contested{..})` → go
>         to 6; other `Err` propagates. Surround the effect with
>         `crash_if_armed(BeforeExternalApply)` and
>         `crash_if_armed(AfterExternalApply)`. Then insert ack; surround
>         `commit_intent("ack:<step-uuid>")` with `crash_if_armed(BeforeAcknowledge)`
>         and `crash_if_armed(AfterAcknowledge)`.
>       - **Poststate** → synthesize
>         `ack = StepAck { step, observed_poststate: m.expected_poststate.clone(), at: now }`;
>         insert; surround `commit_intent("ack:<step-uuid>")` with
>         `crash_if_armed(BeforeAcknowledge)` and
>         `crash_if_armed(AfterAcknowledge)`. *(No external-apply boundary — nothing
>         external happened in this process.)*
>       - **Neither** → go to 6.
>    After the loop: `state = ExternalApplied`;
>    `commit_intent("state:external-applied")`.
> 4. **ExternalApplied:** `state = Finalizing`; `commit_intent("state:finalizing")`.
> 5. **Finalizing:** `crash_if_armed(BeforeFinalize)` *(top of this branch, so both
>    fresh runs and recovery re-entries cross the boundary "immediately before the
>    Finalize transaction")*. Build ONE txn: for each step in `order` whose operation
>    is `Graph(op)` → `txn.apply(op.clone())`; set `state = Committed`
>    (legality-checked); put the whole intent (D02.2: kept, never deleted); commit
>    `meta("ilrp:finalize", origin)`. On `Err(Conflict | NotFound)` (graph ops
>    invalid against current state) → go to 6 (`Finalizing → NeedsReview` is legal);
>    other store errors propagate. Then
>    `crash_if_armed(AfterFinalizeBeforeNotify)`; return `Ok(Committed)`.
> 6. **needs_review:** `state = NeedsReview`; `commit_intent("state:needs-review")`;
>    return `Ok(NeedsReview)`. Target files are never touched on this path —
>    preservation IS the action. (Contested-overlay reification is M5.)
> 
> Happy-path enumeration for a k-step plan (C = commit, F = fault point fired after):
> 
> | # | Event | F |
> |---|---|---|
> | C1 | prepare: intent `prepared` | `ilrp/before_intent_commit:1`, `ilrp/after_intent_commit:1` |
> | C2 | intent `applying` | — |
> | — | external apply, step i (stage → rename) | `ilrp/before_external_apply:i`, `ilrp/after_external_apply:i` |
> | C2+i | ack for step i persisted | `ilrp/before_ack:i`, `ilrp/after_ack:i` |
> | C3+k | intent `external-applied` | — |
> | C4+k | intent `finalizing` | — (then `ilrp/before_finalize:1` immediately before C5+k) |
> | C5+k | FINALIZE: all Graph ops + intent `committed`, ONE record | `ilrp/after_finalize_before_notify:1` |
> 
> Baseline trace for `promote_single_step` (k=1) is therefore exactly:
> `before_intent_commit:1, after_intent_commit:1, before_external_apply:1,
> after_external_apply:1, before_ack:1, after_ack:1, before_finalize:1,
> after_finalize_before_notify:1` — all eight registered points, so this one scenario
> already satisfies the meta-test.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-8ef38d9f96d94126957f -->

> ### C. `FsExecutor` (crates/liminal-daemon/src/executor.rs)
> 
> `pub struct FsExecutor { root: Utf8PathBuf }`; `abs(path) = root.join(&path.0)`;
> predicates/acks carry the workspace-relative `PathId` exactly as written in the
> plan.
> 
> `verify(m)`: extract the file path from the operation (`WriteFile{path,..}` at M2;
> `InsertSourceId`/`External` → `Err(Executor("deferred to M4: <variant>"))`).
> `obs = observe(&abs)?`, classify with `matches(pred, obs)`:
> 
> | `StatePredicate` | `obs = Some(o)` | `obs = None` |
> |---|---|---|
> | `FileContent { hash, .. }` | `o.hash == hash` | false |
> | `FileAbsent { .. }` | false | true |
> | `Any` | true | true |
> | `NodeAt` / `RelationAt` / `ExternalRevision` | `Err(Executor("non-file predicate in file step"))` | same |
> 
> Return: prestate match → `Prestate` (**checked FIRST** — if pre and post both
> match, e.g. identical contents, re-apply wins and is idempotent); else poststate
> match → `Poststate`; else `Neither`.
> 
> `apply(m)` for `WriteFile { path, contents }`:
> 
> 1. `staged = stage(&abs, contents)?`.
> 2. `expected_pre` = `FileContent{hash,..}` → `Some(hash)`; `FileAbsent` → `None`;
>    `Any` → `observe(&abs)?.map(|o| o.hash)` (TOCTOU window accepted in the toy;
>    documented); others → `Err(Executor(..))`.
> 3. `staged.commit_if(expected_pre)`:
>    - `Ok(obs)` → `Ok(StepAck { step: m.id, observed_poststate: FileContent { path: path.clone(), hash: obs.hash }, at: now })`.
>    - `Err(PrestateMismatch{..})` → best-effort remove the staged sibling, then
>      `Err(IlrpError::Contested { step: m.id })`.
>    - `Err(Io(e))` → `Err(Executor(e.to_string()))`.
>

<!-- source-block:source-6b5961a6b74105c060e1 -->
> ### D. `recover_all` (v4 §7.8 step 5) — with per-branch idempotence argument
> 
> 1. `all = store.scan_aux(ILRP_INTENT)?` (key-ordered — deterministic).
> 2. Deserialize each; malformed → `Err(Corrupt)`.
> 3. Filter `!state.is_terminal()`.
> 4. For each, in key order: `outcome = advance(id, intent, Origin::Recovery)?`.
> 5. Return `Vec<(RepairId, IntentState)>` (empty when nothing was nonterminal).
> 
> Resume semantics per observed state:
> 
> - **Prepared** — no external effect exists; run the full pipeline. Idempotent:
>   crashing again reproduces a state this table covers.
> - **Applying** — per-step verify walk. Acked steps skip. Un-acked: `Prestate` →
>   re-apply (same staged bytes, same `expected_pre`; `rename(2)` atomicity means
>   the target is entirely-old or entirely-new, never torn); `Poststate` → the apply
>   landed but the ack-commit was lost — synthesize the ack, exactly the missing
>   durable record; `Neither` → `NeedsReview`, target untouched. Never guess.
> - **ExternalApplied** — all effects landed and acked; proceed to Finalizing, then
>   finalize.
> - **Finalizing** — the finalize txn writes `state=committed` **atomically with the
>   graph ops in one log record**; observing `Finalizing` at recovery PROVES that
>   record never committed → redo finalize. Exactly-once graph acceptance holds by
>   record atomicity.
> - **Terminal** — filtered; recovery performs zero commits. Hence a second
>   `recover_all` finds nothing nonterminal and the world digest is unchanged — the
>   idempotence assertion.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-6b5961a6b74105c060e1 -->

> ### E. World digest (crates/liminal-daemon/src/digest.rs)
> 
> ```rust
> pub fn workspace_file_hashes(root: &Utf8Path) -> io::Result<BTreeMap<String, String>>;
> pub fn world_digest(root: &Utf8Path, store: &GraphStore) -> Result<String, WorkspaceError>;
> ```
> 
> Exclusions (forced by `ToyRun::trace_path()` living inside the root): the
> `root/state` subtree and the exact root-level names `crash-trace.log`,
> `recover-trace.log`, `scenario.toml`. **Nothing else** — `.lim-staged` files are
> deliberately INCLUDED so a leftover staged file breaks digest idempotence loudly.
> 
> Byte-exact algorithm:
> 
> 1. `h = blake3::Hasher::new(); h.update(b"liminal-world-digest/v1\n")`.
> 2. `h.update(format!("head:{}\n", store.head()?.0))`.
> 3. Every regular non-excluded file under root, sorted by workspace-relative UTF-8
>    path (byte order): `h.update(format!("file:{rel}:{hex}\n"))`,
>    `hex = ContentHash::of(&bytes).to_hex()`.
> 4. `(key, value)` in `store.scan_aux(ns::ILRP_INTENT)?` (key-ordered):
>    `h.update(format!("intent:{key}:{json}\n"))`, `json = serde_json::to_string`
>    (canonical: workspace serde_json has no `preserve_order`, so maps are
>    key-sorted). Hashing full JSONs of ALL intents — including terminal — catches
>    recovery mutating acks.
> 5. `(key, _)` in `store.scan_aux(ns::JUR_OVERLAY)?`:
>    `h.update(format!("overlay:{key}\n"))` (empty until M5; future-proofs the digest).
> 6. Output: 64 lowercase hex chars of `h.finalize()`.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-affc99e04b7b9a932cab -->

> ### F. `liminald exec` / `recover` (crates/liminal-daemon/src/runner.rs)
> 
> ```rust
> pub fn exec(root: &Utf8Path, scenario_path: &Utf8Path) -> anyhow::Result<()>;
> #[derive(Serialize)]
> pub struct RecoverOutcome { pub terminals: Vec<IntentState>, pub world_digest: String }
> pub fn recover(root: &Utf8Path) -> anyhow::Result<RecoverOutcome>;
> ```
> 
> `main.rs` delegates; `Exec` prints NOTHING on success (silence culture; failures
> via anyhow to stderr, exit 1); `Recover` prints one JSON line of `RecoverOutcome`.
> 
> `exec` algorithm: (1) `ScenarioScript::load` (model relocated per AM-2.1);
> (2) setup files: `create_dir_all` + `fs::write` — pre-existing world state, written
> directly, not system-mediated; (3) `ToyWorkspace::open(root)?` (sweep + recovery;
> no-op on fresh root, D02.7); (4) setup buffers (AM-2.2): contents = file bytes;
> one minted `ClientId` per distinct client name; any `setup.graph` entry →
> `bail!("setup.graph is M4")` *(M3 order supersedes this with real ingestion)*;
> (5) steps in order — `buffer_edit { client, path, find, replace }`: replace FIRST
> occurrence in the buffer, absent `find` → bail (scenario bug, loud);
> `save { client, path }`: build the plan below, `driver.prepare` + `driver.run`;
> any other kind → `bail!("step kind {kind:?} not implemented until M3/M4")`;
> (6) if `expect.terminal` is `Some(t)`: compare
> `normalize(t) == normalize(<kebab name of terminal>)` where
> `normalize = lowercase + strip '-'` (fixtures write `"Committed"`, serde writes
> `"committed"`); (7) exit silently.
> 
> `save` → plan construction, exact:
> 
> 1. `rel = PathId(path)`; `base = observe(&abs)?`.
> 2. `expected_prestate` = base present → `FileContent{path: rel, hash: base.hash}`,
>    else `FileAbsent{path: rel}`.
> 3. `expected_poststate = FileContent{path: rel, hash: ContentHash::of(&new_bytes)}`.
> 4. One `ProposedMutation` — `subject: Node(NodeId::new())` *(M2 placeholder; M3
>    replaces with the parsed block Node)*, `operation: WriteFile{path, contents}`,
>    fresh `RepairStepId`/`IdempotencyKey`.
> 5. `RepairPlan` — fresh `RepairId`; basis:
>    `WorkspaceBasis { transaction: TransactionId::new() /* M6 makes capture real */,
>    perspective: ClientScoped{client}, components: [(JurisdictionKey::Path(rel),
>    FileContent{path, hash: base.hash})] when base exists else empty }`;
>    `dependencies: []`; `inverse: None`.
> 6. `evidence = StructurallyDisjoint { description: "single-step file promotion;
>    durable file unchanged since buffer base (verified as ILRP prestate)" }` — the
>    M4 safety machinery does not exist yet; this hardcoding is the M2 scope
>    boundary, commented with R4 §6.
> 7. `driver = IlrpDriver { store: ws.store(), executor: FsExecutor::new(root),
>    crash: <exec-scoped injector> }` — one driver reused for prepare and run.
> 
> `recover` algorithm: `ToyWorkspace::open` (sweep + `recover_all` inside, outcomes
> stashed behind the additive `recovery_outcomes()` accessor); then rescan ALL
> intents in key order and collect every state (so a crash after finalize still
> reports `["committed"]` and a second recovery reports identical terminals); any
> nonterminal after recovery → bail (recovery bug, loud); compute `world_digest`.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-e2b365d83a08fe9d5b12 -->

> ### G. `ToyRun` bodies (conformance/src/harness.rs) + `lim-toy`
> 
> - `baseline(scenario)`: `toml::to_string(scenario)` → `root/scenario.toml` (the
>   frozen signature passes the parsed model; `ScenarioScript` derives Serialize —
>   if toml serialization ordering errors surface, that is a Discovered gap, not a
>   workaround site); spawn `env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_lim-toy")` with
>   `["exec", root, root/scenario.toml]`, `env_remove(LIMINAL_CRASHPOINT)`,
>   `LIMINAL_CRASH_TRACE = trace_path()`; ensure success else bail with stderr;
>   `HitTrace::parse`; ensure hits non-empty.
> - `run_to_crash(scenario, point, occurrence)`: same spawn +
>   `LIMINAL_CRASHPOINT=<point>:<occurrence>`; ensure `!success`,
>   `code().is_none()`, `signal() == Some(6)`; parse trace; **ensure
>   `trace.fired(point, occurrence)`** — a crash test whose point never fired is a
>   false pass and must fail here; return `CrashState`.
> - `recover()`: spawn `["recover", root]` with crash arming removed and
>   `LIMINAL_CRASH_TRACE = root/recover-trace.log` (separate file keeps the crash
>   trace pristine and out of the digest); parse the JSON line; **assert every
>   terminal `is_terminal()`**; return `RecoveryReport`.
> - `crash_matrix(scenario)`:
>   1. Baseline in its own root; capture trace + `workspace_file_hashes` (minus the
>      E-exclusions).
>   2. `expected = normalize(scenario.expect.terminal.unwrap_or("committed"))`.
>   3. For every `(point, occ)` in `trace.enumerate_faults()` (ensure non-empty):
>      fresh `ToyRun` (label `<id>-<point '/'→'-'>-<occ>`); `run_to_crash`;
>      `r1 = recover()` — terminals non-empty, every normalized state == expected;
>      `r2 = recover()` — `r2.world_digest == r1.world_digest` AND
>      `r2.terminals == r1.terminals` (recovery that only works once is not
>      recovery); if expected == committed: file hashes == baseline's (crash+recover
>      converges to the no-crash file world); no `.lim-staged` files remain.
> - Additive `pub fn runnable_crash_scenarios() -> anyhow::Result<Vec<ScenarioScript>>`:
>   loads from `fixtures/scenarios/` exactly the ids in
>   `const RUNNABLE: &[&str] = &["promote_single_step"]; // M4 appends "dag_id_then_reattach"`
>   — the single source of truth for matrix scope.
>

> ## Pre-made decisions
> 
> - **D03.1 — grammar module = `crates/liminal-source/src/paragraph.rs`** (the
>   grammar is a property of source bytes, not of the daemon).
> - **D03.2 — kind constants** = new `crates/liminal-graph/src/kind.rs`, re-exported
>   as `liminal_graph::kind`: `FILE = KindId(1)`, `PARAGRAPH = KindId(2)`,
>   `COMMENT = KindId(3)` (0 reserved = unset).
> - **D03.3 — alias mapping** lives in aux ns `jur.alias`
>   (`ns::JUR_ALIAS`): key = the id string, value =
>   `{"node":"<uuid>","entity":"<uuid>"}`. Fresh `EntityId` at first ingestion;
>   re-ingestion reuses the entity when identity is preserved. First occurrence wins
>   within one commit; later duplicates get no alias and the checker reports JUR042.
> - **D03.4 — profile dispatch by kind**: Node kind FILE|PARAGRAPH → external-file;
>   COMMENT|EXTERNAL_VALUE → graph-native; any other kind →
>   `CheckerError::Ungoverned`. All Relations → graph-native (all Phase -1
>   Relations are graph-held). EXTERNAL_VALUE was added at M08.6 and routed here
>   by AM-12.3.
> - **D03.5 — the Contract declares the FLOOR; the node's grade is COMPUTED**
>   (`grade_of`): external-file `required_identity = Anchored` (v4 §7.11 "otherwise
>   anchored or heuristic continuity"); a `{#id}` paragraph computes `Explicit`.
> - **D03.6 — `surface_after = 0`** in both lifecycle policies: everything surfaces
>   immediately in Phase -1 → deterministic tests; `escalate_after = 3600s`.
> - **D03.7 — name alias:** the plan's `capture_never_rejected` ≡ the gate test
>   `no_edit_is_rejected`; the plan's `sound_workspace_is_silent` ≡
>   `sound_states_are_silent`. No duplicate tests.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-2aea883c8462b8942c58 -->

<!-- source-block:source-239aa962f6c2dc44bc24 -->
> ## Data schemas
> 
> `paragraph.rs`:
> 
> ```rust
> pub struct Block { pub text: String, pub id: Option<String>, pub range: SourceRange }
> pub fn parse(input: &str) -> Vec<Block>   // TOTAL — never errors (Law 3B)
> ```
> 
> Grammar rules (exhaustive):
> - A **block** is a maximal run of non-blank lines; a blank line is empty or
>   whitespace-only; blocks are separated by ≥1 blank lines; leading/trailing blank
>   lines produce no blocks.
> - **ID marker:** if the block's final line ends with `{#` + id + `}` where id
>   matches `[A-Za-z0-9_-]+` (nonempty), optionally preceded by spaces/tabs:
>   `id = Some(id)`; `text` = lines joined `\n` with the marker (and preceding
>   spaces/tabs) stripped from the last line, then that line's trailing whitespace
>   stripped.
> - **Malformed stays literal:** unclosed `{#`, empty id, invalid chars, or marker
>   not at end-of-block → `id = None`, text unchanged. Only the LAST suffix is a
>   marker: `foo {#a} {#b}` → id `b`, text `foo {#a}`.
> - `range` = byte span of the block in the input (inclusive/exclusive), including
>   marker bytes, excluding surrounding blank lines.
> 
> Ingestion per `[[setup.file]]` (one commit each, in the daemon runner; replaces
> M02's `setup.graph` bail):
> 1. `CreateNode` FILE node (payload `None`); raw bytes →
>    `put_aux(SYS_BLOB, "file/<path>", <json string of bytes>)`.
> 2. Per parsed block i: `CreateNode` PARAGRAPH node — payload `Text(block.text)`,
>    flags `HAS_DURABLE_ID` iff id present.
> 3. `InsertChild { parent: file, child: para, index: i }` in parse order.
> 4. Per id: `put_aux(JUR_ALIAS, id, {"node","entity"})` (D03.3).
> 
> Per `[[setup.graph]]` `kind = "comment-relation"`: `CreateNode` COMMENT node
> (payload `Text(body)`) + `AddRelation { source: comment, target:
> Node(alias→node), kind: COMMENT, requires: Some(IdentityRequirement { minimum:
> <requires_grade> }) }` (AM-3.1).
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-239aa962f6c2dc44bc24 -->

> ### A. Contract literals (returned verbatim by `contract_for`)
> 
> `ExternalFileProfile` — FILE/PARAGRAPH nodes (path from the owning file's blob
> key):
> 
> ```rust
> JurisdictionContract {
>     scope: SubjectSelector::Exact(subject),
>     resolution: HolderResolution {
>         candidates:      vec![Holder::File { path }],
>         read_precedence: vec![Holder::File { path }],
>         fallback:        None,                    // unavailable → Overlay, never a block (Law 3B)
>         merge_runtime:   None,                    // §7.11's "Text/Git" is external, not a Federated runtime
>     },
>     mutation: MutationPolicy {
>         write_route: Holder::File { path },
>         foreign_edits: ForeignEditPolicy::Accept, // v4 §8.5 step 4
>         repair_authorization: RepairAuthorization::Automatic,
>         safety: SafetyRequirement::StructuralDisjointness, // v4 §7.7
>     },
>     continuity: ContinuityPolicy {
>         required_identity: IdentityGrade::Anchored,        // FLOOR (D03.5)
>         on_dangling: DanglingPolicy::PreserveAndSurface,   // v4 §7.7 final bullet
>     },
>     lifecycle: LifecyclePolicy {
>         surface_after: Duration::from_secs(0),             // D03.6
>         escalate_after: Duration::from_secs(3600),
>         declared_transient: true,                          // offline drafts awaiting sync (R4 §2.3)
>     },
> }
> ```
> 
> `GraphNativeProfile` — COMMENT nodes and ALL Relations: same shape with
> `candidates/read_precedence = vec![Holder::Graph]`, `write_route: Holder::Graph`,
> `foreign_edits: Review` (v4 §8.2: byte equality is not the merge protocol),
> `required_identity: Managed` (v4 §7.6/§7.11), `declared_transient: false`.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-b0ce30cb549897c63ccb -->

> ### B. `grade_of(subject)` (new fn in checker.rs, used by Q4)
> 
> | Subject | Grade |
> |---|---|
> | PARAGRAPH node with `HAS_DURABLE_ID` | Explicit |
> | PARAGRAPH node without | Anchored |
> | FILE node | Anchored |
> | COMMENT node | Managed |
> | EXTERNAL_VALUE node | Managed (AM-12.3) |
> | any node with `Object(_)` payload | ContentAddressed (overrides; unused at M3) |
> | any Relation | Managed |
> 
> `Inferred` first appears with M4/M7 heuristic re-ingestion; not producible at M3.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-1734d978418bbf9b0a84 -->

<!-- source-block:source-71877dc8b00463f3d6e8 -->
> ### C. Checker Q1–Q8
> 
> - **Q1 `resolve_holder`:** contract = dispatch + `contract_for`; if
>   `basis.perspective` is `ClientScoped{client}` AND the owning file's
>   `basis.components[Path(p)]` is `BufferGeneration{client: c == client, buffer, ..}`
>   → `Holder::Buffer{client, buffer}`; else `read_precedence[0]`.
> - **Q2 `write_route`:** `contract.mutation.write_route` verbatim (buffer capture
>   is not routing).
> - **Q3:** `contract.resolution.merge_runtime.clone()` (always None in Phase -1).
> - **Q4 `identity_satisfies_relations`:** for each Relation targeting the node with
>   `requires = Some(req)`: `!grade_of(node).satisfies(req.minimum)` → JUR041.
>   Alias claimed by ≥2 live blocks → JUR042.
> - **Q5 `unresolved_overlays`:** scan `JUR_OVERLAY`, keep
>   `Active|RepairProposed|Contested`, filter by subject, sorted. (Empty before M5 —
>   which is what soundness needs.)
> - **Q6:** already implemented.
> - **Q7 `authorize`:** per step, consult ONLY `step.subject`'s own contract (that
>   IS Law 3F); `ReviewRequired` → refusal JUR051.
> - **Q8 `evaluate_repair`:** conjunction collecting reasons: (a) basis current
>   (plan.basis.transaction vs head) else JUR053; (b) every prestate matches now
>   else JUR053; (c) Q7 refusals empty else JUR051; (d) retargeting steps pass Q4 at
>   the new target else JUR041; (e) `profile.safety_check` errors map to JUR052;
>   (f) `inverse.is_some()` else JUR052. All hold → AutoApply, else
>   NeedsReview(reasons). **No Reject exists.** M3 ships a trivial safety_check
>   (steps touch pairwise-distinct subjects → Ok); M4 replaces it.
> - **`check_workspace`:** Q4 over every node with incoming required Relations +
>   JUR050 per unresolved overlay + JUR042 for ambiguous aliases; findings sorted by
>   `(code, subject)`.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-71877dc8b00463f3d6e8 -->

> ### D. Finding-code table (codes internal; UI renders everyday language, R4 §3)
> 
> | Code | Meaning | Everyday rendering |
> |---|---|---|
> | JUR010 | holder-unavailable | source unavailable or stale |
> | JUR020 | write-route-unavailable | draft not yet saved or synced |
> | JUR030 | merge-runtime-missing | conflicting changes need review |
> | JUR041 | identity-grade-unsatisfied | conflicting changes need review |
> | JUR042 | identity-ambiguous (duplicate id/alias) | conflicting changes need review |
> | JUR050 | unresolved-overlay | draft not yet saved or synced |
> | JUR051 | repair-not-authorized | repair could not be applied safely |
> | JUR052 | repair-unsafe (deterministic ≠ safe) | repair could not be applied safely |
> | JUR053 | repair-stale-basis | conflicting changes need review |
> | JUR060 | dangling-relation | conflicting changes need review |
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-89e8d7d15e08207b4758 -->

> ### E. CLI
> 
> `lim check`: sound → exit **0**, byte-empty stdout AND stderr. Unsound → exit
> **1**; one line per finding sorted by `(code, subject)`:
> `"{everyday}: {subject-alias-or-id} [{code}]\n"` (subject rendered as alias when
> one exists, else `node:<uuid>`); stderr empty. Checker error → exit **2**, message
> on stderr.
> 
> `lim jurisdiction explain <subject>` (exit 0 / 2; the ONLY surface using internal
> vocabulary):
> 
> ```
> subject: node:<uuid> (alias: p-fourier)
> profile: external-file
> holder: file:notes.md
> write route: file:notes.md
> perspective: durable-only
> identity: explicit (required floor: anchored)
> merge runtime: none
> overlays: none
> contract:
>   <toml::to_string_pretty(JurisdictionContract), indented 2 spaces>
> narrative:
>   <one paragraph assembled from the fields; may say Jurisdiction/Holder/Overlay/Promotion>
> ```
> 
> Holder rendering: `file:<path>` | `buffer:<client>/<buffer>` | `graph` |
> `object:<hash>` | `git:<oid>` | `service:<source>`.
>

> ## Discovered gaps
> 
> - **DG-3.1 — RESOLVED (found by post-completion review, 2026-07-18).** D03.3
>   ("first occurrence wins within one commit; later duplicates get no alias and
>   the checker reports JUR042") was not implemented: ingestion wrote the alias
>   unconditionally (last-wins) and nothing surfaced the duplicate — a file with
>   two `{#dup}` blocks produced ZERO findings (silent identity ambiguity). No
>   test covered the path, so the gap survived the exit gate. Resolution:
>   ingestion now skips the alias when one already exists (first-wins);
>   `Checker::ambiguous_aliases` additionally reports JUR042 for any live

> ## Pre-made decisions
> 
> - **D04.1 — merge module = `crates/liminal-source/src/merge.rs`** (AM-4.3),
>   sibling of `paragraph.rs`: merging is a property of source blocks, not policy.
> - **D04.2 — block alignment is identity-stable:** blocks pair across versions by
>   `{#id}` when present on both sides; anonymous blocks pair by index among the
>   anonymous blocks in order; base blocks absent on one side are deletions; new
>   blocks are insertions at their position.
> - **D04.3 — same-block dual edits are never auto-safe:** a deterministic
>   line-level merge inside one block yields `UniqueOverlap` — a unique candidate
>   that the safety predicate REFUSES (R4 §6: determinism is not safety). This is
>   the `unsafe_unique_merge` scenario by construction.
> - **D04.4 — graph-before-file ordering is unexecutable under ILRP:** `Graph(_)`
>   steps execute inside the Finalize transaction in topo order; a plan where any
>   file/external step depends on a graph step is refused by `IlrpDriver::run` with
>   `IlrpError::Executor("graph-before-file ordering cannot be executed under ILRP")`.
> - **D04.5 — heuristic-founded DAG plans carry `inverse: None`:** R4 §6 requires an
>   inverse only for AUTOMATICALLY accepted repairs; the DAG plan auto-refuses on
>   identity grounds, and human acceptance records `HumanApproval` evidence without
>   a revert promise.
> - **D04.6 — new aux namespaces** (`store::ns`): `JUR_PLAN = "jur.plan"` (persisted
>   proposals, key `repair:<uuid>`), `JUR_DECISION = "jur.decision"` (the
>   `RepairDecision` for each plan), `JUR_REPAIR = "jur.repair"` (accepted
>   `RepairRecord`s, written in the Finalize txn).
> - **D04.7 — `selected_rule` strings (exact):** `"save-promotion"`,
>   `"disjoint-merge"`, `"id-insert-then-reattach"`, `"undo:<original repair id>"`.
> - **D04.8 — `lim repairs` prints no timestamps** — UUIDv7 already orders records;
>   clock output would break goldens.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-b205c4477ebf19381963 -->

> ## Data schemas
> 
> `merge.rs`:
> 
> ```rust
> pub enum MergeOutcome {
>     /// No aligned slot changed by both sides (or identical changes): merged
>     /// result is unique AND structurally disjoint.
>     Disjoint { merged: String },
>     /// A unique candidate exists but ≥1 slot was changed by both sides
>     /// (line-disjoint within the block): deterministic, NOT safe (R4 §6).
>     UniqueOverlap { merged: String, overlapping: Vec<String /* slot keys */> },
>     /// No unique candidate (same lines touched incompatibly).
>     Conflict,
> }
> pub fn three_way(base: &str, ours: &str, theirs: &str) -> MergeOutcome
> ```
> 
> Slot key = the block's `{#id}` when present, else `anon:<index>`.
> 
> Algorithm: parse all three with `paragraph::parse`; align per D04.2; per slot
> compute `ours_changed`/`theirs_changed` vs base; no slot with both → `Disjoint`
> (merged = per-slot changed side, deletions honored, insertions appended in side
> order ours-then-theirs); slots with both but identical text → still `Disjoint`;
> slots with both where the changed LINE sets within the block are disjoint →
> line-level merge, `UniqueOverlap` listing those slot keys; otherwise `Conflict`.
> 
> `RepairRecord` persisted value = the six R4 §6 fields verbatim (serde of the
> frozen struct), key `repair:<uuid>` in `JUR_REPAIR`.
> 
> New fixture (this order authors it): `fixtures/scenarios/dag_accept.scenario.toml`
> — the `dag_id_then_reattach` world plus a final `accept_repair` step (AM-4.2) and
> `[expect] terminal = "Committed"`; used by `crash_matrix_two_step_dag` and the
> DAG-ordering trace assertions, because the base DAG fixture intentionally ends at
> `NeedsReview`.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-6dd308acba1def542df2 -->

<!-- source-block:source-a8e710f9b37d8c59cf2c -->
> ### A. Plan builders
> 
> **Save-as-Promotion** (replaces M02's placeholder construction): single
> `WriteFile` step; `expected_prestate` = observed base file hash (or `FileAbsent`);
> `expected_poststate` = merged-bytes hash; `inverse` =
> `Some(InverseRepairPlan(plan with one WriteFile of the OLD bytes, prestate = the
> new hash, poststate = the old hash))`; subject = the FILE node (real, from M03
> ingestion). Basis = `ClientScoped` capture (still M02-shaped until M6 makes
> capture real — comment the seam).
> 
> **Foreign-edit ingestion + the two-step DAG** (`ingest::foreign_change` in the
> daemon): on a foreign file change, re-parse; if a comment Relation's target alias
> vanished and only a heuristic candidate exists (structural match), build:
> 
> ```text
> s_insert:   InsertSourceId { path, at: end-of-candidate-block, entity: E }
>             prestate = FileContent(current hash); poststate = FileContent(hash after marker insertion)
> s_reattach: Graph(RetargetRelation { id: r, target: Node(candidate) })
>             prestate = RelationAt { relation: r, revision: current }
>             poststate = RelationAt { relation: r, revision: current + 1 }
> dependencies = [ { before: s_insert, after: s_reattach } ]
> inverse = None                                   // D04.5
> ```
> 
> Finalize graph ops on acceptance: `RetargetRelation` + `DeleteNode(old node)` +
> aux `JUR_ALIAS[alias] = {node: candidate, entity: E}` (EntityId continuity) +
> `JUR_REPAIR[record]`, and the M5 order adds overlay-key deletion here.
> 
> **`InsertSourceId` execution** (`FsExecutor`, which gains a store handle —
> AM-4.1's second half: `FsExecutor<'s> { root, store: &'s GraphStore }`):
> 
> 1. `bytes = read(abs)`; hash must equal the step prestate (else the verify path
>    already classified `Neither`).
> 2. `alias` = scan `JUR_ALIAS` for the entry whose `.entity == m.entity` → `a`.
> 3. `new_bytes = bytes[..at.start] ++ " {#a}" ++ bytes[at.start..]` (`at` was
>    computed against prestate bytes at plan time; the hash check makes it valid).
> 4. `stage` + `commit_if(Some(prestate hash))`.
> 5. Ack with the observed poststate hash.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-a8e710f9b37d8c59cf2c -->

<!-- source-block:source-7afe8baafc79da634202 -->
> ### B. `Checker::evaluate_repair` — the full v4 §7.7 conjunction (replaces M03's skeleton)
> 
> ```
> 0. reasons = []
> 1. ONE VALID RESULT AT THE CAPTURED BASIS
>    a. topo_order(plan) — Err(e) → "not a dependency DAG: {e}"
>    b. per-step prestate vs basis: expected_prestate must match the basis component
>       for its subject key, OR match an earlier (topo) step's expected_poststate on
>       the same key (intra-plan chaining). Mismatch → "prestate mismatch for
>       {subject}: {detail}"
>    c. WriteFile merge steps: recompute three_way(base, ours, theirs) from
>       SYS_BLOB + the current file; Conflict → "no unique result at the captured basis"
> 2. PER-SUBJECT AUTHORIZATION (mutation-local, Law 3F)
>    a. authorize(plan) — each refusal → "unauthorized: {message}"
>    b. any subject with repair_authorization == ReviewRequired →
>       "{subject}: repairs to this item always require review"
> 3. IDENTITY + INVARIANTS (what stops the DAG — v4 §7.7 worked example)
>    a. per InsertSourceId step: claim grade := Explicit if the target block ALREADY
>       carries alias(entity), else Inferred (the binding was heuristically derived —
>       nothing in Holder-controlled source proves it)
>    b. per RetargetRelation step: req = relation.requires.minimum; effective grade
>       of the new target = min(claim grades of plan steps establishing that
>       target's identity; else grade_of(target)). !satisfies(req) →
>       "reattachment relies on a heuristic match (inferred) but the relation
>       requires {req}"
>    c. dangling: no step may leave a PreserveAndSurface relation dangling
> 4. DOMAIN SAFETY (profile predicate — AM-4.1)
>    group steps by governing profile; call profile.safety_check(plan, store);
>    Err(rs) → reasons += rs. Evidence combination: all StructurallyDisjoint → one,
>    descriptions "; "-joined; mixed kinds → "mixed safety evidence; automatic
>    composition is not attempted in Phase -1"
> 5. IDEMPOTENT + REVERTIBLE
>    every step has an idempotency_key (structural); revertible :=
>    plan.inverse.is_some() OR every WriteFile prestate blob exists in SYS_BLOB;
>    neither → "no revert path recorded"
> 6. reasons empty → AutoApply { evidence } ; else NeedsReview { reasons: sorted, deduped }
> ```
> 
> `ExternalFileProfile::safety_check(plan, store)`: per governed WriteFile step,
> recompute the merge from `SYS_BLOB[base]`, `SYS_BLOB[ours]`, and the hash-verified
> on-disk file (drift → `ReviewReason("the file changed while planning")`);
> `Disjoint` with `merged == contents` → evidence; `UniqueOverlap{overlapping}` →
> `"not structurally disjoint: both edits touch {keys}"`. `InsertSourceId` steps are
> content-preserving (marker only) → contribute
> `"id-insert: #<alias> content-preserving"` to the description.
> `GraphNativeProfile::safety_check`: recomputes condition 3b for its steps; pass →
> `DomainValidator { validator: "graph-native/identity-requirement", report:
> "targets satisfy declared identity requirements at basis" }`.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-7afe8baafc79da634202 -->

<!-- source-block:source-0f3bb46875d0201d519b -->
> ### C. `ClientSession::save` (ends in the ONE IlrpDriver — R4 §4)
> 
> ```
> 1. (path, base_hash, ours) = workspace buffer state          // M6 migrates this into AvailableInputs
> 2. persist SYS_BLOB[blake3(ours)]; base blob already persisted at open
> 3. if !holder_available(store, path) → M5 branch (stub: always available at M4)
> 4. outcome = three_way(blob[base], ours, current file bytes)
>    Disjoint | UniqueOverlap → plan = save-promotion builder (merged bytes)
>    Conflict → persist JUR_PLAN[draft plan carrying ours] + (M5: Overlay + item);
>               return Ok(plan.id)                              // capture never rejected (Law 3B)
> 5. one txn: JUR_PLAN[plan] + JUR_DECISION[checker.evaluate_repair(&plan)]
> 6. AutoApply{evidence} → driver.prepare(plan, evidence); driver.run → expect
>    Committed; return Ok(plan.id)
> 7. NeedsReview{reasons} → (M5 adds Overlay + reconciliation item in this txn);
>    return Ok(plan.id)
> ```
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-0f3bb46875d0201d519b -->

<!-- source-block:source-beef1ac115d452ee976e -->
> ### D. `plan_undo` + `lim repair undo`
> 
> ```
> plan_undo(record, current):
> 1. inverse = record.inverse.as_ref().ok_or(UndoBlocked::NoInverse)?
> 2. per inverse step: check expected_prestate against `current`:
>    FileContent{path,hash} → current.components[Path(path)] must carry that hash;
>    graph predicates and Any pass here (ILRP re-verifies at apply).
>    mismatch → Err(StaleState{ detail: "<path>: expected <hex8>, found <hex8>" })
> 3. all match → Ok(inverse.clone() with basis := current.clone())
>    (step/plan ids REUSED so a double-undo is detected as already applied)
> ```
> 
> CLI flow: unknown id → stderr + exit 1. `Ok(plan)` → evidence =
> `StructurallyDisjoint{"undo of <id>: restores recorded preimages"}`;
> `evaluate_repair` must return AutoApply; prepare + run; new record with
> `selected_rule = "undo:<id>"`; stdout exactly `undone: repair:<uuid>\n`, exit 0.
> `Err(StaleState{detail})` → build a reviewable proposal (preimage WriteFile steps
> with prestate = the CURRENTLY OBSERVED durable hash — explicitly acknowledging it
> would overwrite intervening edits, which is exactly why it needs review); persist
> `JUR_PLAN` + `JUR_DECISION(NeedsReview)`; stdout
> `undo queued for review: repair:<uuid> (<detail>)\n`, exit 0. `Err(NoInverse)` →
> stderr `repair:<uuid> recorded no inverse`, exit 1.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-beef1ac115d452ee976e -->

> ### E. `lim repairs` output (zero records + zero nonterminal intents → zero bytes, exit 0)
> 
> ```
> repair:<uuid>  <selected_rule>  <evidence-kind>  <n> steps  undo available|undone|no inverse
> repair:<uuid>  needs review: <first ReviewReason>            (JUR_DECISION without a record)
> repair:<uuid>  interrupted (<state kebab>) — run recovery    (nonterminal ilrp.intent)
> ```
> 
> Sorted by repair id (UUIDv7 ⇒ chronological). `undone` = another record's
> `selected_rule` is `undo:<this id>`.
>

<!-- source-block:source-23a7e1c13d51e5b9cc13 -->
> ## Pre-made decisions
> 
> - **D05.1 — unavailability is store-resident, not filesystem tricks:** scenario
>   step `holder_unavailable` writes `SYS_UNAVAILABLE[path] = {"mode":"read-only"}`
>   (durable ⇒ survives the fixture's `daemon_restart`); `holder_available(store,
>   path)` (M04's stub) reads it; the step `holder_available` deletes the key then
>   runs `sweep_overlays`. `FsExecutor::apply` also consults it and returns
>   `Executor("holder unavailable: <path>")` — defense in depth.
> - **D05.2 — offline save still returns a `RepairId` with no API change:** the file
>   is readable (read-only mode), so the plan IS built and persisted (`JUR_PLAN`);
>   one txn writes plan + Overlay(`Active`, declared-transient lifecycle) +
>   `SYS_BLOB[ours]` — **no** decision, **no** item (a profile-declared transient
>   draft within its window ⇒ `reconciliation_items = 0`, `overlays = 1`, exactly
>   the fixture, R4 §2.3).
> - **D05.3 — coalescing keeps one current draft plus the full chain:** a second
>   offline save to the same subject updates the existing `Active` overlay
>   (`operation` = new draft, `last_activity` = now, same id/created_at) and appends
>   `JUR_OVERLAY_LOG["overlay:<uuid>/0001"] = {"at":…, "operation":{…prior…}}`
>   (4-digit seq) — v4 §7.10.2: coalesce without erasing history.
> - **D05.4 — fake clock = store-resident offset, honestly traded:** REJECTED: a
>   `LIMINAL_CLOCK` env read inside `Timestamp::now()` (core-crate amendment,
>   per-call env) and a `Clock` abstraction (ripples through frozen structs).
>   CHOSEN: `advance_clock { by_secs }` accumulates `SYS_CLOCK["offset_ms"]`; daemon
>   helper `now_with_offset(store) = Timestamp::now() + offset` used by ALL aging
>   math and by `lim overlays` (separate process, same store). `created_at` remains
>   real wall time; determinism comes from offsets (days) ≫ test runtime (ms) plus
>   coarse age rendering. This is a deliberate honesty trade, documented here; no
>   core amendment.
> - **D05.5 — root-cause key grammar (binding, reused by M11):**
>   `<category>:<key>`, categories `conflict | identity | offline | ambiguity |
>   undo` — e.g. `conflict:path:notes.md`, `identity:path:notes.md#p-fourier`,
>   `offline:path:notes.md`, `undo:repair:<uuid>`,
>   `ambiguity:client:<uuid>:path:notes.md`.
> - **D05.6 — Overlay departure paths only:** accepted repair (the Finalize txn
>   deletes the overlay key — history stays in the log), explicit discard, explicit
>   searchable archive (v4 §7.10.7). No GC exists (prohibition #13).
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-23a7e1c13d51e5b9cc13 -->

> ## Data schemas
> 
> Overlay value (ns `JUR_OVERLAY`, key `overlay:<uuid>`):
> 
> ```json
> {"id":"<uuid>","subject":{"node":"<uuid>"},"base":{…WorkspaceBasis…},
>  "operation":{"write-file":{"path":"notes.md","contents":[…]}},
>  "created_at":1789000000000,"last_activity":1789000000000,
>  "profile":"external-file",
>  "lifecycle":{"surface_after":{"secs":3600,"nanos":0},"escalate_after":{"secs":86400,"nanos":0},"declared_transient":true},
>  "state":"active"}
> ```
> 
> Creation sites (complete list): (1) offline save (D05.2); (2) NeedsReview save
> (M04 Algorithm C step 7 — this order fills that seam: same txn writes one Overlay
> with `state: RepairProposed(plan.id)` + one coalesced `conflict:` item);
> (3) DAG proposal (two overlays — source-ID insertion + relation endpoint — one
> item, per v4 §7.7); (4) ILRP recovery `Neither` → `Contested` (M02 machinery; M05
> verifies the shape); (5) stale undo (M04 Algorithm D).
>

> ### B. `sweep_overlays` (runs at workspace open after recovery, after every
> scenario step, and before `lim overlays` / `lim check` output)
> 
> - Aging: per `Active` overlay, `age = now_with_offset − created_at`;
>   `(declared_transient && age > escalate_after) || (!declared_transient && age >
>   surface_after)` → upsert item (`offline:path:<p>`, Pending, overlays=[id]).
> - Holder-return: overlay whose write route is now available → load/rebuild the
>   plan (re-verify prestates; drift → rebuild via `three_way` at a fresh basis) →
>   `evaluate_repair` → AutoApply ⇒ prepare + run (Finalize deletes the overlay key
>   and resolves any covering item); NeedsReview ⇒ `state = RepairProposed(plan.id)`
>   + item.
>

<!-- source-block:source-edc65a4f5dba95f1b40d -->
> ### C. `lim overlays` output (everyday vocabulary ONLY — R4 §3)
> 
> Zero active overlays → zero bytes, exit 0. One line per overlay, sorted by
> `created_at` then id, two-space columns: `<status>  <path>  <age>`.
> 
> Status: `Active`+transient → `pending sync`; aged past escalate →
> `pending sync (overdue)`; `Active` non-transient → `draft`; `RepairProposed` →
> `review needed`; `Contested` → `review needed (conflict)`; `--all` adds
> `archived`/`discarded` rows. Age: `<n>s` <60s, `<n>m` <60m, `<n>h` <24h, else
> `<n>d`. Example: `pending sync  notes.md  5s`.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-edc65a4f5dba95f1b40d -->

>   fixtures declare `checker_stdout = ""` despite carrying Overlays, and the

>   asserts byte-silence on a workspace with exactly one `RepairProposed`

>   visible incident per root cause — `lim check` must not duplicate it.

>   Frozen surfaces list): JUR050 now fires only for `OverlayState::Contested`
>   (the genuine "ILRP recovery could not resolve, never guess" case, v4 §7.8
>   step 5) — a state Phase -1 never actually constructs yet (creation site 4

>   shape"). `Active`/`RepairProposed` drafts stay checker-silent and are
>   surfaced exclusively via `lim overlays` / the Reconciliation Queue, matching

<!-- source-block:source-2d7b2515eb5a8677bcde -->
> ## Pre-made decisions
> 
> - **D06.1 — `resolve()` reads ONLY the requester's working map** — Law 3J by
>   construction, not by filtering.
> - **D06.2 — ambiguity is handled at PUBLISH time, not resolve time** (the frozen
>   `working` map holds one component per key): when a client opens a SECOND
>   divergent buffer over an already-buffered path with no selection, the daemon
>   (a) removes `working[client][key]` (subject falls back to durable — v4 §7.5) and
>   (b) upserts one coalesced `ambiguity:client:<uuid>:path:<p>` item.
>   `ClientSession::select_working` (AM-6.2) records the selection, republishes that
>   buffer's component, and resolves the item.
>   `PerspectiveError::AmbiguousWorkingHolder` remains the guard for the
>   inconsistent state (selection names a buffer other than the published one — a
>   bug, surfaced loudly).
> - **D06.3 — epoch source:** `ToyWorkspace::open` bumps `SYS_EPOCH["epoch"]` by one
>   (its own txn) → the process's `SessionEpoch`. Generation = per-buffer counter
>   starting at 0.
> - **D06.4 — buffer blobs at `SYS_BLOB["buf/<client>/<buffer>/<generation>"]`** so
>   memoized queries can read exact generation bytes.
> - **D06.5 — M04's private buffer map migrates into `AvailableInputs`** (single
>   source of truth); `save` now captures a real `basis(ClientScoped{client})` and
>   the M02 placeholder basis construction is deleted.
> - **D06.6 — memo staleness is defined on component VALUES, not keys** (all three
>   perspectives read `path:notes.md`; key equality cannot distinguish clients):
>   an entry is stale ⇔ re-resolving its perspective yields, for some key in
>   `deps.read`, a component ≠ the entry's captured `snapshot[key]`.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-2d7b2515eb5a8677bcde -->

Classification: `mixed-clause`. Original lines 73–95; text SHA-256: `e4c0dd31443ad8745cac73eeae3b62106524664a26391dae68bdf74cf7dd76a9`.

<!-- source-block:source-9c56be2e6e2a26399040 -->
> ### A. `resolve(inputs, perspective, at)` — every v4 §7.5 rule
> 
> ```
> 1. components = match perspective:
>    DurableOnly → inputs.durable.clone()                    // ignores ALL working claims
>    ClientScoped{client}:
>      a. base = inputs.durable.clone()
>      b. for (key, comp) in inputs.working.get(client).unwrap_or_default():
>         match inputs.working_selection.get(client).and_then(|m| m.get(key)):
>           None → base[key] = comp                          // publisher guarantees uniqueness (D06.2)
>           Some(sel) if comp is BufferGeneration{buffer == *sel} → base[key] = comp
>           Some(_) → return Err(AmbiguousWorkingHolder{key, client})
>         // other clients' maps are NEVER read — Law 3J by construction
>      c. base
>    Published{..} → Err(PerspectiveError::PublishedUnavailable)   // AM-6.1
>    Federated{..} → Err(PerspectiveError::NoFederationFrontier)
> 2. Ok(WorkspaceBasis { transaction: at, perspective: perspective.clone(), components })
> ```
> 
> Requester-less consumers (exports, background jobs) never call `ClientScoped` —
> the daemon's consumers pass `DurableOnly` explicitly; the fail-closed rule is
> asserted by the M12 gate test.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-9c56be2e6e2a26399040 -->

<a id="source-1680c707d267174dcb6d"></a>

Classification: `mixed-clause`. Original lines 96–105; text SHA-256: `b3a7044b7febf9aa1c16041091930f0f50bd19ce1626fb1215d9c472f1980dad`.

<!-- source-block:source-1680c707d267174dcb6d -->
> ### B. Buffer generation production
> 
> `open_buffer(path)`: mint `BufferId`; read file → `H_base`; persist
> `SYS_BLOB["buf/<c>/<b>/0"]`; register buffer state; publish
> `working[client][Path(p)] = BufferGeneration { client, buffer, epoch,
> generation: 0, content_hash: Some(H_base), base_file_hash: Some(H_base) }` — or
> run the D06.2 ambiguity procedure. `edit(buffer, contents)`: `generation += 1`;
> hash + persist blob; build the component; publish if this buffer is the
> selected/only one; return it.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-1680c707d267174dcb6d -->

<!-- source-block:source-9e39ff0a096b89192ddb -->
> ## Pre-made decisions
> 
> - **D07.1 — placement:** lab code is a module of the conformance crate —
>   `conformance/src/identity/{mod.rs, strategy.rs, ops.rs, gitenv.rs, matrix.rs,
>   claims.rs}`. No new workspace member.
> - **D07.2 — normalization** (shared by sidecar/content-hash/structural):
>   `normalize(text)` = per line trim, collapse whitespace runs to one space, join
>   `"\n"`, drop leading/trailing empty lines.
> - **D07.3 — structural matching is defined, not vibes:** exact `normalize`
>   equality first; else Jaccard over 3-gram character sets of normalized text
>   (text < 3 chars = one gram); unique argmax ≥ 0.5 → `Recovered(score)`; tie
>   (|Δ| ≤ 1e-9) → `Ambiguous`; best < 0.5 → `Lost`. A heuristic never grades above
>   `Inferred`.
> - **D07.4 — determinism:** every random choice comes from
>   `SmallRng::seed_from_u64(seed)`; same seed twice → identical bytes (tested).
> - **D07.5 — worst-outcome total ordering:** `Lost < Ambiguous < Recovered(c)`
>   (lower c worse) `< Preserved(g)` (weaker grade worse, per
>   `IdentityGrade::strength` — expose a helper if needed as an additive fn).
> - **D07.6 — git version floor:** assert `git --version` ≥ 2.44 (merge-ort era);
>   FAIL the run on older git — never skip; record the exact string in the report
>   header.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-9e39ff0a096b89192ddb -->
