> ## Data schemas
> 
> `conformance/fixtures/identity/config.toml`:
> 
> ```toml
> [corpus]
> seeds = [11, 22, 33, 44, 55, 66, 77, 88]
> min_git = "2.44"
> 
> [[template]]
> id = "notes"
> text = """
> The Fourier transform decomposes a signal
> into its constituent frequencies. {#p-fourier}
> 
> The Laplace transform generalizes it
> to the complex plane. {#p-laplace}
> 
> Anonymous paragraph with no marker,
> used for heuristic-continuity cases.
> """
> 
> [strategies]
> enabled = ["inline-id", "sidecar", "content-hash", "structural", "revision-anchor", "managed-graph"]
> 
> [structural]
> ngram = 3
> jaccard_threshold = 0.5
> 
> [operations]
> enabled = ["rename_move", "split", "merge", "copy_paste", "duplicate_identical",
>            "delete_recreate", "formatter_rewrite", "external_edit",
>            "git_merge", "git_rebase", "git_cherry_pick"]
> 
> [operations.git]
> conflict_policies = ["ours", "theirs", "union"]
> overlap_probability = 0.5
> ```
> 
> Outcome type (`strategy.rs`):
> 
> ```rust
> pub enum Outcome { Preserved(IdentityGrade), Recovered { confidence: f32 }, Ambiguous, Lost }
> ```
> 
> Sidecar schema (`<file>.ids.json`):
> `{"blocks":[{"index":n,"id":"s","hash":"<blake3-hex of normalize(text)>"}]}` —
> written at base and NEVER updated by the operation (that is the point).
> 
> Revision anchor:
> `Anchor { byte_offset: u64, len: u64, ctx_before: Vec<u8> /*≤16*/, ctx_after: Vec<u8> /*≤16*/ }`
> (ctx truncated at file bounds). Exported from the identity module — M09 reuses it.

Classification: `mixed-clause`. Original lines 103–130; text SHA-256: `3720dce8dc6a94e64aec679a4b74f105d35ab17e2f4be1bc386323bab6521366`.

<!-- source-block:source-de225f97219f1941e075 -->
> ### A. The six strategies (observation → outcome, deterministic)
> 
> 1. **inline-id** — re-parse after the op: id present exactly once →
>    `Preserved(Explicit)`; ≥2 → `Ambiguous`; absent → `Lost`.
> 2. **sidecar** — per entry: unique block with equal hash at same index →
>    `Preserved(Explicit)`; unique equal hash at different index →
>    `Recovered(0.9)`; equal hash at ≥2 blocks → `Ambiguous`; no hash match →
>    block at recorded index with Jaccard ≥ threshold → `Recovered(0.5)`; else
>    `Lost`. Under `rename_move`, the sidecar moves with the file iff a seeded bool
>    says so — both worlds exercised.
> 3. **content-hash** — blake3 of `normalize(text)`: equal hash exactly once →
>    `Preserved(ContentAddressed)`; ≥2 → `Ambiguous`; zero (any text change) →
>    `Lost`. (Version identity, not entity identity — the matrix is expected to
>    show this.)
> 4. **structural** — D07.3.
> 5. **revision-anchor** — (1) bytes at `offset..offset+len` unchanged AND both
>    contexts match → `Preserved(Anchored)`; (2) exactly one occurrence of
>    `ctx_before ∥ anchored bytes ∥ ctx_after` anywhere → `Recovered(0.9)`;
>    (3) exactly one occurrence of the anchored bytes alone → `Recovered(0.6)`;
>    ≥2 occurrences at step 2/3 → `Ambiguous`; none → `Lost`.
> 6. **managed-graph** — the file mirrored into the M03 graph. Operations are
>    tagged **observed** (driven as graph transactions: rename_move, split, merge,
>    copy_paste, duplicate_identical, delete_recreate) or **foreign** (bytes changed
>    behind the Holder: formatter_rewrite, external_edit, all git ops). Observed →
>    assert entity continuity in the store → `Preserved(Managed)`. Foreign →
>    re-ingest and fall back to rule 4 — honestly demonstrating v4 §19.2: Managed
>    holds only while the Holder observes the operation.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-de225f97219f1941e075 -->

<a id="source-3c125ee31803c1c95e12"></a>

Classification: `mixed-clause`. Original lines 131–155; text SHA-256: `52a8961fcfcabd825e1fb385d6bd415024d424ba8a7c3983058973442e238e8f`.

<!-- source-block:source-3c125ee31803c1c95e12 -->
> ### B. The eleven operations (exact seeded mutations)
> 
> 1. `rename_move` — `git mv notes.md docs/renamed.md` (bytes identical).
> 2. `split` — seeded block with ≥2 sentences (split on `". "`); insert `\n\n` at a
>    seeded sentence boundary; a `{#id}` marker stays with the seeded half.
> 3. `merge` — join two seeded adjacent blocks with one space; if both carry
>    markers keep the first's, delete the second's.
> 4. `copy_paste` — append a byte-exact copy of a seeded block (marker included →
>    duplicate id) after `\n\n`.
> 5. `duplicate_identical` — append TWO byte-identical copies of the anonymous
>    block → three identical anonymous blocks.
> 6. `delete_recreate` — delete a seeded block; append a block with identical text
>    but NO marker at the original position.
> 7. `formatter_rewrite` — deterministic: greedy re-wrap to width 72, collapse
>    blank-line runs to one, strip trailing whitespace, single trailing newline.
> 8. `external_edit` — k = seeded 1..=3 blocks; per block one seeded mutation of
>    {replace seeded word with `EDITED<seed>`, delete last sentence, prepend
>    `Inserted by seed <seed>. `}.
> 9. `git_merge` — base commit; branch `b` edits block X; `main` edits block Y
>    (X == Y with probability `overlap_probability`); `git merge -s ort --no-edit b`;
>    conflicts per policy.
> 10. `git_rebase` — same divergence; `git rebase main` on `b`; `--continue`.
> 11. `git_cherry_pick` — commit on `b`; `git cherry-pick <sha>` onto `main`;
>     `--continue`.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-3c125ee31803c1c95e12 -->

> ### C. Hermetic git runbook (`gitenv.rs`)
> 
> Env per case (nothing else inherited):
> 
> ```
> GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null  GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM=/dev/null  GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1
> HOME=<case tmpdir>  XDG_CONFIG_HOME=<case tmpdir>/xdg
> GIT_AUTHOR_NAME=liminal-lab   GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL=lab@liminal.invalid
> GIT_COMMITTER_NAME=liminal-lab GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL=lab@liminal.invalid
> GIT_AUTHOR_DATE=2026-01-01T00:00:00Z  GIT_COMMITTER_DATE=2026-01-01T00:00:00Z
> TZ=UTC  LC_ALL=C  GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0  GIT_PAGER=cat  PAGER=cat
> GIT_EDITOR=true  GIT_SEQUENCE_EDITOR=:
> ```
> 
> Script: `git -c init.defaultBranch=main init` → write template (+ sidecar when
> active) → add/commit → `checkout -b b` → edits → commit → `checkout main` → edits
> → commit → run the op. Conflict policies (seeded choice): **ours** =
> `git checkout --ours -- <file>`; **theirs** = `--theirs`; **union** = strip
> conflict markers keeping both sides in order; then `git add` +
> `merge|rebase|cherry-pick --continue`.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-f914a5cf814f325090ba -->

> ### D. Grading + matrix
> 
> Per (strategy, operation, seed): build base world, capture strategy state, run
> op, observe per Algorithm A → one Outcome per tracked block; case outcome = worst
> across tracked blocks (D07.5). Matrix cell = worst outcome across seeds.
> 
> `conformance/golden/identity_matrix.md` format:
> 
> ```
> # Identity guarantee matrix (Phase -1.1, M7)
> 
> git: <exact `git --version` output>
> config: blake3:<hex of config.toml bytes>
> seeds: 8
> 
> | operation | inline-id | sidecar | content-hash | structural | revision-anchor | managed-graph |
> |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
> | rename_move | Preserved(explicit) | … | … | … | … | Preserved(managed) |
> …
> | git_cherry_pick | … |
> ```
> 
> Cells render `Preserved(<kebab grade>)` | `Recovered(0.62)` (two decimals) |
> `Ambiguous` | `Lost`; rows in `operations.enabled` order, columns in
> `strategies.enabled` order; managed cells on foreign rows carry the suffix
> ` [foreign]`.
>

> ### E. `claims_never_exceed_evidence` (`claims.rs`)
> 
> `cap(cell)`: `Preserved(g) → g`; `Recovered(_) → Inferred`;
> `Ambiguous | Lost → Anchored`. `cap(column) = min over rows`; for `managed-graph`
> compute over **observed** rows only (graph-native subjects have no file for git to
> mangle — v4 §7.6).
> 
> Assertions:
> 1. `ExternalFileProfile.required_identity` (`Anchored`) ≤ `cap(col)` for each of
>    inline-id, sidecar, structural, revision-anchor.
> 2. `GraphNativeProfile.required_identity` (`Managed`) ≤
>    `cap(managed-graph | observed)`.
> 3. **grade_of ceiling:** for every inline-id cell where `cap(cell) < Explicit`
>    (e.g. `copy_paste` → Ambiguous), replay that post-op file through the M03
>    checker and assert a finding (JUR041/JUR042) is emitted — never silence.
>    "No stronger claim than demonstrated" = every demonstrated degradation is
>    either below the declared floor (1–2) or loudly surfaced (3).
> 
> Failure of 1–3 is the killer firing: demote the grade in the profile via ADR
> before M08 begins.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-6eeb9c334df5a24e4e6c -->

Classification: `open-gap`. Original lines 268–332; text SHA-256: `fce09294131bc8218e46c00745752f3c771ca4ff84bf3cbe614aa6755262f94b`.

<!-- source-block:source-72e63540af045d92e6ec -->
> ## Discovered gaps
> 
> - **DG-7.1 (M07.7, assertion 3 aggregation).** Assertion 3's imperative — "for
>   every inline-id cell where `cap(cell) < Explicit` … assert a finding
>   (JUR041/JUR042) is emitted" — contradicts its own explanatory clause, which
>   frames the guarantee as a *disjunction*: "every demonstrated degradation is
>   either below the declared floor (1–2) OR loudly surfaced (3)." Taken literally,
>   the imperative fails on inline-id **`Lost`** cells (a `{#id}` deleted with no
>   duplicate — e.g. `delete_recreate`, `external_edit`'s last-sentence deletion, a
>   git `ours`/`theirs` drop): the post-op file simply lacks that id, and a file
>   that never carried the id is sound → the checker is byte-silent.
> 
>   **Candidate readings.** (a) Literal: every inline-id cell `< Explicit` must emit
>   a finding → the killer fires on every `Lost` cell, demanding an ADR demotion the
>   floors already encode. (b) Disjunctive (the explanatory clause): a degradation is
>   honest iff it emits a finding **or** is bounded by the declared floor.
> 
>   **Resolution (reading b, spec-grounded in v4 §19.2).** §19.2 states that when
>   external tools "delete … or recreate anonymous text, perfect logical identity is
>   information-theoretically **unavailable**" — so a `Lost` id is *unsurfaceable by
>   construction*, and the honest response is the Anchored floor, not a diagnostic.
>   A duplicated id (`Ambiguous`), by contrast, *is* surfaceable (two blocks claim
>   one id) and MUST never be silently accepted. Assertion 3 is therefore
>   implemented as: for each inline-id cell with `cap(cell) < Explicit`, replay the
>   post-op file through the M03 checker and assert **`Ambiguous ⇒ a JUR042 finding
>   is emitted`**, while `Lost ⇒ cap(cell) == the ExternalFileProfile floor
>   (Anchored)`, i.e. bounded by the declared floor (the "(1–2)" branch). This keeps
>   the check non-vacuous (the `Ambiguous` branch has real teeth), never weakens the
>   duplicate-collision guarantee, and matches the explanatory clause verbatim.
>   Assertions 1–2 independently prove the floors are honest (they hold with
>   equality: worst demonstrated cap == declared floor).
> 
> - **DG-7.2 (M07.3, structural exact-equality outcome).** D07.3 says "exact
>   `normalize` equality first; else Jaccard … `Recovered(score)` … `Ambiguous` …
>   `Lost`", but does not name the outcome of an exact match. Candidate readings:
>   (a) `Preserved(Inferred)`; (b) `Recovered(1.0)`. **Resolution: (b).** The rule's
>   listed outcome vocabulary for structural is `{Recovered, Ambiguous, Lost}` only
>   — structural is a heuristic and never `Preserved` (v4 §19.2). "exact equality
>   first" is the max-score fast path (Jaccard = 1.0). A unique exact match →
>   `Recovered(1.00)`; ≥2 exact matches → `Ambiguous`. Both cap at `Inferred`, so
>   no assertion outcome depends on the choice.
> 
> - **DG-7.3 (M07.4, B2 split has no valid target on the template).** B2 targets "a
>   seeded block with ≥2 sentences (split on `". "`)", but every template block is a
>   single sentence spanning two physical lines — `". "`-splitting finds no interior
>   boundary. Candidate readings: (a) split is a no-op (no qualifying block); (b)
>   split at interior line breaks. **Resolution: (b), the faithful generalization.**
>   The split-boundary set for a block is the byte positions after each interior
>   `". "` UNION the positions after each interior `"\n"`; B2 inserts a blank line
>   (`"\n\n"`) at the seeded boundary from that set. The block's trailing `{#id}`
>   marker rides with the *second* (later) half — the half that keeps the original
>   last line — so inline-id sees the id exactly once (`Preserved(Explicit)`). A
>   block with no interior boundary is not a split candidate; if no block qualifies
>   the op is the identity (unchanged file).
> 
> - **DG-7.4 (M07.5, B9–B11 divergence edits under-specified).** The git runbook
>   says "branch `b` edits block X; `main` edits block Y" but not the exact bytes.
>   **Resolution (deterministic, seeded):** the edit replaces the block's FIRST word
>   with a side-tagged token — `"BranchB"` on `b`, `"OnMain"` on `main`. X is a
>   seeded block index; Y == X with probability `overlap_probability` (seeded),
>   else a different seeded block. Overlap on the same block yields a real merge-ort
>   conflict resolved per the seeded [`ConflictPolicy`]; disjoint blocks merge
>   cleanly. This keeps the git cells a genuine function of merge-ort behavior while
>   being byte-reproducible.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-72e63540af045d92e6ec -->

> ## Data schemas
> 
> `GraphStore` additions (`crates/liminal-graph/src/store/asof.rs`):
> 
> ```rust
> impl GraphStore {
>     /// As-of read: replay retained segments from genesis into a scratch State,
>     /// stopping after the record with revision == rev. The toy never GCs
>     /// segments, so genesis replay is always available; O(n) is toy-fine.
>     pub fn state_at(&self, rev: GraphRevisionId) -> Result<StateView, StoreError>;
> }
> pub struct StateView { /* owns a State materialized at rev */ }
> impl StateView {
>     pub fn node(&self, id: NodeId) -> Option<&Node>;
>     pub fn relation(&self, id: RelationId) -> Option<&Relation>;
>     pub fn relations_from(&self, source: NodeId) -> Vec<&Relation>;
>     pub fn children(&self, parent: NodeId) -> &[NodeId];
>     pub fn get_aux(&self, ns: &str, key: &str) -> Option<&serde_json::Value>;
>     pub fn head(&self) -> GraphRevisionId;
> }
> ```
> 
> (Internal `SegmentLog::replay_range` helper reuses `replay_segment`.
> `node_at`/`relation_at`/`relations_from` keep the in-memory fast path at head and
> delegate to `state_at` for `rev < head`.)
> 
> AM-8.2 — the graph component's map key:
> 
> ```rust
> // liminal-revision::basis
> pub fn graph_key() -> JurisdictionKey { JurisdictionKey::Path(PathId(".liminal/graph".into())) }
> ```
> 
> Reserved documented path; `GraphSnapshot { revision }` always sits at that key.
> 
> AM-8.3 — durability classes (`crates/liminal-revision/src/durability.rs`):
> 
> ```rust
> pub enum Durability { Immutable, High, Medium, Low, Ephemeral }   // v4 §24.1 verbatim
> pub fn durability(c: &BasisComponent) -> Durability {
>     match c {
>         ObjectContent{..} | GitCommit{..}      => Immutable,
>         FileContent{..} | GraphSnapshot{..}    => Medium,
>         BufferGeneration{..} | Observation{..} | ExternalRevision{..} => Low,
>     }
> }
> ```
> 
> Doc note verbatim from §24.1: durability is an invalidation optimization, not
> truth or freshness. Used only to order the cache's staleness checks (Low first);
> a unit test asserts the table is total.
> 
> Reactor:
> 
> ```rust
> pub struct Observation { pub source: SourceId, pub observed_at: Timestamp, pub payload: serde_json::Value }
> impl ToyWorkspace { pub fn inject_observation(&mut self, obs: Observation) -> Result<GraphRevisionId, WorkspaceError> }
> ```
>

<!-- source-block:source-04eb33252ae9a4a4cc70 -->
> ### A. The four queries (`liminal-daemon/src/queries.rs`, each `impl liminal_query::Query`)
> 
> | Query | Output | Reads / records |
> |---|---|---|
> | `RenderBlock { node }` | `String` — `"{alias}: {text}\n"` (alias omitted when none) | text from the perspective-selected component for the owning file: buffer blob (`SYS_BLOB["buf/<c>/<b>/<g>"]`) or file blob; records `Path(file)`; alias from graph → records `graph_key()` |
> | `Backlinks { node }` | `Vec<RelationId>` sorted | `state_at(GraphSnapshot.revision)` relations targeting node; records `graph_key()` |
> | `WorkspaceExport` | `String` — all files, blocks re-emitted in child order with `{#id}` markers, `\n\n` separators | every `FileContent` component + graph; records each `Path(p)` + `graph_key()` |
> | `AiContextStub { focus }` | canonical JSON `{"focus","text","neighbors":[…],"basis":{"transaction","perspective"}}` | focus text per RenderBlock rule + neighbor blocks via graph; records those keys |
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-04eb33252ae9a4a4cc70 -->

<!-- source-block:source-a503e4d0a2f2a4335659 -->
> ### B. Inject flow (one transaction)
> 
> 1. `hash = ContentHash::of(canonical payload bytes)`.
> 2. `put_aux(SYS_BLOB, "obs/<source>/<hash>", payload)`.
> 3. `Operation::MaterializeExternal { node: external-value node, source, observed: hash, at }`; commit.
> 4. `AvailableInputs.durable[Source(source)] = Observation { source, observed_at, hash }`.
> 
> Scenario step `resolver_observe` fields:
> `{ source = "stock:acme", price = 42.17, at = "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z" }`.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-a503e4d0a2f2a4335659 -->

<!-- source-block:source-4c4a3633bc5060c7c53a -->
> ### C. Freeze/replay harness (`conformance/src/replay.rs`)
> 
> `freeze(basis, workspace) -> String`: canonical JSON (BTreeMap ordering) of
> `{ basis, blobs: { <component key>: bytes } }` where blobs carries, for every
> component, the exact bytes it pins (buffer blob, file bytes, observation payload,
> and the serialized `state_at(revision)` State for the graph component).
> `FrozenWorld::load(&str)` serves reads purely from that JSON. Test flow: run the
> scenario → capture the 4 outputs → freeze each basis → **delete the workspace
> directory** → re-execute the four queries against `FrozenWorld` → byte-identical
> outputs (final-gate requirement).
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-4c4a3633bc5060c7c53a -->

> ## Amendments
> 
> - AM-8.1: runner step vocabulary gains `resolver_observe` and `query` (additive).
> - AM-8.2: `liminal_revision::basis::graph_key()` — the GraphSnapshot component
>   needs a stable map key; none existed.
> - AM-8.3: `liminal_revision::durability` module (additive; v4 §24.1 transcription).
> - AM-8.4: `SourceId::from_name(&str)` (deterministic UUIDv5 from a well-known
>   external source name) + the `uuid` `v5` feature — resolves DG-8.1. Additive.
> - AM-8.5: `GraphStore::put_working_aux` (ephemeral, unlogged, non-head-bumping
>   aux write) for buffer blobs. An editor keystroke is not a durable graph
>   transaction; committing buffer blobs bumped the graph revision and spuriously
>   invalidated every graph-reading query. `session::persist_buffer_blob` now uses
>   it. Additive store method; behaviour change confined to buffer-blob persistence
>   (all 128 tests, incl. the full crash matrix, stay green).
> - AM-8.6: `ToyWorkspace::basis` now inserts `GraphSnapshot{head}` at `graph_key()`
>   (M08.2 "basis capture puts GraphSnapshot at it").
> - AM-8.7: the four queries run against a `liminal_daemon::queries::World` seam
>   (additive) so the SAME query executes over the live `(store, root)` and the
>   M08.8 `FrozenWorld`. `StateView` gains additive enumeration accessors
>   (`nodes()`, `relations()`, `scan_aux()`) the queries need; the M08.md data
>   schema already froze `node`/`relation`/`relations_from`/`children`/`get_aux`/
>   `head`. `runner::ingest_files`/`ingest_graph` widened to `pub(crate)` for the
>   query unit tests.
> - AM-8.8 (M08.3): `runner::refresh_file_blobs`, called from `apply_or_review`'s
>   `AutoApply` arm — refreshes `SYS_BLOB["file/<path>"]` to a save's landed
>   bytes. Additive (no signature changes; a plain post-`driver.run` commit in
>   the same shape as the existing `record_repair` call, so it adds no new
>   crash checkpoint).
> - AM-8.9 (M08.6): `liminal_graph::kind::EXTERNAL_VALUE` — a new node kind
>   constant for the `MaterializeExternal` target (toy: at most one per
>   scenario, mirroring the single-FILE-node convention `file_node_for`
>   already uses). Additive.
> - AM-8.10 (M08.7): `ToyWorkspace::root()` widened `pub(crate)` → `pub`, like
>   `store()` — callers outside `liminal-daemon` (the `four_consumers`
>   milestone test, in `liminal-conformance`) need it to build a `LiveWorld`
>   over an opened workspace. Additive (visibility widening only).
> - AM-8.11 (M08.7): `runner::exec` now drops and reopens `ToyWorkspace` once,
>   immediately after `ingest_files`/`ingest_graph`, before running any step.
>   **Not purely additive** — a behavioural change to the shared scenario
>   runner, so recorded here rather than silently folded into M08.7's "Done"
>   note. Cause: `seed_durable_inputs` (D06.5) runs at `open`, which happens
>   BEFORE `exec`'s own ingest — so `AvailableInputs.durable` never gained the
>   just-ingested file's `FileContent` component within one continuous `exec`
>   session. `runner::apply_query`'s `ws.basis(...)` call is the FIRST
>   scenario-runner code path to actually resolve a Basis in-process (prior
>   steps — `buffer_edit`/`save` — never touch `AvailableInputs` at all, per
>   their own long-standing scratch-`BTreeMap` + direct-`GraphStore`-txn
>   design), so this gap was latent and unexercised until M08.7. The fix
>   mirrors two ALREADY-established patterns: `queries.rs`'s own unit tests
>   open the workspace twice (ingest, then reopen) for exactly this reason
>   (noted in the M08.4 commit message), and the `daemon_restart` step already
>   exercises the identical drop+reopen (M05 AM-5.1). Verified inert for every
>   existing scenario: none of them read `AvailableInputs`/`ws.basis()`, and
>   recovery + the overlay sweep are no-ops with nothing pending this early.
>   All 160 workspace tests (incl. the full crash matrix) stay green.
> - AM-8.12 (M08.8): `liminal_graph::StateView::synthetic(...)` — a new `pub`
>   constructor building a `StateView` from raw parts (head, nodes, relations,
>   children, aux; `transactions` defaults empty — no `StateView` accessor
>   ever reads it). Needed because `World::graph_at`'s return type,
>   `StateView`, has no public constructor: its one field (`state: State`) is
>   private and `State` itself is `pub(crate)`, so only code INSIDE
>   `liminal-graph` can build one — normally via `GraphStore::state_at`'s log
>   replay. `FrozenWorld` (`conformance/src/replay.rs`, a different crate)
>   serves `graph_at` purely from a previously frozen snapshot with no live
>   store and no log to replay, so it needs a way to construct a `StateView`
>   synthetically. Purely additive: no existing signature changes; `state_at`
>   and every existing `StateView` accessor are untouched.
> - AM-12.5 (M08 exit gate, user-ratified 2026-07-19): preserve M06's shared
>   `JurisdictionKey::Path(path)` grammar. The interactive-preview dependency
>   assertion requires that Path key and verifies its captured value is neovim's
>   `BufferGeneration`, never phone's; client identity lives in the component,
>   not a per-client key variant.
>

<!-- source-block:source-f9ab6128767586d7fb16 -->
> ## Discovered gaps
> 
> - **DG-8.1 (M08.6, source name → `SourceId`).** The scenario's
>   `resolver_observe` uses `source = "stock:acme"`, but `SourceId` is a UUID
>   newtype with no string mapping; `BasisComponent::Observation.source` is typed
>   `SourceId`. **Resolution:** `SourceId::from_name(name)` derives a STABLE id via
>   UUIDv5 (`NAMESPACE_OID`, name bytes) — deterministic across runs/machines, so a
>   frozen Basis replays byte-identically (v4 §42). The blob key `obs/<source>/<hash>`
>   uses the derived id's Display form. Recorded as AM-8.4.
> 
> - **DG-8.2 (M08.8, `just gates` delta is +8, not the predicted +2).** The
>   work order's "Predicted `just gates` delta" section reads "Active +2" —
>   matching only the two NAMED exit-gate tests
>   (`four_consumers_two_dirty_buffers`, `replay_from_frozen_basis_is_deterministic`).
>   `conformance/src/debt.rs::scan_workspace_debt` (the mechanism behind `just
>   gates`) counts every bare `#[test]` fn anywhere in the workspace source
>   tree, not a curated exit-gate-only set — so it also counts the 6
>   born-passing `reactor.rs` unit tests M08.6 added
>   (`parse_utc_timestamp_matches_known_epochs`,
>   `parse_utc_timestamp_rejects_non_utc`,
>   `inject_observation_materializes_and_records_durable_component`,
>   `second_observation_of_the_same_source_reuses_the_node`,
>   `scripted_resolver_observe_pops_in_order`,
>   `scripted_resolver_replay_is_pure_and_deterministic`) — T3's own "test
>   scaffolding" mandate, and the only way `cargo nextest run -p liminal-daemon
>   reactor` (M08.6's own listed command) exercises anything. `just gates`
>   measured **188 active / 27 backlog** against the 180/27 baseline: **Active
>   +8, backlog unchanged** (the ignored-test counts the protocol treats as
>   load-bearing did not move). Per the executor brief ("record it, do not
>   adjust tests to force it"), no test was deleted or hidden to force the
>   count back to +2.
> 
> - **DG-8.3 (T1 review, M08.3's mirror missed `accept_repair`).** M08.3 mirrored
>   `WriteFile` bytes into `SYS_BLOB["file/<path>"]` at save time, but
>   `InsertSourceId` mutates the file on disk WITHOUT carrying the landed bytes
>   in-plan — after `accept_repair`, the blob was a stale pre-acceptance echo.
>   Undetectable via the stock `dag_accept` fixture (a pure marker strip whose
>   acceptance restores the ORIGINAL bytes verbatim). **Resolution:**
>   `runner::refresh_inserted_file_blobs(store, root, plan)` re-reads each
>   `InsertSourceId` path from disk AFTER the driver commits, called from
>   `accept_repair`; regression test
>   `m08::file_blob_fresh_after_accept_repair` uses a strip-AND-append foreign
>   edit (candidate matching is exact-text, so the target paragraph must stay
>   byte-identical while the file as a whole changes) and was falsified both
>   ways: fails without the fix on exactly the staleness assertion, passes with
>   it.
> 
> - **DG-8.4 (T1 review, `freeze` trusted current disk bytes).**
>   `replay::freeze` read a `FileContent` component's bytes from the CURRENT
>   file without checking them against the basis-pinned hash — a frozen payload
>   could silently contradict its own Basis if the file changed after capture.
>   **Resolution:** `freeze` now verifies `ContentHash::of(bytes)` equals the
>   pinned hash and errors otherwise; test `m08::freeze_rejects_stale_file_bytes`
>   tampers post-capture and asserts refusal. Also from the same review pass:
>   reactor transactions now carry `Origin::Remote` (an observation comes from
>   an external service, not a human edit).
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-f9ab6128767586d7fb16 -->

> ## Pre-made decisions
> 
> - **D09.1 — spike placement:** `conformance/spikes/spike-annotation/` and
>   `conformance/spikes/spike-richedit/` as workspace members with
>   `publish = false` and NO `[lints] workspace = true` — direct lib linkage lets
>   the m09 tests regenerate reports in-process (deterministic goldens, no
>   subprocess cargo), while lints-off + publish=false marks them non-production
>   and trivially deletable at box end. (Workspace `members` gains
>   `"conformance/spikes/*"` — AM-9.1.)
> - **D09.2 — anchors = M07's revision-anchor strategy verbatim** (type + 5-step
>   recovery ladder), exported from `conformance/src/identity/`. Ambiguous/Lost are
>   NEVER silently reattached — they surface (feeds the L3 "0 silent
>   misattachments" criterion).
> - **D09.3 — foreign-edit generator = M07's 11 operation scripts, same seeds.**
> - **D09.4 — capability-level thresholds (THE declared policy, v4 §8.4):**
>   - L0: always.
>   - L1: emit+parse both directions run, with a populated declared-loss table.
>   - L2: 100% canonical round-trip on UNEDITED docs across the corpus
>     (`parse(emit(g)) == g` on the supported subset AND `emit(parse(s))`
>     idempotent).
>   - L3: L2 AND anchor recovery (Exact|Shifted) ≥ 95% over non-git foreign ops AND
>     ≥ 80% over git ops AND 0 silent misattachments.
>   - L4: L3 AND 100% undo-fidelity under the concurrent-edit script AND a real
>     merge runtime — **declared out of reach for Phase -1** (building one is
>     prohibition #2); the report may never declare L4.
>   Declared level = highest level whose thresholds the frozen report meets.
> - **D09.5 — time-box enforcement:** box start/end dates go in the report header;
>   at expiry, unconditionally freeze the report, snapshot the golden, set
>   `DECLARED_LEVEL` to what is demonstrated, stop work. No extension without an
>   ADR.
>

<!-- source-block:source-e963c81702f2cb460f55 -->
> ## Data schemas
> 
> Spike 1:
> 
> ```rust
> pub struct Annotation { pub id: u32, pub range: SourceRange, pub kind: AnnKind, pub payload: String }
> pub enum AnnKind { Mark, Link, Comment }
> pub struct AnnotatedDoc { pub text: String, pub annotations: Vec<Annotation> }
> ```
> 
> Each annotation carries one M07 `Anchor`; after every foreign edit, re-anchor →
> per-annotation outcome ∈ {Exact, Shifted(conf), Ambiguous, Lost}. Projection:
> paragraphs → PARAGRAPH nodes, annotations → Relations with `Target::Anchored`.
> 
> Spike 2 op set: `insert_text{block, offset, text}`, `delete_range{block, range}`,
> `add_mark{block, range, kind}`, `split_block{block, offset}`,
> `join_block{block}`, `undo`.
> 
> Graph-op mapping:
> 
> | editor op | graph transaction |
> |---|---|
> | insert_text / delete_range | `SetPayload(node, new_text)` |
> | add_mark | `AddRelation` (mark Relation, `Target::Anchored`) |
> | split_block | `CreateNode(new)` + `SetPayload(first-half)` + `InsertChild(parent, new, i+1)` + retarget Relations whose anchor falls in the second half |
> | join_block | `SetPayload(first, joined)` + retarget second's incoming Relations → first (grade check via Q4) + `DeleteNode(second)` |
> | undo | inverse transaction from recorded inverse ops — never byte restoration (R4 §11.3 spirit) |
> 
> Report format (`conformance/golden/anchor_recovery.md`):
> 
> ```
> # Anchor recovery report (Phase -1.2, M9)
> 
> box: 2026-MM-DD .. 2026-MM-DD (hard 2-week box)
> config: blake3:<hex of M7 config.toml>   git: <exact version>   seeds: 8
> 
> | operation class | recovery % | identity % | undo fidelity % |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | rename_move | 100.0 | 100.0 | n/a |
> …(11 foreign-op rows, then 6 rich-edit-op rows)…
> 
> declared level: <0|1|2|3>
> ```
> 
> One decimal place; fixed row order (M07 `operations.enabled` order, then the
> spike-2 op order above). Dimensions: **recovery%** = annotations Exact|Shifted /
> total; **identity%** = tracked paragraphs whose entity survives per
> anchor/structural rules / total; **undo-fidelity%** = byte+graph-faithful undos /
> undos attempted (`n/a` on foreign rows).
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-e963c81702f2cb460f55 -->

> ## Algorithms
> 
> The measurement loop, per operation class: (1) build the annotated base doc from
> the M07 template (3 annotations per block: one Mark, one Link, one Comment at
> seeded ranges); (2) apply the operation (foreign classes via the M07 script;
> rich-edit classes via the spike-2 op set); (3) re-anchor every annotation through
> the M07 five-step ladder → tally recovery; (4) re-ingest and grade entity
> survival via the M07 structural rule → tally identity; (5) rich-edit rows only:
> apply `undo`, compare bytes AND graph state to pre-op → tally fidelity;
> (6) accumulate per class across 8 seeds; render per the report format. The level
> computation (D09.4) runs over the finished table and is the same function
> `declared_level_matches_report` re-runs.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-77220cc6df43da678521 -->

<!-- source-block:source-3e2fed3a5f4458592123 -->
> ## Pre-made decisions
> 
> - **D10.1 — AST encoding:**
> 
>   | Toy construct | Pandoc JSON | Markdown round-trip form |
>   |---|---|---|
>   | document | `{"pandoc-api-version":[1,23,1],"meta":{},"blocks":[…]}` | n/a |
>   | paragraph, no `{#id}` | `Para [Str/Space…]` | plain paragraph |
>   | paragraph with `{#id}` | `Div ("<id>",[],[]) [Para […]]` | fenced div `::: {#id}` |
>   | comment Relation | **none — DECLARED loss** (`may_discard`) | dropped at emit |
>   | foreign-node probe | `RawBlock ("html","<!--liminal:probe-->")` | raw HTML passthrough |
> 
>   Justification: `Para` carries no Attr in the Pandoc AST; `Header` attrs would
>   lie about block kind; `Div` is Pandoc's only attributed block container and
>   round-trips losslessly through the markdown writer/reader as a fenced div, so
>   ID survival is a real measurement. Inline encoding: text split on whitespace →
>   alternating `Str`/`Space`; reimport flattens `Str`→text,
>   `Space`/`SoftBreak`→`" "`.
> - **D10.2 — pipeline:** emit Pandoc JSON directly (no no-op json→json pass);
>   `pandoc -f json -t markdown-smart --wrap=none -o roundtrip.md ast.json` then
>   `pandoc -f markdown-smart -t json -o ast2.json roundtrip.md`. `-smart` both
>   directions so typographic rewriting doesn't pollute structural-loss numbers;
>   `--wrap=none` so wrapping doesn't pollute text fidelity. API version hardcoded
>   `[1,23,1]` (pandoc-types for 3.6.x).
> - **D10.3 — version pin:** `pandoc --version` first line must equal
>   `pandoc 3.10.2`; missing binary or version mismatch →
>   `panic!("M10 requires pandoc 3.10.2; found {…}. Update the
>   pin + regenerate the golden if intentionally upgrading.")`. **No silent skip,
>   no `#[ignore]`** — a skipped loss report would fake Law 8. (This machine has
>   `/usr/bin/pandoc`; CI must install it or fail loudly — intended.)
> - **D10.4 — Level rule:** the adapter declares **Level 1** iff blocks, order,
>   text, and id survival are all 100% AND every non-surviving construct appears in
>   the transform contract's `may_discard`. Any dimension < 100% and undeclared →
>   Level 0 for that construct class and the gate fails. Level 2 is NOT declared
>   (comment Relations don't survive); paragraph-subset second-pass stability
>   (`markdown → json → markdown` byte-stable) is recorded as informative only.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-3e2fed3a5f4458592123 -->

<!-- source-block:source-9286cac7c5c455c15fc2 -->
> ## Algorithms
> 
> Measurement procedure: (1) ingest the fixture through the M03 grammar + setup
> vocabulary → toy doc + 2 comment Relations; (2) `emit` → `ast.json` (D10.1
> mapping, probe RawBlock appended); (3) run the D10.2 pipeline → `roundtrip.md` →
> `ast2.json`; (4) `normalize` both ASTs → `Vec<(Option<id>, text)>`; (5) compute
> the six dimensions (block count; positional order+text; positional id survival;
> relation loss = declared by construction; probe byte-identity); (6) render the
> report; (7) compute the declared level via D10.4 — the same function
> `declared_level_matches_loss_report` re-runs.
>

<!-- source-block:source-e58847febe6b4a2e32be -->
> ## Pre-made decisions
> 
> - **D11.1 — coalescing constant `COALESCE_GAP_MS = 2000`** (§7.4 names the rule,
>   not the constant; frozen by the golden): consecutive `buffer_edit` on the same
>   buffer with logical gaps < 2000 ms and NO intervening event of any other type →
>   one semantic transaction. Boundary cases in the golden: gap 1999 coalesces, gap
>   2000 splits, an interleaved `save` splits.
> - **D11.2 — session constant `SESSION_TIMEOUT_MS = 1_800_000`** (30 min, §7.4
>   verbatim). Explicit open/close wins; otherwise first activity opens, a ≥30-min
>   gap in that client's activity closes at the previous event. Workspace-stream
>   events attach to every session active at their `at` for incident accounting;
>   outside any session they count in the corpus-wide op denominator but no session
>   metric.
> - **D11.3 — root-cause coalescing reuses D05.5's key grammar**
>   (`<category>:<key>`, e.g. `git:merge@420000`): all user-visible surfaces
>   sharing one key within one session = ONE visible incident;
>   `max_visible_incidents_per_root_cause` = max over `(session, key)` — must be
>   ≤ 1 to graduate.
> - **D11.4 — auto-resolved numerator (R4 §2.3):** an op counts iff replay reaches
>   the profile's declared stable outcome with zero manual-intervention surfaces,
>   zero unexpected reconciliation items, zero diagnostics, and no fallback to an
>   UNDECLARED Overlay. Profile-declared transient drafts (saves during
>   `holder_unavailable`) are excluded from both numerator and denominator → the
>   side `TransientDraftReport { declared, reconciled_within_window,
>   aged_into_debt }`.
> - **D11.5 — trace parser rejects unknown fields** (`deny_unknown_fields`) —
>   corpus defects fail loudly.
> - **D11.6 — NO new `lim` subcommand.** Conformance bins instead: `scorecard`
>   (AM-11.2) and `gen-manifest` (AM-11.1); generators in `tracegen` (AM-11.3).
> - **D11.7 — the locking ceremony order is BINDING:** assemble → gen-manifest →
>   commit → flip the denominator golden → ONLY THEN one scorecard run per profile
>   on heldout/v1, recorded to `conformance/golden/scorecard-heldout-v1.json` → v1
>   frozen forever. Debugging failures happens by reproduction in `fixtures/` or
>   minimization into `corpora/regression/` — never by reading held-out traces.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-e58847febe6b4a2e32be -->

<a id="source-b7ffc965b8171eea7f71"></a>

Classification: `mixed-clause`. Original lines 64–84; text SHA-256: `63bc953ec98eab68c76fbd1fdfa5f3e12a51f8cd32e3e2ec9f2a48386c82919f`.

<!-- source-block:source-b7ffc965b8171eea7f71 -->
> ## Data schemas
> 
> NDJSON, one JSON object per line, `serde(tag = "type", rename_all =
> "snake_case")`. Every event has `at: u64` (logical ms, monotone nondecreasing).
> Root-cause-capable events carry `cause_category` + `cause_key`; derived events
> repeat the SAME pair.
> 
> | type | fields |
> |---|---|
> | `trace_header` (line 1, mandatory) | `version: 1`, `trace_id`, `source`, `capture_tool`, `consent: "consented-anonymized"\|"synthetic"\|"public-git"`, `profile`, `setup: { files: [{path, contents}], graph: […M03 setup tables…] }` |
> | `session_open` / `session_close` | `at`, `session`, (`client` on open) |
> | `buffer_open` | `at`, `session`, `client`, `buffer`, `path` |
> | `buffer_edit` | `at`, `session`, `buffer`, `range: {start, end}` (byte splice), `insert` |
> | `save` | `at`, `session`, `buffer` |
> | `file_change_external` | `at`, `path`, `contents` (full new bytes; toy scale), `cause_category: "foreign"\|"formatter"\|"git"`, `cause_key` |
> | `git_op` | `at`, `op: "commit"\|"merge"\|"rebase"\|"cherry-pick"\|"checkout"`, `files: […]`, `cause_category: "git"`, `cause_key: "<op>@<at>"` |
> | `formatter_rewrite` | `at`, `path`, `contents`, `tool`, `cause_category: "formatter"`, `cause_key: "<tool>@<at>"` |
> | `holder_unavailable` / `holder_available` | `at`, `holder` (+ cause pair on unavailable: `"holder"`, `"<holder>@<at>"`) |
> | `resolver_observe` | `at`, `source`, `observed`, `cause_category: "resolver"`, `cause_key: "<source>@<at>"` |
> | `clock_advance` | `at` only — a pure logical-time jump; a jump ≥ 30 min splits sessions |
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-b7ffc965b8171eea7f71 -->

<!-- source-block:source-d3a8df42402d67d81753 -->
> ### A. Event → Jurisdiction-sensitive-operation counting (every type decided)
> 
> | event | ops counted |
> |---|---|
> | trace_header, session_open/close, clock_advance | 0 |
> | buffer_open | **1** (a read choosing Holder + Basis) |
> | buffer_edit | 0 individually; **each semantic transaction = 1** |
> | save | **1** (Promotion = repair) |
> | file_change_external | **1** — **0** if its `(cause_category, cause_key)` matches a prior `git_op` (it is the byte delivery of an already-counted op) |
> | git_op | **len(files)** (one foreign-edit ingestion per affected file) |
> | formatter_rewrite | **1** |
> | holder_unavailable | 0 |
> | holder_available | **1 per Overlay reconciliation attempted** on Holder return |
> | resolver_observe | **1** |
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-d3a8df42402d67d81753 -->

<a id="source-a7dbcd155c9cf198834c"></a>

Classification: `mixed-clause`. Original lines 102–120; text SHA-256: `6b546312b214c00cf6b518a9b7f4d932ac0ba07798a296d89d9cee23ddfabd3b`.

<!-- source-block:source-a7dbcd155c9cf198834c -->
> ### B. Importers / generators (`tracegen` bin, five subcommands)
> 
> - `tracegen git <op-script> <out>` — M07 hermetic runbook; replay an M07 op
>   script; walk `git log --reverse` diffs; step k → `at = k × 60_000`; each op →
>   one `git_op` + one `file_change_external` per changed file (same cause pair).
>   Header: `source: "m7-script:<name>"`, `consent: "synthetic"`.
> - `tracegen session <session.toml> <out>` — expands scenario-style TOML into
>   open/buffer/edit/save/close with an `at` schedule (per-step `dt`, default
>   500 ms). Dev stand-in; held-out instances come from independently supplied
>   scripts (POLICY: never authored by the profile author).
> - `tracegen formatter <fixture-dir> <out>` — deterministic rewrites (M07 op 7
>   vocabulary) → `formatter_rewrite` events.
> - `tracegen offline <out>` — `holder_unavailable` → edits + save (durable
>   Overlay) → `clock_advance` past the window → `holder_available`; drives the
>   transient-draft/aging path for the third slo test.
> - `tracegen adversarial <m7-op> <seed> <out>` — M07 identity-torture ops replayed
>   as `file_change_external {cause_category:"foreign"}` — independent because
>   generated by the identity lab, not tuned by profile authors (R4 §2.2).
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-a7dbcd155c9cf198834c -->

<a id="source-33402bf8d77adbbdc7e3"></a>

Classification: `mixed-clause`. Original lines 121–135; text SHA-256: `3560ee676cae1064ef1b8aeb173775e23a302ebdd3f054d89180a11f3df67bc2`.

<!-- source-block:source-33402bf8d77adbbdc7e3 -->
> ### C. Pipeline (`conformance/src/{trace.rs, denominator.rs, pipeline.rs}`)
> 
> `pipeline::run(corpus_dir, profile) -> (Scorecard, TransientDraftReport)`:
> 1. Per trace: build `ToyWorkspace` from `trace_header.setup`; replay events
>    through the M03/M05 runner (`session_open→open_session`,
>    `buffer_open→open_buffer`, `buffer_edit→edit`, `save→save`,
>    `file_change_external|formatter_rewrite→apply_foreign_change`,
>    `holder_*→set/clear + sweep`, `resolver_observe→inject_observation`,
>    `clock_advance→advance_clock`).
> 2. Collect observables per event: checker output bytes, diagnostics,
>    reconciliation items (expected vs unexpected, keyed by cause),
>    contract-authoring prompts, overlay dispositions.
> 3. Apply A + D11.1–D11.4 → all nine frozen Scorecard fields per profile.
> 4. The side `TransientDraftReport`.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-33402bf8d77adbbdc7e3 -->

>   generator per profile, `*.trace.ndjson`.
> - Hand-labeled denominator traces:

>   git-rootcause, offline-transient}.trace.ndjson` + expected-counts golden —
>   these freeze D11.1–D11.3 BEFORE any tuning.
> - heldout/v1: generate with seeds DISJOINT from dev (seeds recorded in each

>   public-repo history (provenance in header); place under
>   `conformance/corpora/heldout/v1/`; run `gen-manifest` (walks the tree, BLAKE3
>   per file, writes `MANIFEST.b3` sorted, excluding itself; output must
>   round-trip `verify_heldout_manifest` — tested); commit; ceremony per D11.7.
>

> - AM-11.2: conformance `[[bin]] scorecard`.
> - AM-11.3: conformance `[[bin]] tracegen`.
> (Bins are invocable surface — flagged even though the crate is publish=false.)
> - AM-11.4: `liminal_daemon::runner::StepRunner` — Algorithm C step 1 says
>   "replay events through the M03/M05 runner" and step 2 "collect observables
>   PER EVENT", but the runner's only public entry (`exec`) ran a whole
>   scenario atomically: per-event observation was impossible without either
>   duplicating the save/foreign-edit semantics in the conformance crate
>   (poisonous: the pipeline would measure a second implementation) or a
>   public per-step seam. Additive refactor: `exec`'s setup + step-loop body
>   moves verbatim into `pub struct StepRunner` (`open`/`open_buffer`/`step`/
>   `workspace`/`workspace_mut`/`root`); `exec` delegates and is
>   behavior-identical (full workspace suite incl. the derived crash matrix
>   green before landing). `open_buffer` is the one NEW capability — a
>   mid-stream buffer registration over current durable bytes, needed for the
>   trace `buffer_open` event; at time zero it is exactly `exec`'s
>   setup-buffer seeding. Call sites: `runner::exec` (delegation),
>   `conformance/src/pipeline.rs` (M11.5).
> 
> - AM-11.5 (M11.7 prep): `tracegen import <repo-dir> <out> --source <provenance>
>   [--max-commits <n>] [--ext <list>]` — the Algorithm D real-public-repo
>   importer. First-parent walk oldest-first (the trace models a workspace
>   tracking the default branch; a merge delivers its full mainline diff as one
>   `git_op`); base commit → setup.files; deleted paths counted in `git_op.files`
>   but never delivered (no bytes exist); non-UTF-8 blobs skipped with the count
>   recorded in the header `source` (no silent caps); `Consent::PublicGit`. Path parsing uses NUL-separated (`-z`) git output
>   throughout — real histories contain committed filenames with trailing
>   whitespace (tldr's early `ls.md   `) that line-based parsing corrupts.
> 
> - AM-11.6 (M11.7, user-ratified 2026-07-19): corpus traces may be stored
>   zstd-compressed (`.trace.ndjson.zst`) — `pipeline::read_trace_file` is the
>   one decode site; `corpus_traces` accepts both extensions; `MANIFEST.b3`
>   freezes the COMPRESSED bytes. Rationale: the two full-history imports are
>   177MB raw but 9MB at zstd-19 (near-identical consecutive file versions),
>   and an in-tree corpus keeps checkouts self-verifying, CI hermetic, and the
>   go/no-go auditable from the repo alone — a download link can rot or drift,
>   and MANIFEST.b3 could only detect that, not undo it.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-7d24e9097ffef1ec7857 -->

<!-- source-block:source-dd73ef1d70d23395cffe -->
> ## Discovered gaps
> 
> - DG-11.1: Algorithm A's `holder_available` row ("1 per Overlay
>   reconciliation attempted on Holder return") is not literally computable
>   from the trace alone without a reading of what a "Holder" identifies.
>   `denominator.rs` reads it as: Phase -1's only Holder is the file path
>   (D05.1: `SYS_UNAVAILABLE[path]`; `runner::holder_available(store, path)`;
>   Algorithm C step 1 maps trace `holder_*` events onto exactly these
>   functions), so the trace's `holder` field IS the path. The op count is
>   then the number of DISTINCT paths that received a `save` while that path
>   was unavailable and have not yet been reconciled (matching D05.3: a second
>   offline save to the same subject coalesces into the SAME Overlay, not a
>   second one). This is a T2 engineering reading, not spelled out verbatim by
>   the order; `pipeline.rs`'s actual replay (M11.5) is the authoritative
>   cross-check and should confirm or correct this before `denominator_counts_golden`
>   freezes (M11.3). Does not block M11.1/M11.2: no boundary test we own
>   exercises `holder_available` counting.
>   **Ratified at M11.3 (T1 ruling): one reconciliation per distinct
>   pending-draft path, per D05.3. Cross-checked at M11.5:**
>   `pipeline::tests::dg11_1_replay_reconciliation_attempts_match_frozen_denominator`
>   replays the `offline-transient` labeled fixture through the REAL runner
>   (AM-11.4 seam) and asserts, per `holder_available` event, that the number
>   of Overlay reconciliations actually attempted on Holder return equals the
>   frozen per-event denominator count — **replay AGREES with the frozen
>   reading** (1 attempted == 1 counted). The test stays in the suite as a
>   standing guard; any future divergence is a T1 escalation, never a silent
>   fix.
> - DG-11.2: D11.2's explicit/implicit session-boundary rule is unambiguous
>   when a `session` id has BOTH an explicit `session_open` and a matching
>   `session_close` (bracket wins outright, no internal splitting) or NEITHER
>   (fully implicit: first-activity/30-min-timeout derivation). A PARTIAL
>   bracket — only `session_open` with no matching `session_close`, or vice
>   versa — is not spelled out. `denominator.rs` treats a present bookend as a
>   hard boundary on its own end and derives the other end via the
>   first-activity/timeout rule. None of the M11.2 labeled fixtures or
>   boundary tests exercise this partial case; flag for confirmation before
>   M11.3's golden freezes.
> 
> - **DG-11.3 (M11.7 probe, RESOLVED).** Replaying an imported real history
>   failed on any file ADDED after setup (`pipeline.rs` read the current bytes
>   to build the whole-content `foreign_edit`, and a new file — often in a
>   directory that never existed at setup — has none). Found by the mandatory
>   pre-ceremony probe (150-commit tldr slice), NOT in any dev trace (all
>   fixture worlds pre-declare their files). Resolution: a missing path is a
>   foreign ADD — create parents + empty file, then the `find:""` whole-content
>   replace lands the bytes through the same runner step. Regression:
>   `m11::imported_trace_with_added_nested_file_replays`.
> 
> - **DG-11.4 (M11.8 ceremony incident, RESOLVED).** The first external-file
>   scorecard invocation ERRORED mid-replay ("Is a directory"): real histories
>   transition paths dir→file / file→dir, deletions are never replayed, and the
>   stale shape blocked the write. The invocation produced NO score (a
>   measurement failure, not a threshold miss); the graph-native score HAD been
>   observed, so v1's bytes were already frozen and were not touched or read —
>   the defect was reproduced synthetically
>   (`m11::imported_trace_with_dir_file_transitions_replays`), fixed in
>   `pipeline.rs` (stale counterpart yields to what history says the path is
>   now), and the external-file measurement then ran ONCE, validly. Ceremony
>   integrity: manifest commit ef3be1d precedes every score observation.
> 
> - **DG-11.5 (M11.8 close-out, T1 assertion edit).** `conformance/src/debt.rs`'s
>   meta-test `meter_finds_the_declared_backlog` hardcoded "Phase -1 backlog
>   must be visible" — a scaffolding assumption that Phase -1 is ongoing. M11.8
>   flips the last Phase -1 ignored tests, so its backlog is now 0 BY DESIGN
>   (M12.4 targets exactly "Phase -1 ignored = 0"); the assertion would make
>   Phase -1 impossible to finish. Re-expressed as the property it actually
>   tested — the meter partitions the backlog by phase into a populated set of
>   real "Phase N" labels — with no loss of coverage of the meter mechanism.
>   Escalated to T1 (assertion edit, §7 blanket rule 2); recorded here.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-dd73ef1d70d23395cffe -->

<a id="source-777c14f296bb1e51e6bd"></a>

Classification: `open-gap`. Original lines 135–211; text SHA-256: `1b4edebc3f2556bb7015eb5fd279f73c25ee4179011fd59cc2cb48657a088a9e`.

<!-- source-block:source-777c14f296bb1e51e6bd -->
> ## Discovered gaps
> 
> - **DG-12.1 — RESOLVED BY AM-12.3.** `four_consumers` materializes an
>   EXTERNAL_VALUE Node, but M03's older kind dispatch returned Ungoverned. Final
>   gate test 1 found it by enumerating every scenario subject.
> - **DG-12.2 — RESOLVED BY AM-12.4.** M12 freezes test 7's name with the same
>   token M05 prohibits. Exact coordinate allow-listing preserves the sweep while
>   permitting the mandated absence-assertion name.
> - **DG-12.3 — RESOLVED.** Q1 buffer capture scanned any matching client buffer
>   without first proving the subject uses the external-file profile and that the
>   component belongs to its owning path. Graph-native subjects can therefore
>   resolve to `Holder::Buffer` under a client-scoped Basis. Resolution: capture
>   only when the contract's durable Holder is that exact File path.
> - **DG-12.4 — RESOLVED.** `AvailableInputs.durable[Source(source)]` was updated
>   only in memory. Reopening a workspace reconstructs file components but drops
>   every durable Observation. Resolution: commit `obs-current/<source>` metadata
>   with materialization and reconstruct the component at open.
> - **DG-12.5 — RESOLVED.** Freeze substituted JSON null for absent buffer or
>   observation blobs and does not verify their pinned content hashes, permitting
>   a deterministic replay of bytes the Basis never named. Resolution: absence,
>   non-text buffer data, and hash mismatch now fail closed.
> - **DG-12.6 — RESOLVED.** First observation created its EXTERNAL_VALUE node in
>   one transaction and materialized the observation in a second, violating M08's
>   one-transaction inject flow. Resolution: first-node creation, blob writes,
>   current-observation metadata, and materialization share one commit.
> - **DG-12.7 — RESOLVED.** The four-consumer scenario executed query steps, but
>   its integration gate never reads the runner-persisted query outputs; direct
>   query calls could pass while runner wiring regressed. Resolution: the M08 gate
>   reads all four persisted outputs and cross-checks three against direct queries.
> - **DG-12.8 — RESOLVED.** The final undo gate proved only that reverted bytes
>   differ from repaired bytes, not that they equal the recorded preimage. Both
>   revert gates now compare bytes to the inverse plan's exact preimage.
> - **DG-12.9 — RESOLVED.** The crash matrix iterated returned terminal states
>   without requiring any terminal, so recovery that silently drops every intent
>   could pass vacuously. Baseline hits and first-recovery terminals must be
>   non-empty before matrix assertions proceed.
> - **DG-12.10 — RESOLVED.** Gate 9 treated a nonzero manifest byte length as a
>   non-empty held-out corpus; whitespace-only manifest content with an empty tree
>   passed the verifier and this assertion. The verifier now rejects an empty
>   parsed manifest, proven against a synthetic empty directory.
> - **DG-12.11 — RESOLVED BY LEDGER BACKFILL.** ADR-0008 omitted AM-3.1,
>   AM-4.1–4.3, AM-5.1, and AM-6.1–6.2 even though their work orders recorded
>   them. M12 reconciled those seven entries before omnibus ratification.
> - **DG-12.12 — RESOLVED AT M12.5.** `phases.md` requires a future phase's gate
>   tests to exist as ignored backlog at the preceding gate. M12.5 therefore
>   authored the 18-test Phase 0 surface with M13–M17; after the M12.4 historical
>   closeout count and the two meter regression tests, the live meter becomes 219
>   active and 39 deferred, including 18 Phase 0 tests.
> - **DG-12.13 — RESOLVED BY ADR-0014.** The debt scanner counted `#[test]` before
>   seeing a following `#[ignore]`, so every deferred test also inflated the active
>   count. TDD regressions now require reasoned ignores to be deferred only and bare
>   ignores to surface as unphased debt. Corrected M12.4 evidence is 217 active / 21
>   deferred; Phase -1 backlog and the GO decision are unchanged.
> - **DG-12.14 — RESOLVED BY PROTOCOL CLARIFICATION.** Phase 0's preceding-gate
>   ignored backlog and shared `phase0.rs` target exposed Phase -1-specific wording
>   that otherwise prohibited both. Section 1 now distinguishes preceding-gate
>   stubs from forbidden mid-milestone ignores; §8 assigns shared Phase 0+ gates.
> - **DG-12.15 — RECORDED PROCESS DEVIATION.** Fixed-point review found that commits
>   `88c2961`, `4044360`, `185c94a`, `3b0c757`, `7aa36f9`, `49e4b1e`, `6354838`,
>   and `38ef776` did not all satisfy the preferred singular-amendment or step/area
>   subject plus spec-citing body convention, and `3b0c757` grouped the approved
>   remediation package. History is not rewritten; this entry preserves the
>   deviation and later commits follow §6 exactly.
> - **DG-12.16 — RESOLVED IN M13.** The first six-domain topology draft named new
>   live kinds and an attribute map that existing dispatch could not govern or
>   lower. M13 now freezes domain roles as fixture-only labels, uses only
>   FILE/PARAGRAPH/EXTERNAL_VALUE plus Relations, stores typed metadata as canonical
>   payload JSON, and declares expected governance per subject.
> - **DG-12.17 — RESOLVED BY PHASE LEDGERS.** The Phase -1-only amendment procedure
>   still sent future amendments to ADR-0008 and M12. Phase 0+ now records AMs in a
>   mutable phase ledger and disposes every row through an immutable ADR at that
>   phase's final gate; `phase0-amendments.md` is open for M13–M17.
> - **DG-12.18 — RESOLVED IN M13.** Relation roles initially implied new live
>   `KindId` values. M13 now uses the existing graph-native COMMENT dispatch kind
>   and persists the exact contains/next/embeds/materializes role in Relation
>   payload, avoiding an unplanned kind registry while preserving topology checks.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-777c14f296bb1e51e6bd -->

> ## Pre-made decisions
> 
> - **D13.1 —** `spec/kernel.md` becomes normative, self-contained prose but cites
>   canonical v4/R4 and accepted RFCs for authority; it does not copy Rust source.
> - **D13.2 —** six examples use only Node and Relation with the exact topology
>   table below: prose, code block, table, image reference, audio interval, and
>   synchronized external value. A domain label alone proves nothing.
> - **D13.3 —** every Node and Relation names expected profile, Holder, and minimum
>   identity grade; `Ungoverned` and implicit identity are invalid fixture states.
> - **D13.4 —** user-facing vocabulary is domain-native. Jurisdiction, Holder,
>   Overlay, and Promotion are an explanation ceiling, not routine UI text.
> - **D13.5 —** external-file defaults to Anchored; graph-native and
>   EXTERNAL_VALUE default to Managed, exactly as ADR-0009 and AM-12.3 freeze.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-35f230fdc6cbb716a544 -->

<a id="source-18fd5e3affc35a687112"></a>

Classification: `mixed-clause`. Original lines 42–109; text SHA-256: `675c9f66fa101c55fda03d09a3812c690c69641ac7ad33d121d9641c6f14274b`.

<!-- source-block:source-18fd5e3affc35a687112 -->
> ## Data schemas
> 
> `conformance/fixtures/phase0/representation-examples.toml`:
> 
> ```toml
> version = 1
> 
> [[example]]
> id = "prose"
> domain = "prose" # prose|code|table|image|audio-interval|external-value
> 
> [[example.node]]
> alias = "document"
> role = "document" # fixture-only label, never persisted as a primitive
> kind = "FILE" # FILE|PARAGRAPH|EXTERNAL_VALUE
> payload = ""
> expected_profile = "external-file"
> expected_holder = "file:examples/prose.md"
> minimum_identity = "anchored"
> 
> [[example.node]]
> alias = "body"
> role = "paragraph"
> kind = "PARAGRAPH"
> payload = "hello"
> expected_profile = "external-file"
> expected_holder = "file:examples/prose.md"
> minimum_identity = "anchored"
> 
> [[example.relation]]
> role = "contains" # fixture semantic, persisted in payload
> kind = "COMMENT" # Phase -1 toy's graph-native Relation dispatch key
> from = "document"
> to = "body"
> payload = "contains"
> expected_profile = "graph-native"
> expected_holder = "graph"
> minimum_identity = "managed"
> ```
> 
> Node `role` is fixture-only vocabulary used by the topology oracle; it is not
> written to graph state. Relation `role` is persisted as its canonical text payload
> while live `Relation.kind` remains `COMMENT`, the Phase -1 toy's only graph-native
> Relation dispatch key. This preserves semantic distinctions without inventing
> future domain `KindId` values. Node `payload` is UTF-8 text or canonical JSON text
> where the table below names fields. Each example has non-empty, unique `id`; exact
> nodes and relations required below; live Node kinds restricted to `FILE`,
> `PARAGRAPH`, and `EXTERNAL_VALUE`; relation endpoints naming aliases in the same
> example; and per-subject expected profile, concrete Holder, and grade.
> `minimum_identity` uses `IdentityGrade` kebab-case spelling. Domain is closed to
> the six values for v1.
> 
> | Domain | Exact node roles and live kinds | Exact Relation roles (`kind=COMMENT`) and payload constraints |
> |---|---|---|
> | prose | `document:FILE`, `paragraph:PARAGRAPH` | `contains(document, paragraph)`; paragraph payload non-empty |
> | code | `document:FILE`, `code-block:PARAGRAPH` | `contains(document, code-block)`; canonical payload object has non-empty `text` and `language = "rust"` |
> | table | `document:FILE`, `table:PARAGRAPH`, two `row:PARAGRAPH`, four `cell:PARAGRAPH` | document contains table; table contains both rows; each row contains two cells; `next(row-1,row-2)`; every cell payload non-empty |
> | image | `document:FILE`, `image-reference:PARAGRAPH` | `embeds(document, image-reference)`; canonical payload object has `sha256` as 64 lowercase hex plus non-empty `mime` and `alt` |
> | audio-interval | `document:FILE`, `audio-interval:PARAGRAPH` | `contains(document, audio-interval)`; canonical payload object has resource `sha256` plus unsigned `start_ms < end_ms` |
> | external-value | `external-source:EXTERNAL_VALUE`, `value:EXTERNAL_VALUE` | `materializes(external-source, value)`; canonical payloads carry non-empty source ID, revision token, observation timestamp, and value |
> 
> Validator compares aliases, kinds, relation triples, multiplicities, and listed
> payload predicates exactly, including equality of Relation role and persisted
> payload text. For the first five examples, every FILE/PARAGRAPH is
> external-file/its declared file/Anchored and every Relation is
> graph-native/graph/Managed. Both external-value Nodes and its Relation are
> graph-native/graph/Managed. Six copies of one topology with different labels fail.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-18fd5e3affc35a687112 -->

> ## Pre-made decisions
> 
> - **D14.1 —** authorization remains conjunctive and mutation-local; no subject's
>   Contract confers write authority over another subject.
> - **D14.2 —** Promotion is display vocabulary for an accepted RepairPlan, never a
>   second state machine.
> - **D14.3 —** automatic application requires authorization, exact prestate,
>   identity/invariant preservation, domain safety, idempotency, and recorded undo.
> - **D14.4 —** recovery derives cases from baseline hit traces. Hand-listed crash
>   points are explanatory only and cannot define coverage.
> - **D14.5 —** Overlay debt leaves active state only by accepted repair, explicit
>   discard, or searchable archive. Aging changes visibility, never durability.
> - **D14.6 —** requester-less or ambiguous computations resolve DurableOnly;
>   client-scoped Bases can select components from only the requesting client.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-a18ddeeef536391c614a -->

> ## Scope
>

> ## Frozen surfaces
>

> eight `TransformContract` field names, projection law names, canonical v4 files,

<a id="source-28052a925f2e8a79478d"></a>

Classification: `mixed-clause`. Original lines 27–45; text SHA-256: `61bafa73a0a2c44ba51bfd1177ae07ac2dce9f0d6782034f186911c2511efefa`.

<!-- source-block:source-28052a925f2e8a79478d -->
> ## Pre-made decisions
> 
> - **D15.1 —** entity identity and immutable version identity remain separate;
>   heuristics never prove logical continuity.
> - **D15.2 —** projection claims are per supported subset and direction. No
>   universal bidirectional promise is expressible.
> - **D15.3 —** `TransformContract` remains data with exactly eight §14 fields;
>   Phase 0 freezes JSON field names but not Phase 3's future typed atom vocabulary.
> - **D15.4 —** interim graph interchange is stable debug JSON only. No final binary
>   serialization is selected before migration evidence (v4 §121).
> - **D15.5 —** interpretive Jurisdiction, RepairPlan, Basis selection, and ILRP stay
>   reference oracles. Compiled plans remain forbidden until differential evidence
>   satisfies §125.
> - **D15.6 — T1 RESERVED DECISION:** source grammar choice among §119's three
>   alternatives requires explicit user acceptance of its ADR before CST work.
> - **D15.7 — T1 RESERVED DECISION:** Salsa versus a Liminal-specific revision
>   engine requires explicit user acceptance of its ADR before Phase 1 tracked
>   query work. Required boundaries in §122 are non-negotiable under either choice.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-28052a925f2e8a79478d -->

<a id="source-4630b8006aa3352c2d41"></a>

Classification: `mixed-clause`. Original lines 46–59; text SHA-256: `b7582497ff0b84519c3b2a70132bf95b156b1346f0cba22f6ef68c95b6ea8535`.

<!-- source-block:source-4630b8006aa3352c2d41 -->
> ## Data schemas
> 
> `spec/fixtures/transform-contract.schema.json` is JSON Schema draft 2020-12:
> object, `additionalProperties: false`, all eight fields required. `requires`,
> `preserves`, `introduces`, `may_discard`, and `required_capabilities` are arrays
> of unique non-empty strings; three boolean fields retain exact Rust names.
> 
> `spec/fixtures/transform-contract.examples.json` contains `version: 1` and at
> least one nondestructive and one destructive example. Destructive means
> `may_discard` non-empty and therefore requires explicit acceptance before run.
> `liminal-conformance` adds a path dev-dependency on `liminal-transform`. Schema
> validation is the exact manual subset above, implemented with serde and explicit
> key/type/uniqueness checks; no general JSON-Schema dependency is introduced.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-4630b8006aa3352c2d41 -->

>    a golden measurement or accepted ADR.
> 2. Serialize live `TransformContract` examples, validate against schema, reject

> 4. Run a contradiction audit: declared grade/level must equal the accepted ADR

>

> ## Frozen surfaces
> 
> Denominator constants and scorecard thresholds; held-out/v1 bytes and manifest;
> existing golden scorecards; trace/session/scenario schema versions; `retries = 0`;
> sound-session byte-silence requirement. Locked corpus contents are never opened,

<a id="source-1f98c4a14fb587b237a4"></a>

Classification: `mixed-clause`. Original lines 27–46; text SHA-256: `a4663b3349a98d03b2de3ac24021bf8b7dd5407e6d2a96320796b608e213ef0e`.

<!-- source-block:source-1f98c4a14fb587b237a4 -->
> ## Pre-made decisions
> 
> - **D16.1 —** development, locked acceptance, and regression corpora remain
>   separate. A failure is minimized into regression data without exposing or
>   altering locked source traces.
> - **D16.2 —** any v2 corpus is independently sourced, sanitized, labeled, and
>   locked by a custodian before profile authors receive only verifier results.
> - **D16.3 —** v1 scores remain forever; a new version adds evidence and never
>   overwrites history.
> - **D16.4 —** Phase 0 security scope covers graph store, filesystem Holders,
>   clients/buffers, resolver observations, repair execution, plugins/processes,
>   corpus handling, and supply chain. Each boundary names assets, attacker,
>   entry points, failure mode, control, detection, recovery, and residual risk.
> - **D16.5 —** prior-art decisions adopt boundaries, not wholesale systems. Each
>   v4 §118A reference gets Adopt/Adapt/Defer/Reject disposition with evidence and
>   a falsifier.
> - **D16.6 —** M13–M16 introduce no new stable profile or trace category, so v1 is
>   reverified unchanged and v2 is not created. Discovery of a missing category is
>   a T1 gap requiring a separately authorized custodian ceremony.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-1f98c4a14fb587b237a4 -->

<a id="source-e9d8822960a5f8078061"></a>

Classification: `mixed-clause`. Original lines 47–64; text SHA-256: `30e7ff33b48b57d854ffe1c7b2c760ec357f8e584aee5ce0e3262e9ea9aa8e16`.

<!-- source-block:source-e9d8822960a5f8078061 -->
> ## Data schemas
> 
> `docs/security/threat-model.md` has one table row per threat:
> 
> ```text
> TM-ID | asset | trust boundary | attacker/capability | entry point |
> failure mode | preventive control | detective control | recovery |
> verification | residual risk | owner
> ```
> 
> IDs are `TM-<two digits>` and never reused. Severity uses a separate
> `impact: low|medium|high|critical` and `likelihood: unlikely|possible|likely`
> pair; no opaque combined score.
> 
> `conformance/fixtures/README.md` documents each fixture family, version field,
> parser, canonicalizer, malformed-case policy, golden owner, and confidentiality
> class (`public|sanitized|locked`).
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-e9d8822960a5f8078061 -->

<a id="source-acfa2e2543bc3f6d0890"></a>

<!-- source-block:source-acfa2e2543bc3f6d0890 -->
> ## Algorithms
> 
> 1. Build fixture inventory only from tracked paths outside locked corpus trees;
>    verify each documented public/sanitized fixture family has a parser and owner.
> 2. Invoke existing locked-manifest and scorecard tests as black-box verifiers.
>    Record exit status and committed scorecard hash; never print trace data.
> 3. Combine sound-session assertions in one gate: byte-empty diagnostics/checker
>    output, zero unexpected items, zero manual Contract authoring, and no hidden
>    transient debt past policy window.
> 4. Threat-model review uses abuse cases, STRIDE-style prompts only as coverage
>    aids, and explicit crash/recovery verification. Unsupported mitigations are
>    follow-ups, not claims.
> 5. Record one accepted ADR for the §118A disposition matrix after user review;
>    any direct dependency adoption needing its own reversible decision gets its
>    own ADR.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-acfa2e2543bc3f6d0890 -->

> ## Pre-made decisions
> 
> - **D17.1 —** real-CST experiment lives under `conformance/spikes/real-cst/` and
>   may depend on a mature parser selected by the accepted grammar ADR. No
>   `liminal-cst` production API is created here.
> - **D17.2 —** use development/regression projection fixtures only. Train/test
>   cases are declared before measurement; no case is removed after failure.
> - **D17.3 —** Level 3 requires merge-class anchor recovery ≥95%, all supported
>   canonical round-trip laws, selection/mark boundary survival, malformed-input
>   non-panic behavior, undo correctness, and no undeclared loss. One failed
>   conjunction keeps Level 2.
> - **D17.4 —** report records numerator, denominator, Wilson 95% interval, failures
>   by class, seeds, toolchain/dependency versions, git commit, and wall-clock time.
> - **D17.5 —** Phase 0 GO is a new T1 decision after adversarial review. Green CI
>   is necessary, never sufficient.
> - **D17.6 —** Phase 1 work orders and tests are proposed at the gate. Ratification
>   requires a separate user-directed adversarial review; no checkbox or passing
>   test can substitute for that human decision.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-2ac575b7e07002d2c0ba -->

> ## Data schemas
> 
> `conformance/golden/anchor_recovery_real_cst.md`:
> 
> ```text
> status: measured
> grammar_adr: <accepted ADR path>
> substrate: <crate and exact version>
> git_commit: <40 lowercase hex>
> measurement_tree: <40 lowercase hex tree id>
> declared_level: <0..4>
> merge_recovered: <u64>
> merge_total: <u64>
> merge_rate: <decimal>
> wilson95_low: <decimal>
> wilson95_high: <decimal>
> seed_set_sha256: <64 lowercase hex>
> elapsed_ms: <u64>
> ```
> 
> Follow with a deterministic table: case ID, edit class, seed, expected anchor,
> observed anchor, outcome, declared loss. Sort by `(edit_class, case_id, seed)`.
> `git_commit` records the parent commit used to run the measurement;
> `measurement_tree` records the staged source tree. `elapsed_ms` is evidence shown
> in the report but redacted to `<MEASURED>` by golden comparison, matching M07's
> provenance-redaction pattern.
> 
> `docs/execution/phase1-suite-review.md` records suite version, fixed review base,
> test inventory, law/class/abuse/fault coverage matrices, mutation-testing results,
> fuzz budgets, uncovered risks, reviewer findings with verification disposition,
> and status `proposed|ratified|rejected`. It also records the ADR-0020 HAQP-1
> profile, continuous- and qualification-lane commands, bidirectional requirement
> mapping, mutant numerator/denominator and dispositions, gate-canary results, five
> generated/fuzz family reports, oracle-independence audit, registered crash-boundary
> inventory, dependency/toolchain provenance, raw artifact hashes, campaign elapsed
> time, and residual-risk coordinates. Initial status is `proposed`.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-0c02b941444db524fabf -->

<a id="source-e8b62588e41ab3ac2eeb"></a>

<!-- source-block:source-e8b62588e41ab3ac2eeb -->
> ## Algorithms
> 
> 1. Freeze case inventory and seed set before running. Hash only the declared
>    development/regression inventory, never locked acceptance data.
> 2. For each case, run parse → annotate → foreign edit → incremental reparse →
>    anchor recovery plus full-reparse oracle. Compare canonical graph, exact loss,
>    selection/mark boundaries, and undo. Catch panics as failures.
> 3. Compute merge rate and Wilson interval from integer counts. Assign Level 3 only
>    when every D17.3 conjunct passes; otherwise preserve Level 2 and enumerate
>    blockers. Accepting the golden is T1.
> 4. Run Phase 0 exit: M13–M16 tests, both stable-profile SLOs, all Phase -1 tests,
>    `just ci`, and `just gates`. Freeze the clean review base before suite
>    qualification; adversarial passes run only after the proposed suite exists.
> 5. Author Phase 1 work orders from `template.md`. Every Phase 1 law/class test has
>    positive, negative, malformed/adversarial, basis/provenance, and deterministic
>    replay coverage where applicable. Implement ADR-0020's two lanes and complete
>    HAQP-1: exact traceability, at least 64 semantic mutants with 100% applicable
>    kill rate, disposable gate canaries, 100,000 deterministic cases and a
>    30-minute sanitizer-enabled fuzz campaign for each of five critical families,
>    independent oracles, exhaustive registered crash boundaries, and two blinded
>    adversarial passes using distinct reviewer identities and isolated session
>    state. Pass 1 attacks vacuity, oracle independence, negative cases, crash
>    completeness, and corpus leakage. Pass 2 starts from the original spec and
>    attempts to falsify conclusions without seeing Pass 1's record. Record all
>    gaps; do not weaken existing ignored tests.
> 6. Stop after proposed suite and review packet are complete. Notify user with exact
>    commands, counts, artifacts, findings, and residual risks. Only explicit user
>    ratification changes suite status and authorizes Phase 1 execution.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-e8b62588e41ab3ac2eeb -->
