<!-- source-block:source-158846c211afda77171e -->
> ## Amendments
> 
> AM-17.1 (user-ratified 2026-07-20): require ADR-0020 HAQP-1 before the proposed
> Phase 1 suite becomes eligible for ratification. This strengthens the existing
> packet gate without adding or renaming tests; predicted counts remain unchanged.
> 
> AM-17.2 (user-ratified 2026-07-20): resolve the pre-authorization qualification
> cycle with a Phase-0-only executable reference harness, synthetic subjects, and
> five sanitizer fuzz targets. These qualify shared test contracts, not production
> Phase 1 code; all seven Phase 1 gates and the conditional migration gate remain
> deferred. Use five critical mutation families with thirteen predeclared semantic
> mutants each, sixteen disposable canaries, and two concurrent blind reviewers:
> DeepSeek V4 Pro plus a context-free Codex agent. A first clean HAQP run exceeding
> eight hours is diagnostic and ineligible; optimize and rerun. A second clean
> overrun requires a superseding ADR. No threshold is reduced.
> 
> AM-17.4 (user-ratified 2026-08-08, ADR-0021): stage HAQP-1 around Phase 1
> authorization. M17.5's exit criterion becomes **HAQP-1a** — everything ADR-0020
> requires except §3's mutant clauses, which defer to **HAQP-1b** at M24.
> 
> Rationale (M17.5 finding F-28): §3 requires 64 semantic mutants at a 100% kill
> rate, and all 35 distinct killing tests backing the packet's 65 mutants were
> unrunnable — 27 did not exist and 8 are `#[ignore]`d under AM-17.2. Lifting the
> quarantine needs Phase 1 authorization, which M17.6 grants AFTER M17.5. ADR-0020
> §3 assumed the suite it mutates already exists; for Phase 1 it does not.
> 
> No threshold is reduced: every §3 clause survives verbatim into 1b, only its
> evaluation point moves. §3's gate-canary clause stays in 1a, because canaries
> run against the packet's own gates rather than against Phase 1 tests. The packet
> records `qualification_stage`, and the verifier rejects a 1a packet claiming
> mutant kills as well as a 1b packet without them.
> 
> Also reconciles M17.8's predicted counts, which were authored before the suite
> grew: it predicted 237 active / 21 backlog; the meter reads 356 active / 43
> backlog (Phase 1 deferred rose to 27 as M18–M23's 20 milestone tests were
> written and quarantined). The prediction is corrected rather than the meter.
> 
> AM-17.6 (user-ratified 2026-08-16): the qualification metadata child may lift
> EXACTLY ONE `#[ignore]` — the one on
> `phase1_suite_packet_is_complete_and_unratified` in
> `conformance/tests/phase0.rs` — and change nothing else in that file.
> 
> Rationale: that gate is M17.5's stated exit criterion and it asserts the packet
> is COMPLETE, so it cannot be live before the flip that completes the packet.
> Every other placement fails. Un-ignoring at the fixed base commits a red tree
> and makes the base look broken to anyone who checks it out. Un-ignoring after
> the flip moves HEAD, so `provenance.evidence_parent == HEAD^` no longer holds
> and the qualified gate refuses. The metadata child is the only position left.
> 
> Discovered by running M17.5's exit command as written: it reports
> `0 tests run: 0 passed, 18 skipped`, not the `1 passed` the work order predicts.
> The trap was an ordering constraint nobody had written down, in the same family
> as F-28 and the first ADR-0021 deadlock — no piece is defective, and the
> sequence they compose into is impossible.
> 
> No threshold is reduced and the guarantee is not widened to the file.
> `qualification_metadata_path` still refuses `conformance/tests/phase0.rs`;
> `verify_gate_unignore_only` inspects the DIFF and requires one removed line, no
> added lines, and that the removed line is that exact attribute. Gate logic
> therefore still cannot change in the child, which is what `verify_provenance`
> exists to prevent. Four canaries pin it, including one asserting the pinned
> attribute string still matches the tree — otherwise the check passes vacuously
> against a file it no longer describes.
> 
> AM-17.7 (user-ratified 2026-08-26): ADR-0020 §5's "exhaustive registered crash
> boundaries" is scoped, for HAQP-1a, to the eight `ilrp/*` protocol boundaries.
> Every other durable transition in the runtime is deferred to M17.9. The scope is
> declared in `packet.crash_boundary_scope` rather than left implicit.
> 
> Rationale: §5 requires exhaustiveness without saying over what, and M17.5 A05
> measured the honest answer. The registry covers **8 of the runtime's 38 durable
> transitions**. `liminal-graph/src/store/mod.rs` documents its own commit path as
> "Durable boundary: the record is fsynced before the commit returns", so every
> `txn.commit()` is one — 22 in `liminal-daemon/src/runner.rs` alone — and none
> carries a crash boundary. Registering them requires deciding which fsynced
> transitions across the whole runtime are *registrable* boundaries, which is
> runtime design work; doing it inside a qualification campaign would either block
> 1a on Phase 1 or settle the question by picking whichever definition passes.
> ADR-0020 §3 forbids improvising qualification semantics, so the claim is bounded
> and disclosed instead of quietly widened.
> 
> A prose scope note would rot the first time somebody added a commit site, which
> is the same defect A05 found in the unscoped claim. `verify_crash_boundary_scope`
> binds it to tracked source: every durable transition must sit inside a declared
> in-scope subsystem or a declared deferred surface, with site counts matching
> `git ls-files` exactly. A new `txn.commit()` anywhere turns the packet red until
> it is registered or disclosed. Canary C33 pins the realistic failure — a surface
> understated by one site.
> 
> Note for M17.9: A05's original survey claimed the daemon held 11 unregistered
> crash-injection sites. It holds **zero** — `crash.rs` is the injector
> implementation and `main.rs`'s `Fire` subcommand resolves its point from
> `CrashPoint::all()`, so it is closed over the registry by construction. What
> M17.9 inherits is the larger question the survey missed: which of the ~38
> durable transitions are registrable boundaries.
> 
> AM-17.8 (user-ratified 2026-09-04): a registrable crash boundary is a point at
> which a crash leaves state that recovery must reconcile. This is the criterion
> AM-17.7 lacked. Under it ILRP's eight protocol steps are the boundary set, and
> the runtime's remaining fsynced transitions — single checksummed appends whose
> torn tail is truncated on recovery — carry no reconciliation obligation. The
> evidence already existed: `prop_torn_tail_truncates_cleanly`
> (`crates/liminal-graph/tests/store.rs`). A05 closes by definition plus citation,
> not by registering thirty boundaries whose only test would be that an atomic
> append is atomic. M17.9 no longer inherits it.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-158846c211afda77171e -->

<a id="source-02d3ed8d45600c18c15c"></a>

Classification: `open-gap`. Original lines 262–277; text SHA-256: `aeb62a5500fc9f0c121c223d57ec5f4b749a113758cb67ef72839d9d77e6452a`.

<!-- source-block:source-02d3ed8d45600c18c15c -->
> ## Discovered gaps
> 
> DG17.1 (M17.1): ADR-0015 selects the constrained Markdown-compatible frontend
> but does not bind a concrete parser package. The spike pins
> `tree-sitter-md 0.5.3` with `tree-sitter 0.26.3` because it exposes block and
> inline CSTs plus edited-tree incremental reparsing. Upstream explicitly warns
> that its Markdown output retains known inaccuracies, and it has no lossless
> native serializer; M17 therefore treats it as measurement evidence only and
> keeps the declaration at Level 2. No production `liminal-cst` API depends on it.
> 
> DG17.2 (M17.4): ADR-0020 requires five fuzz campaigns before Phase 1 suite
> ratification, while the implementation-plan defer list originally created
> `fuzz/` only after the production `liminal-cst` crate landed. AM-17.2 permits
> only conformance reference targets before authorization and preserves the
> production-parser prohibition.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-02d3ed8d45600c18c15c -->

<!-- source-block:source-402094beec51a476885d -->
> ## Exit criteria
> 
> - Real-CST report is reproducible, statistically explicit, and honestly graded.
> - Every Phase 0 and retained Phase -1 gate is green; `just ci` and `just gates` pass.
> - Two independent adversarial passes have zero unresolved verified findings.
> - HAQP-1 qualification satisfies every ADR-0020 threshold from one fixed clean
>   review base and the final full rerun.
> - Proposed Phase 1 work orders and test coverage matrix are complete.
> - User is notified; Phase 1 suite remains unratified until explicit acceptance.

<!-- source-block:source-11416aa9c54e8a53ae6f -->
> ## Scope
> 
> Build the first production L0 path: a `ropey 1.6.1` raw-UTF-8 view over bytes from
> one already-selected Holder and a Liminal-owned, `rowan 0.16.1` bounded,
> lossless, error-tolerant CST for the constrained Markdown-compatible frontend.
> This activates only `docs/implementation-plan.md` §4 item 3 at its Phase 1 gate;
> it does not add CLI subcommands, HIR/graph lowering, formatting, HTML, macros,
> transforms, compiled Jurisdiction, sync, an editor, or a persistent daemon.
>

<!-- source-block:source-6e8f33f1e4c967b3ab9f -->
> ## Pre-made decisions
> 
> - **D18.1 —** the source buffer is `ropey 1.6.1`; it is a physical UTF-8 view of
>   bytes supplied by an already-resolved Holder, never a competing Holder or
>   semantic authority.
> - **D18.2 —** production CST storage is `rowan 0.16.1`, wrapped entirely by
>   Liminal-owned types; no rowan type crosses a serialized or public interchange
>   boundary.
> - **D18.3 —** `MAX_SOURCE_BYTES = u32::MAX as u64`, matching rowan `TextSize`;
>   `MAX_NESTING = 256`; `MAX_ERRORS = 1024`. Exceeding a bound returns a typed
>   result and never panics or drops source text.
> - **D18.4 —** L0 accepts well-formed UTF-8 only. Invalid UTF-8 is a Holder-load
>   error with exact byte coordinates; malformed *syntax* remains valid input and
>   is retained inside `ERROR` nodes.
> - **D18.5 —** every input byte belongs to exactly one rowan token in source order.
>   Error recovery wraps existing tokens; it never synthesizes, deletes, or rewrites
>   token text. Concatenating all tokens therefore reproduces the UTF-8 input bytes.
> - **D18.6 —** the supported frontend is exactly ADR-0015 AM-15.1's constrained
>   Markdown-compatible path: ATX headings, paragraphs, ordered and unordered
>   lists, block quotes, fenced code, emphasis, strong text, inline code, links,
>   and explicit IDs. Unknown extensions, raw HTML, unsupported constructs, and
>   malformed regions are lossless `OPAQUE`/`ERROR` content, not rejected input.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-6e8f33f1e4c967b3ab9f -->

<a id="source-c862a9cfc607f7936966"></a>

Classification: `mixed-clause`. Original lines 57–232; text SHA-256: `8d736d2bced51cf2c1c324f06073233c4863d9d2d3e67e1e62bd3f94471315b7`.

<!-- source-block:source-c862a9cfc607f7936966 -->
> ## Data schemas
> 
> In `liminal-source`:
> 
> ```rust
> pub const MAX_SOURCE_BYTES: u64 = u32::MAX as u64;
> 
> #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
> #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
> pub struct SourceBasis {
>     pub source: SourceId,
>     pub content_hash: ContentHash,
> }
> 
> #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
> pub struct Utf8HolderView {
>     pub basis: SourceBasis,
>     text: ropey::Rope,
> }
> 
> #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, thiserror::Error)]
> pub enum SourceLoadError {
>     #[error("source exceeds rowan TextSize: {actual} > {maximum}")]
>     TooLarge { actual: u64, maximum: u64 },
>     #[error("source hash mismatch: expected {expected}, got {actual}")]
>     HashMismatch { expected: ContentHash, actual: ContentHash },
>     #[error("source is not UTF-8 at byte {valid_up_to}")]
>     InvalidUtf8 { valid_up_to: u64, error_len: Option<u64> },
> }
> 
> #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, thiserror::Error)]
> pub enum SourceSliceError {
>     #[error("byte slice {start}..{end} exceeds source length {len}")]
>     OutOfBounds { start: usize, end: usize, len: usize },
>     #[error("byte offset {offset} is not a UTF-8 boundary")]
>     NotCharBoundary { offset: usize },
> }
> 
> impl Utf8HolderView {
>     pub fn from_bytes(
>         basis: SourceBasis,
>         bytes: &[u8],
>     ) -> Result<Self, SourceLoadError>;
>     pub fn basis(&self) -> &SourceBasis;
>     pub fn len_bytes(&self) -> usize;
>     pub fn byte_slice(
>         &self,
>         range: std::ops::Range<usize>,
>     ) -> Result<ropey::RopeSlice<'_>, SourceSliceError>;
>     pub fn to_string(&self) -> String;
> }
> ```
> 
> `Utf8HolderView::from_bytes(basis, bytes)` verifies the byte length, verifies
> `ContentHash::of(bytes) == basis.content_hash`, validates UTF-8, and constructs
> the rope. The view exposes `len_bytes`, `byte_slice`, `to_string`, and `basis`; it
> exposes no mutation API.
> 
> In `liminal-cst`:
> 
> ```rust
> pub const MAX_NESTING: u16 = 256;
> pub const MAX_ERRORS: usize = 1024;
> 
> #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash)]
> pub enum LiminalLanguage {}
> 
> #[repr(u16)]
> #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash)]
> pub enum SyntaxKind {
>     Root, Heading, Paragraph, OrderedList, UnorderedList, ListItem, BlockQuote,
>     Fence, Inline, Reference, ExplicitId, Text, Whitespace, Comment, Delimiter,
>     Newline, Opaque, Error,
> }
> 
> #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
> pub struct ParseError {
>     pub code: ParseErrorCode,
>     pub range: SourceRange,
> }
> 
> #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
> pub enum ParseErrorCode {
>     NestingLimit, ErrorLimit, UnclosedDelimiter, InvalidAttribute,
>     InvalidReference, UnsupportedConstruct,
> }
> 
> #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
> pub struct Parse {
>     green: rowan::GreenNode,
>     errors: Vec<ParseError>,
>     basis: SourceBasis,
> }
> 
> pub type SyntaxNode = rowan::SyntaxNode<LiminalLanguage>;
> 
> pub fn parse(source: &Utf8HolderView) -> Parse;
> 
> impl Parse {
>     pub fn syntax(&self) -> SyntaxNode;
>     pub fn errors(&self) -> &[ParseError];
>     pub fn basis(&self) -> &SourceBasis;
>     pub fn emit_lossless(&self) -> String;
> }
> ```
> 
> `LiminalLanguage` implements `rowan::Language<Kind = SyntaxKind>` with checked
> raw-kind conversion. `Parse::syntax()` returns the typed root; `errors()` is in
> `(range.start, range.end, code)` order; `emit_lossless()` concatenates source-order
> token text and returns `String`. Every public item, field, method, enum variant,
> alias, and constant shown above receives a doc comment citing v4 §5.3, §9, or
> §22 as applicable; these citations are part of the schema.
> 
> The constrained Markdown-compatible block grammar is:
> 
> ```ebnf
> document  = [ bom ], { blank | heading | ordered_list | unordered_list
>           | block_quote | fence | opaque_extension | opaque_html | paragraph } ;
> bom       = U+FEFF ;
> blank     = spacing, newline ;
> heading   = hashes, " ", inline, [ explicit_id ], line_end ;
> hashes    = "#" | "##" | "###" | "####" | "#####" | "######" ;
> ordered_list = ordered_item, { ordered_item } ;
> ordered_item = ordinal, ". ", inline, [ explicit_id ], line_end ;
> ordinal   = DIGIT, { DIGIT } ;
> unordered_list = unordered_item, { unordered_item } ;
> unordered_item = ( "- " | "+ " | "* " ), inline, [ explicit_id ], line_end ;
> block_quote = quote_line, { quote_line } ;
> quote_line = ">", [ " " ], inline, [ explicit_id ], line_end ;
> fence     = "```", { codepoint - newline }, newline,
>             { codepoint }, fence_close ;
> fence_close = line_start, "```", spacing, line_end ;
> paragraph = paragraph_line, { paragraph_line } ;
> paragraph_line = inline, [ explicit_id ], line_end ;
> explicit_id = spacing, "{#", ident, "}" ;
> opaque_extension = extension_open, { extension_body_line }, [ extension_close ] ;
> extension_open = ":::", { codepoint - newline }, line_end ;
> extension_body_line = ? line not matching extension_close ?,
>                       { codepoint - newline }, line_end ;
> extension_close = ":::", spacing, line_end ;
> opaque_html = spacing, "<", { codepoint - newline }, line_end ;
> inline    = inline_atom, { inline_atom } ;
> inline_atom = code_span | strong | emphasis | reference | text_char ;
> code_span = "`", { codepoint - "`" - newline }, "`" ;
> emphasis  = "*", { code_span | reference | plain_char }, "*" ;
> strong    = "**", { code_span | reference | plain_char }, "**" ;
> reference = "[", { code_span | strong | emphasis | reference_char }, "](",
>             destination, ")" ;
> destination = { codepoint - ")" - control - whitespace } ;
> text_char = codepoint - "`" - "*" - "[" - newline ;
> plain_char = codepoint - "`" - "*" - "[" - newline ;
> reference_char = codepoint - "]" - newline ;
> ident     = ( ALPHA | "_" ), { ALPHA | DIGIT | "_" | "." | ":" | "-" } ;
> spacing   = { " " | "\t" } ;
> newline   = "\n" | "\r\n" ;
> line_end  = newline | eof ;
> ```
> 
> `line_start` means byte zero or the byte after `newline`. A block marker is
> recognized only at `line_start`; otherwise its bytes are paragraph text.
> An `ordinal` is one through nine ASCII digits. An `explicit_id` is recognized
> only as the final non-newline suffix of a heading, list item, quote line, or
> paragraph line; an unmatched `{#` remains `Error` text. `paragraph` ends before
> blank, heading, either list, block quote, fence, opaque-extension, or opaque-HTML
> start. Inline parsing is left-to-right with precedence code span, strong,
> emphasis, reference, then text; delimiters do not cross a newline. An unmatched
> inline delimiter is
> plain `Text`. A line whose first nonspacing byte is `<` is one `Opaque` HTML line.
> An extension opening at line start with `:::` is one `Opaque` region through the
> first later line containing only `:::` plus horizontal spacing, inclusive, or
> through EOF when no close exists. An unclosed fence is one `Error` node through
> EOF with the opening delimiter retained. Any other unsupported block marker is
> one `Opaque` line; a malformed supported construct is one `Error` region through
> its line end.
> Nesting and diagnostic saturation follow D18.3 and Algorithm 4 exactly.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-c862a9cfc607f7936966 -->

<a id="source-693c02e1843ebdf5f6e3"></a>

Classification: `mixed-clause`. Original lines 233–254; text SHA-256: `337ca91d9fc9ff77f278f5b0ef2ce51dfe336a089819efe613d7c7210a6e5c6e`.

<!-- source-block:source-693c02e1843ebdf5f6e3 -->
> ## Algorithms
> 
> 1. `Utf8HolderView::from_bytes` computes `actual_len`; reject above
>    `MAX_SOURCE_BYTES`; compute and compare the content hash; run
>    `std::str::from_utf8`; then build `Rope::from_str`. Freeze these checks in the
>    existing malformed-source gate's oversized/hash/invalid-UTF-8 cases.
> 2. Coarse-scan rope chunks without flattening the source. Record byte boundaries
>    for headings, paragraphs, both list kinds, block quotes, fences, explicit IDs,
>    and opaque regions; every boundary is a UTF-8 boundary and a valid
>    `SourceRange`.
> 3. Feed token text to one `GreenNodeBuilder` in source order. Maintain an explicit
>    stack capped at `MAX_NESTING`; on overflow, emit one `NestingLimit` error and
>    retain the affected input as `Opaque` tokens until the matching boundary.
> 4. Recover locally from malformed syntax by wrapping the original tokens in an
>    `Error` node. Once `MAX_ERRORS` is reached, append one `ErrorLimit` diagnostic
>    and retain the remaining region as one `Opaque` node. No recovery path changes
>    token text.
> 5. Implement `emit_lossless` as the ordered concatenation of every token under the
>    root. The existing gate catches panics and asserts output bytes equal input for
>    every supported AM-15.1 construct, opaque extension and HTML input, boundary,
>    truncated, malformed, hostile, nesting-limit, and error-limit UTF-8 fixtures.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-693c02e1843ebdf5f6e3 -->

<a id="source-3e4f29950349e3065f5c"></a>

Classification: `mixed-clause`. Original lines 42–93; text SHA-256: `30fa4443043dc016a2cd82c0ee5d6e28b1e2917ead1b2bdc6d190320da8005e1`.

<!-- source-block:source-3e4f29950349e3065f5c -->
> ## Pre-made decisions
> 
> - **D19.0 (AM-17.3) —** the canonical round-trip law is instantiated for BOTH
>   surfaces via `Formatter::emit_in_dialect`: `CompactOrExplicitV1` round-trips
>   compact→compact, `ExplicitV1` round-trips explicit→explicit. `emit` stays the
>   canonical (explicit) projection and is not changed. A document with no compact
>   spelling falls back to explicit rather than emitting a lossy approximation.
> 
> - **D19.1 —** annotations and source maps are ephemeral views over one exact
>   `SourceBasis`; raw offsets are never persisted without its content hash and
>   never claim cross-revision identity.
> - **D19.2 —** `SyntaxForm` is exactly v4 §17's literal, node construction,
>   relation construction, attribute assignment, ordered block, reference,
>   expression, and macro invocation. Compact syntax is sugar that lowers to these
>   forms; macro invocation is represented but not executed in M19.
> - **D19.3 —** HIR preserves authorial spelling, source ranges, symbolic defaults,
>   unresolved references, and provenance. Resolution materializes defaults and
>   local references into a separate derived graph; it never mutates HIR.
> - **D19.4 —** external-file source retains Jurisdiction. The L2 graph is marked
>   derived, carries the exact Workspace Basis and source provenance, and is never
>   selected as a governing Holder.
> - **D19.5 —** stable debug JSON v1 is the only Phase 1 graph interchange. It is
>   inspectable and deterministic but explicitly non-final and non-performance-
>   critical; unknown or missing fields fail closed.
> - **D19.6 —** canonical semantic IDs use UUIDv5 with `Uuid::NAMESPACE_URL` over
>   `b"liminal:phase1:derived:v1\0" || subject_tag || 0x00 || holder_source_uuid ||
>   0x00 || form_kebab || 0x00 || path_len_be_u32 || child_index_be_u32*`.
>   `subject_tag` is exactly `b"node"`, `b"relation:explicit"`,
>   `b"relation:contains"`, or `b"relation:reference"`; the path is the preorder
>   root/child-index path. Source offsets and content hash do not enter the ID. A
>   unique explicit ID instead uses UUIDv5 over
>   `b"liminal:phase1:explicit:v1\0" || holder_source_uuid || 0x00 || id_utf8`.
>   The resulting continuity is Anchored for the derived recipe and Explicit for
>   the accepted explicit recipe, never Managed.
>   The synthetic document Node uses `path_len = 0`. Every authored Node,
>   explicit Relation, and reference Relation uses its HIR item's preorder
>   root/child-index path. A generated containment Relation uses its child HIR
>   item's path; its distinct `relation:contains` tag prevents collision with that
>   child's Node or reference Relation.
> - **D19.7 —** `Phase1Document::PartialEq` compares the normalized semantic
>   Node/Relation projection and a law-normalized Workspace Basis. It requires the
>   same Holder key, transaction, perspective, component keys, and non-Holder
>   components. At the selected Holder it requires the same component variant and
>   address metadata but excludes `FileContent.hash` or
>   `BufferGeneration.content_hash`; diagnostics, provenance coordinates, and
>   source-map byte ranges are also excluded. Those coordinates may change when
>   canonical spelling changes without semantic loss; production cache equality
>   continues to use full `WorkspaceBasis::Eq`.
> - **D19.8 —** the only Phase 1 semantic defaults are empty attributes, an empty
>   fence `info` string, and empty macro arguments. Canonical explicit emission
>   writes all three; no domain/schema default is invented before its owning phase.
>

> ## Data schemas
> 
> In `liminal-hir`:
> 
> ```rust

>

>

>

>     pub range: SourceRange,

>     pub attributes: BTreeMap<String, HirValue>,
>     pub children: Vec<HirId>,
> }
> 
> #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]

> pub struct HirDocument {

>     pub roots: Vec<HirId>,
>     pub items: Vec<HirItem>,
>     pub source_map: SourceMap,
> }
> 
> #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Serialize, Deserialize)]
> #[serde(rename_all = "kebab-case")]
> pub enum HirDiagnosticCode {
>     UnknownForm,
>     IntegerOverflow,
>     MalformedSyntax,
>     AttributeWithoutOwner,
> }
> 
> #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
> #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
> pub struct HirDiagnostic {

>     pub range: SourceRange,
>     pub message: String,
> }
> 
> #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
> pub struct LoweredHir {

>     pub diagnostics: Vec<HirDiagnostic>,
> }
> 
> #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, thiserror::Error)]
> pub enum HirError {
>     #[error("invalid source map: {0}")]
>     InvalidSourceMap(String),
>     #[error("dangling HIR id {0:?}")]
>     Dangling(HirId),

> 
> pub fn validate_source_map(
>     map: &SourceMap,
>     source_len: u64,

> pub fn lower(

> ```
> 
> `items` is dense and sorted by `HirId`; every `roots`, `children`, and resolved
> `HirReference` target exists; `Unresolved` retains exact symbolic spelling;
> annotations are sorted by `(range.start, range.end, kind, hir)` and remain within
> the exact source length. Diagnostics are nonfatal and sorted by
> `(range.start, range.end, code, message)`; `HirError` is reserved for violated
> source-map and HIR structural invariants.
> 
> In `liminal-cir`:
> 
> ```rust
> #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
> #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
> pub struct SourceProvenance {
>     pub source: SourceId,
>     pub content_hash: ContentHash,
>     pub range: SourceRange,
>     pub identity_grade: IdentityGrade,
> }
> 
> #[derive(
>     Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Serialize, Deserialize,
> )]
> #[serde(rename_all = "kebab-case")]
> pub enum ProvenanceSubject {
>     Node(NodeId),
>     Relation(RelationId),
> }
> 
> #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
> pub struct DerivedGraph {
>     pub basis: WorkspaceBasis,
>     pub nodes: Vec<Node>,
>     pub relations: Vec<Relation>,
>     pub provenance: BTreeMap<ProvenanceSubject, SourceProvenance>,
> }
> 
> #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord)]
> pub enum ResolveDiagnosticCode {
>     UnresolvedReference,
>     DuplicateExplicitId,
> }
> 
> #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
> pub struct ResolveDiagnostic {
>     pub code: ResolveDiagnosticCode,
>     pub subject: Option<HirId>,
>     pub message: String,
> }
> 
> #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
> pub struct ResolvedGraph {
>     pub graph: DerivedGraph,
>     pub diagnostics: Vec<ResolveDiagnostic>,
> }
> 
> #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
> #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
> pub struct DerivedPayloadV1 {
>     pub schema_version: u32,
>     pub kind: HirItemKind,
>     pub attributes: BTreeMap<String, HirValue>,
> }
> 
> #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
> #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
> pub struct DebugProvenanceV1 {
>     pub subject: ProvenanceSubject,
>     pub source: SourceId,
>     pub content_hash: ContentHash,
>     pub range: SourceRange,
>     pub identity_grade: IdentityGrade,
> }
> 
> #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
> #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
> pub struct DebugGraphV1 {
>     pub schema_version: u32,
>     pub basis: WorkspaceBasis,
>     pub holder: JurisdictionKey,
>     pub source: SourceBasis,
>     pub nodes: Vec<Node>,
>     pub relations: Vec<Relation>,
>     pub provenance: Vec<DebugProvenanceV1>,
> }
> 
> #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, thiserror::Error)]
> pub enum ResolveError {
>     #[error("dangling relation endpoint")]
>     DanglingRelation,
>     #[error("Basis does not select compatible file/buffer Holder {0}")]
>     BasisMismatch(JurisdictionKey),
>     #[error("phase-1 kind collision at {id:?}: {first} vs {second}")]
>     KindCollision { id: KindId, first: String, second: String },
>     #[error("canonical payload serialization failed: {0}")]
>     Payload(String),
> }
> 
> #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, thiserror::Error)]
> pub enum DebugJsonError {
>     #[error("malformed JSON: {0}")]
>     Syntax(String),
>     #[error("JSON shape mismatch at {path}")]
>     Shape { path: String },
>     #[error("unsupported schema version {0}")]
>     Version(u32),
>     #[error("invalid debug graph: {0}")]
>     Invalid(String),
> }
> 
> pub fn resolve(
>     hir: &HirDocument,
>     basis: &WorkspaceBasis,
> ) -> Result<ResolvedGraph, ResolveError>;
> pub fn basis_for_source(
>     base: &WorkspaceBasis,
>     holder: &JurisdictionKey,
>     hash: ContentHash,
> ) -> Result<WorkspaceBasis, ResolveError>;
> pub fn to_debug_v1(
>     graph: &DerivedGraph,
>     holder: JurisdictionKey,
>     source: SourceBasis,
> ) -> DebugGraphV1;
> pub fn serialize_debug_v1(value: &DebugGraphV1) -> Result<Vec<u8>, DebugJsonError>;
> pub fn deserialize_debug_v1(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<DebugGraphV1, DebugJsonError>;
> ```
> 
> JSON bytes are UTF-8, one pretty-printed object, two-space indentation, LF only,
> and one trailing LF. Struct field order above is canonical; every map is a
> `BTreeMap`; `nodes`, `relations`, and `provenance` sort by subject ID;
> `schema_version` must equal `1`; duplicate IDs, dangling endpoints, unknown or
> missing fields, non-derived nodes, missing Node/Relation provenance, and
> Basis/source-hash mismatch are errors. Specifically, `holder` must select a
> `FileContent.hash` or present `BufferGeneration.content_hash` equal to
> `source.content_hash` in `basis`. Strict decoding deserializes into
> `DebugGraphV1`, serializes that value to a canonical `serde_json::Value`, then
> recursively requires identical object-key sets, array lengths, and JSON kinds
> between input and canonical value. The first difference returns
> `DebugJsonError::Shape { path }`; embedded existing types therefore reject
> unknown or missing fields too.
> 
> In `liminal-format`:
> 
> ```rust
> #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
> pub enum Phase1Diagnostic {
>     Hir(HirDiagnostic),
>     Resolve(ResolveDiagnostic),
> }
> 
> #[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
> pub enum Phase1FormatError {
>     #[error(transparent)]
>     Source(#[from] SourceLoadError),
>     #[error(transparent)]
>     Hir(#[from] HirError),
>     #[error(transparent)]
>     Resolve(#[from] ResolveError),
>     #[error("canonical emission failed: {0}")]
>     Emit(String),
> }
> 
> #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
> pub struct Phase1Document {
>     pub holder: JurisdictionKey,
>     pub hir: HirDocument,
>     pub graph: DerivedGraph,
>     pub diagnostics: Vec<Phase1Diagnostic>,
> }
> 
> #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
> pub struct MarkdownFormatter {
>     source: SourceId,
>     holder: JurisdictionKey,
>     basis: WorkspaceBasis,
>     dialect: SourceDialect,
> }
> 
> impl MarkdownFormatter {
>     pub fn new(
>         source: SourceId,
>         holder: JurisdictionKey,
>         basis: WorkspaceBasis,
>         dialect: SourceDialect,
>     ) -> Self;
> }
> ```
> 
> `Phase1Document`'s explicit
> `PartialEq` implementation follows D19.7 by comparing the Workspace Basis and a
> semantic projection of sorted Nodes/Relations; source hashes, ranges,
> diagnostics, and provenance coordinates are excluded. `MarkdownFormatter`
> implements the existing
> `Formatter<Doc = Phase1Document, Error = Phase1FormatError>` seam for both the
> constrained compact frontend and the §17 explicit debug form.
> `CompactOrExplicitV1` selects explicit parsing only when byte zero begins with
> the exact `#!liminal-explicit-v1` marker and otherwise lowers M18 typed nodes as
> compact input. `ExplicitV1` requires that marker; absence produces
> `MalformedSyntax`. Explicit parsing reparses the exact bytes from
> `Parse::emit_lossless` with the grammar below, retaining its tokens and recovery
> ranges in the same source map. Canonical `emit` always writes the marker followed
> by ExplicitV1, so the same formatter instance reparses its own output without
> content-grammar guessing. `parse(source)` constructs
> `SourceBasis { source: self.source,
> content_hash: ContentHash::of(source.as_bytes()) }`, loads `Utf8HolderView`, runs
> M18 `parse`, calls `lower` with `self.dialect`, derives the exact transient Basis
> with `basis_for_source(&self.basis, &self.holder, content_hash)`, and resolves
> only against that Basis. `basis_for_source` clones `base` and replaces only the
> selected `FileContent.hash` or `BufferGeneration.content_hash`; a missing key or
> any other component variant returns `BasisMismatch`. The transient Basis governs
> only this derived parse and never mutates or claims acceptance by the Holder.
> The formatter appends HIR diagnostics in their defined source
> order, followed by resolve
> diagnostics sorted by `(subject, code, message)`; formatting errors remain fatal
> and never appear in that vector.
> 
> The explicit v4 §17 grammar is:
> 
> ```ebnf
> document   = marker, spacing, { form, spacing } ;
> marker     = "#!liminal-explicit-v1", ( "\n" | "\r\n" ) ;
> form       = literal | node | relation | attribute | ordered
>            | reference | expression | macro ;
> literal    = "literal", space1, string, ";" ;
> node       = "node", space1, ident, [ attributes ], block ;
> relation   = "relation", space1, reference_value, spacing, "-[", ident,
>              "]->", spacing, reference_value, [ attributes ], ";" ;
> attribute  = "attribute", space1, ident, spacing, "=", spacing, value, ";" ;
> ordered    = "ordered", spacing, block ;
> reference  = "reference", space1, reference_value, ";" ;
> expression = "expression", space1, string, ";" ;
> macro      = "macro", space1, ident, "(", [ values ], ")", ";" ;
> block      = "{", spacing, { form, spacing }, "}" ;
> attributes = "(", [ assignment, { ",", spacing, assignment } ], ")" ;
> assignment = ident, spacing, "=", spacing, value ;
> values     = value, { ",", spacing, value } ;
> value      = string | integer | "true" | "false" | "null" | reference_value ;
> reference_value = "@", ident ;
> ident      = (ALPHA | "_"), { ALPHA | DIGIT | "_" | "." | ":" | "-" } ;
> string     = JSON_STRING ;
> integer    = [ "-" ], DIGIT, { DIGIT } ;
> spacing    = { " " | "\t" | "\r" | "\n" | comment } ;
> space1     = ( " " | "\t" | "\r" | "\n" ), spacing ;
> comment    = "//", { codepoint - "\r" - "\n" }, [ "\r" ], [ "\n" ] ;
> ```
> 
> Keywords are lowercase ASCII and reserved; identifiers are case-sensitive;
> strings use JSON escapes and Unicode scalar values; integer overflow is a typed
> HIR diagnostic. Nesting uses M18's `MAX_NESTING`. Recovery consumes through the
> next `;` at current brace depth or the current block's `}`, whichever comes first,
> while retaining every consumed CST token under the originating error annotation.
> The productions map field-for-field: `literal` supplies `Literal.value`; `node`
> supplies `NodeConstruction.name`, its parenthesized assignments supply
> `attributes`, and its block supplies ordered `children`; `relation` supplies
> `RelationConstruction.source`, `.kind`, and `.target` plus its parenthesized
> `attributes`; `attribute` supplies `AttributeAssignment.name` and `.value`, with
> `owner` set to the nearest enclosing Node or Relation's `HirId` and a top-level
> assignment retained with `owner = None` plus `AttributeWithoutOwner`; `ordered`
> supplies ordered `children`;
> `reference` supplies `Reference.target`; `expression` supplies
> `Expression.source`; and `macro` supplies `MacroInvocation.name` and ordered
> `.arguments`. Only Node and Relation items may have nonempty `attributes`; only
> Node and OrderedBlock items may have nonempty `children`. `SyntaxForm` is the
> one-to-one tag obtained from `HirItemKind`, never independently stored.
> 
> Compact lowering maps the M18 document's block children to HIR roots exactly:
> 
> | M18 CST | HIR projection |
> |---|---|
> | ATX heading | `NodeConstruction { name: "heading" }`; integer `level`; inline children |
> | paragraph | `NodeConstruction { name: "paragraph" }`; inline children |
> | ordered/unordered list | `NodeConstruction` named `ordered-list`/`unordered-list`; ordered `list-item` children; ordered items carry integer `ordinal` |
> | block quote | `NodeConstruction { name: "block-quote" }`; one `paragraph` child per quote line |
> | fenced code | `NodeConstruction { name: "code-block" }`; string `info`; one exact-body `Literal` child |
> | plain text | `Literal { value }`, coalescing adjacent text tokens |
> | emphasis/strong/inline code | `NodeConstruction` named `emphasis`/`strong`/`inline-code`; inline children, with inline-code bytes in one `Literal` |
> | link | `NodeConstruction { name: "link" }`; string `destination`; label inline children |
> | explicit ID | string `id` attribute on its enclosing block |
> | `Opaque` | `NodeConstruction { name: "opaque" }`; string `class` equal to `extension`, `html`, or `unsupported`; one exact-byte `Literal` |
> | `Error` | `NodeConstruction { name: "error" }`; one exact-byte `Literal` plus `MalformedSyntax` diagnostic |
> 
> Blank lines and nonsemantic delimiters create annotations but no HIR item. All
> table attributes occupy the owning item's `attributes` map. Parenthesized
> explicit attributes populate `attributes`; an
> `AttributeAssignment` contributes to its owner's effective attributes during
> resolution without mutating HIR. On a repeated key, the first source-order value
> wins and the later assignment produces `MalformedSyntax`.
> 
> The HIR-to-graph projection is field-exact:
> 
> 1. Create one synthetic document `Node` with declared kind name `document`, empty
>    attributes, and payload `DerivedPayloadV1 { schema_version: 1, kind:
>    HirItemKind::NodeConstruction { name: "document" }, attributes: BTreeMap::new()
>    }`. Then create one `Node` for each `Literal`,
>    `NodeConstruction`, `OrderedBlock`, `Expression`, and `MacroInvocation` item.
>    Their kind names are respectively `literal`, the construction's `name`,
>    `ordered-block`, `expression`, and `macro-invocation`.
> 2. Set each Node's `payload` to
>    `PayloadRef::Text(serde_json::to_string(&DerivedPayloadV1 {
>    schema_version: 1, kind, attributes })?)`, `revision` to `RevisionId(0)`, and
>    flags to `NodeFlags::DERIVED`. Add `HAS_DURABLE_ID` only for a unique string
>    `id` attribute.
> 3. Emit one `contains` Relation from every document, NodeConstruction, or
>    OrderedBlock parent to each Node-producing child. Its payload is the child's
>    zero-based decimal position, preserving declared order.
> 4. Emit `RelationConstruction` directly from its resolved `source` to
>    `Target::Node(target)`, using its `kind`; emit `Reference` from the nearest
>    Node-producing ancestor, or the document Node at top level, to its resolved
>    target with kind `reference`. `AttributeAssignment` emits no graph subject;
>    it changes only its owner's effective payload attributes.
> 5. Every Relation uses `revision = RevisionId(0)`,
>    `RelationFlags::default()`, and `requires = None`. Its payload is
>    `PayloadRef::Text` of `DerivedPayloadV1` for an explicit/reference Relation
>    and the decimal child position for `contains`.
> 
> `KindId` is the first four bytes, big-endian, of
> `BLAKE3(b"liminal:phase1:kind:v1\0" || declared_name_utf8)`, bitwise-OR
> `0x8000_0000`. Resolution records the first name for every result and returns
> `ResolveError::KindCollision` if a distinct, case-sensitive declared name
> collides. No case folding or punctuation normalization occurs. The symbol table is
> built from unique string `id` attributes over the whole document. A duplicate
> produces `DuplicateExplicitId`, neither duplicate is accepted into the symbol
> table, and both Nodes fall back to D19.6 Anchored IDs. Every unresolved target
> produces `UnresolvedReference` and no Relation; it is never redirected.
> For D19.6, `form_kebab` is the `SyntaxForm` tag for an authored subject,
> `node-construction` for the synthetic document Node, `contains` for a generated
> containment Relation, and `reference` for a generated reference Relation. The
> synthetic document provenance spans the whole source; Node/explicit/reference
> provenance uses that HIR item's range; containment provenance uses the child
> item's range. Unique explicit-ID Nodes have `IdentityGrade::Explicit`; every
> other Node and every Relation has `IdentityGrade::Anchored`.
> Every public item, field, function, method, and enum variant specified above
> receives a doc comment citing v4 §§10–17, §21, or §121 as applicable.
>

<a id="source-912804baf2965f31a468"></a>

Classification: `mixed-clause`. Original lines 566–607; text SHA-256: `af57503e9dae9dedb61f76bd127f87d28d57fce93ddc51e1c6c1dc3ba0988ea5`.

<!-- source-block:source-912804baf2965f31a468 -->
> ## Algorithms
> 
> 1. Walk the M18 typed CST in source order and create annotations for each token,
>    error region, attribute, reference, and recognized form. Allocate dense
>    `HirId`s preorder from zero; validate the complete SourceMap before returning.
> 2. Lower compact Markdown sugar and explicit syntax into the same eight-form HIR
>    using the production mapping above.
>    Explicit syntax accepts only `literal`, `node`, `relation`, `attribute`,
>    `ordered`, `reference`, `expression`, and `macro`; unknown forms become HIR
>    diagnostics while their M18 CST bytes remain lossless. Integer overflow,
>    malformed syntax, and ownerless
>    attributes likewise produce typed, nonfatal HIR diagnostics; invalid source
>    maps and dangling resolved HIR IDs are fatal `HirError`s.
> 3. Resolve HIR at one caller-supplied `WorkspaceBasis`. Materialize symbolic
>    D19.8 defaults and local references; retain unresolved references as
>    `ResolveDiagnostic`s;
>    never perform I/O inside lowering. Derive IDs by D19.6, mark every Node
>    `NodeFlags::DERIVED`, attach Anchored provenance to every Node and Relation,
>    sort by ID, and reject dangling Relations. Return those nonfatal diagnostics
>    beside the graph in `ResolvedGraph`; Basis mismatch and dangling derived
>    relations remain fatal `ResolveError`s.
> 4. Convert `DerivedGraph` to `DebugGraphV1`, validate every invariant, serialize
>    with the fixed v1 framing, deserialize with `deny_unknown_fields`, and require
>    structural equality. No JSON bytes are used as a governing store snapshot.
> 5. Canonical emission writes `#!liminal-explicit-v1\n`, then walks normalized
>    HIR: attributes sort lexicographically, children retain declared order,
>    literals use JSON string escaping, and every implicit default is written
>    explicitly. Parsing compact or explicit input with one formatter instance,
>    emitting canonical explicit form, and parsing again through that same
>    instance must produce an equal `Phase1Document` under D19.7.
> 6. Fill the existing law test with compact/explicit pairs covering all eight forms,
>    derived-graph provenance, malformed-but-retained regions, and deterministic
>    repetition. Invoke
>    `laws::check_canonical_round_trip` unchanged, then exercise strict v1 rejection
>    in the same existing test. The positive JSON case must satisfy
>    `serialize(deserialize(serialize(value))) == serialize(value)` byte-for-byte.
>    Negative cases must reject malformed JSON, a wrong version, duplicate IDs,
>    dangling endpoints, a non-derived node, missing Node provenance, missing
>    Relation provenance, Basis/source-hash mismatch, and an unknown or missing
>    field. Do not duplicate or weaken the generic law and do not create another
>    test.
>

<!-- source-block:source-a6aaa541708f9acea57b -->
> ## Exit gate
>

<!-- source-block:source-21a3f8958a1024995576 -->
> ## Pre-made decisions
> 
> - **D20.0 (AM-17.3) —** `lim fmt` MUST format through
>   `Formatter::emit_in_dialect` with the source's own dialect, never through
>   `emit`. Formatting a compact Markdown document must return compact Markdown;
>   rewriting it to `#!liminal-explicit-v1` on save would destroy the surface the
>   reader chose.
> 
> - **D20.1 —** formatting is `parse → canonical emit`; it normalizes spelling and
>   whitespace but never changes the M19 semantic graph.
> - **D20.2 —** one formatter implementation serves the library and all three CLI
>   paths; CLI code may not reimplement parsing, canonicalization, or diagnostics.
> - **D20.3 —** `lim fmt` formats every governed external-file Holder selected by
>   the explicit workspace root, in normalized path order, using per-file atomic
>   replacement only when bytes differ. It preflights every selected Holder before
>   the first write; once replacement begins, each completed file is durable and
>   later write failure is reported as a partial failure with exact file
>   coordinates, not hidden behind a false workspace-transaction claim.
> - **D20.4 —** `lim check` performs parse, source-map, derived-graph, and formatter
>   checks without writing; success is byte-silent and failures use deterministic
>   path/range/code ordering with domain-native vocabulary.
> - **D20.5 —** `lim expand` never writes source and prints exactly one canonical
>   M19 debug-JSON document plus one trailing newline.
> - **D20.6 —** malformed/opaque CST regions are preserved byte-for-byte. A region
>   the formatter cannot safely canonicalize is emitted unchanged with a check
>   diagnostic; it is never guessed or dropped.
> - **D20.7 —** all positive, negative, malformed, and replay assertions are folded
>   into the existing named gate so the declared test inventory does not change.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-21a3f8958a1024995576 -->

<a id="source-4d4e6a8b3c52cc2eaaad"></a>

Classification: `mixed-clause`. Original lines 59–74; text SHA-256: `f5e774c9c2e40bd1740a5612a06aa6056139fe5b869edba818a50479cdb5d1fa`.

<!-- source-block:source-4d4e6a8b3c52cc2eaaad -->
> ## Data schemas
> 
> No new persisted schema. The command contract is exactly:
> 
> ```text
> lim --workspace <root> fmt
> lim --workspace <root> check
> lim --workspace <root> expand
> ```
> 
> `fmt` writes only changed governed source files and otherwise emits zero bytes.
> `check` never writes. `expand` writes canonical ADR-0016/M19 JSON to stdout and
> nothing to stderr on success. Source diagnostics are sorted tuples
> `(workspace_relative_path, start_byte, end_byte, code, message)`; byte offsets
> refer to the exact Holder bytes at the selected Basis.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-4d4e6a8b3c52cc2eaaad -->

<a id="source-d56fc777039bf0c83f01"></a>

Classification: `mixed-clause`. Original lines 75–94; text SHA-256: `ad96d0801a159b3c4431fdf73a074ab1c09ab3b9a5c8df94c03ee8b6800d60a9`.

<!-- source-block:source-d56fc777039bf0c83f01 -->
> ## Algorithms
> 
> 1. Enumerate governed external-file Holders, reject non-concrete or ambiguous
>    Holders, normalize paths, and process them in bytewise path order.
> 2. Parse through M18. Canonically emit supported CST nodes; copy opaque and
>    malformed regions verbatim. Reparse emitted bytes and compare the M19
>    canonical graph with the pre-format graph.
> 3. Run the formatter twice. Freeze `F20_IDEMPOTENT = second_bytes == first_bytes`
>    and `F20_SEMANTIC = graph_before == graph_after` in
>    `formatter_idempotence_law_holds` over valid, malformed, and already-formatted
>    fixtures.
> 4. For `fmt`, stage all changed bytes first and perform no write unless every
>    file passes Algorithm 3. Replace changed files one at a time with fsync-backed
>    atomic replacement in normalized path order. If a write fails after replacement
>    begins, preserve already completed files, stop, and report the exact partial
>    failure coordinates for rerun/recovery.
> 5. For `check`, run the same parse and comparison without emission side effects.
>    For `expand`, serialize the M19 graph with its canonicalizer and append one
>    newline.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-d56fc777039bf0c83f01 -->

<!-- source-block:source-c710f81aae7fe4adddbf -->
> ## Pre-made decisions
> 
> - **D21.1 —** add exact Salsa 0.28.0 to workspace dependencies with
>   `default-features = false`; `liminal-query` is its only direct production
>   consumer in this milestone.
> - **D21.2 —** Salsa is a private execution mechanism behind Liminal-owned source,
>   Basis, compiler, dependency, and diagnostic interfaces.
> - **D21.3 —** source bytes/revision and every selected Workspace Basis component
>   are explicit inputs. Current directory, clock, environment, filesystem reads,
>   resolver calls, and mutable singleton state are forbidden query inputs.
> - **D21.4 —** full and incremental paths may share published input/data schemas
>   but not the incremental cache, changed-key set, or expected-output builder.
> - **D21.5 —** output equality is byte-exact canonical M19 graph JSON plus ordered
>   diagnostics and, after M22, deterministic HTML; pointer or Salsa-ID equality
>   is never evidence.
> - **D21.6 —** changing one Basis component invalidates only queries whose recorded
>   `ComponentDeps` contain that key. Irrelevant-component mutations must leave
>   results byte-identical and cached dependencies unchanged.
> - **D21.7 —** all differential, stale-Basis, malformed, negative, and replay
>   assertions live in the existing gate so the test inventory stays fixed.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-c710f81aae7fe4adddbf -->

<a id="source-8c1faaaee8ad76a55f0c"></a>

Classification: `mixed-clause`. Original lines 53–66; text SHA-256: `b1046c1225ab02a2bcff776bf7b61aefced54221646b6108f59a3e4d8bd69766`.

<!-- source-block:source-8c1faaaee8ad76a55f0c -->
> ## Data schemas
> 
> No persisted query schema. Liminal owns the in-memory boundary:
> 
> ```text
> FullCompileInput        = (source_bytes, source_revision, WorkspaceBasis)
> IncrementalCompileInput = (source_bytes, source_revision, ordered_edits, WorkspaceBasis)
> CompileOutput           = (canonical_graph_json, ordered_diagnostics, ComponentDeps)
> ```
> 
> `ordered_edits` are M18 byte edits in ascending `(start, old_end, new_end)` order
> and must be non-overlapping. Diagnostics use M20's deterministic tuple. Salsa
> keys and revisions never serialize or cross the `liminal-query` crate boundary.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-8c1faaaee8ad76a55f0c -->

<a id="source-6208874718eb82222f48"></a>

Classification: `mixed-clause`. Original lines 67–84; text SHA-256: `f7f251ccf0541637ae50fc0706c41be7c573166ab2a0375a7c988aadcf5106d9`.

<!-- source-block:source-6208874718eb82222f48 -->
> ## Algorithms
> 
> 1. Add the pinned dependency at the workspace root and consume it privately from
>    `liminal-query`; compile with default features disabled.
> 2. Build the full oracle from a fresh database populated only by the declared
>    source and Basis inputs. Run M18 parse and M19 lowering without incremental
>    state.
> 3. Build the incremental path from the same public input values, apply ordered
>    edits, update only changed explicit inputs, and request the same Liminal-owned
>    output query.
> 4. Compare canonical graph bytes, ordered diagnostics, and recorded Basis
>    dependencies. Freeze `Q21_EQUAL = incremental == full` and
>    `Q21_PRECISE = changed_keys ∩ deps == invalidated_keys` in
>    `incremental_equals_full_compile_law_holds`.
> 5. Replay every case from a fresh database and randomized irrelevant Basis
>    changes. A stale, missing, or ambiguous Basis fails closed; no query performs
>    recovery or external resolution.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-6208874718eb82222f48 -->

<!-- source-block:source-8fdd86abd331ef64ab96 -->
> ## Scope
> 
> Create the native `backends/html` crate, render M19 Human IR to deterministic
> escaped full HTML, and produce minimal block patches whose application is
> byte-identical to a fresh render at the same Basis. This order does not add a
> browser DOM runtime, JavaScript, CSS framework, Pandoc process, daemon preview
> protocol, rich editor, or compiled Jurisdiction plan
> (`docs/implementation-plan.md` §4 items 4, 6, 11, 12).
>

<a id="source-6f12b585cf0a4964bc6e"></a>

Classification: `mixed-clause`. Original lines 32–55; text SHA-256: `3ddf96d55f97c9090b5691b6ffd378d82df818388daa27be1f327ba7dcec928e`.

<!-- source-block:source-6f12b585cf0a4964bc6e -->
> ## Pre-made decisions
> 
> - **D22.1 —** add `backends/*` to workspace members and create one publish-false
>   Rust library crate `liminal-html`; it consumes Liminal-owned IR, never parser
>   events or Salsa types.
> - **D22.2 —** escape text and attribute values deterministically:
>   `& → &amp;`, `< → &lt;`, `> → &gt;`, `" → &quot;`, and `' → &#39;`, in that
>   recognition order so introduced ampersands are not escaped twice.
> - **D22.3 —** unsupported or raw-HTML-like IR is an explicit render error. Source
>   bytes are never inserted as trusted markup and no sanitizer is treated as an
>   excuse for unsafe generation.
> - **D22.4 —** full output is UTF-8 with prefix `<!doctype html>\n<html>\n<body>\n`,
>   suffix `</body>\n</html>\n`, source-order blocks, deterministic attributes,
>   and exactly one trailing newline.
> - **D22.5 —** a patch replaces one stable M19 block at one explicit target Basis.
>   Patches sort by new-document source order and contain already escaped complete
>   replacement fragments.
> - **D22.6 —** unchanged blocks emit no patch. Applying the ordered patch set to
>   the old full document must equal a fresh full render byte-for-byte; otherwise
>   patch generation fails closed.
> - **D22.7 —** full goldens and patch/full equality are independent authorities:
>   expected full HTML is reviewed fixture text, while patch tests compare against
>   a separately invoked fresh renderer.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-6f12b585cf0a4964bc6e -->

<a id="source-116f08f1705495c0c69f"></a>

Classification: `mixed-clause`. Original lines 56–73; text SHA-256: `9ebb968f90bf6bd3a2ed9455048407c62f5f44e17d8694676873022f88abbfe3`.

<!-- source-block:source-116f08f1705495c0c69f -->
> ## Data schemas
> 
> No persisted backend format. The in-memory patch record is field-for-field:
> 
> ```rust
> pub struct HtmlPatch {
>     pub basis: WorkspaceBasis,
>     pub block: NodeId,
>     pub replacement: String,
> }
> ```
> 
> `replacement` is one complete escaped block fragment with its final newline.
> The vector is sorted by the block's new-document source order; duplicate block
> IDs, missing old targets, mixed Bases, or overlapping replacements are errors.
> Full-render fixture pairs live under `conformance/fixtures/phase1/html/` and
> reviewed snapshots under the existing `classes` integration-test snapshot path.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-116f08f1705495c0c69f -->

<a id="source-11793e946dfcd77bfc55"></a>

Classification: `mixed-clause`. Original lines 74–91; text SHA-256: `725eea5dc059a6612bb4c10d0265be475bab12874984dbbc5513c97b7261d0b9`.

<!-- source-block:source-11793e946dfcd77bfc55 -->
> ## Algorithms
> 
> 1. Lower only published M19 Human-IR roles to a closed HTML tag mapping. Sort
>    attributes by bytewise name, escape all text/attribute data with D22.2, and
>    reject unknown roles or invalid structural nesting.
> 2. Render full output using D22.4 constants. Freeze exact bytes per fixture in
>    the existing `full_document_html_matches_golden` snapshot gate; accepting or
>    changing any golden is T1.
> 3. Given old and new M19 documents plus their explicit Bases, identify changed
>    stable blocks from canonical IR equality, render only those blocks, and emit
>    D22.5 patches in new source order.
> 4. Apply patches with an implementation independent from patch selection. Freeze
>    `H22_PATCH_EQ = apply(render(old), patches) == render(new)` and the
>    unchanged-block exclusion in `incremental_patch_equals_full_render`.
> 5. Exercise text containing every escape character, hostile tag/attribute text,
>    malformed opaque source, reordered blocks, deletion/insertion, stale Basis,
>    and deterministic replay inside the two existing gates.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-11793e946dfcd77bfc55 -->

<!-- source-block:source-578048a5bcc96724ef1c -->
> ## Pre-made decisions
> 
> - **D23.1 (AM-23.2) —** the seven production fuzz targets are `cst_parse`,
>   `format_idempotent`, `canonical_round_trip`, `incremental_full_equivalence`,
>   `html_render`, `graph_interchange_codec`, and `ilrp_recovery`; together they
>   exercise parser, formatter, projection, incremental compiler, native
>   renderer, graph interchange, and ILRP recovery.
> - **D23.2 —** each target starts with at least 16 declared, non-locked seeds and
>   stores minimized failures under its own target directory. A failure is fixed
>   only after its minimized input is committed and replayed by
>   `fuzz_regressions_stay_fixed`.
> - **D23.3 —** activate the existing Phase 1 charter entries `cold_startup` and
>   `mem_per_node_and_relation`. The exact gated inventory is those two plus
>   `store_append_txn`, `store_commit_fsync`, `store_recover_1k_records`,
>   `relation_traversal`, and `graph_query_latency`. Each records exactly 30
>   independent samples on the recorded reference environment. Candidate median
>   and p95 values must be no more than 10% and 15% above baseline respectively;
>   equality at either threshold passes. A missing or extra benchmark,
>   environment mismatch, or missing raw sample fails closed.
> - **D23.4 —** accepting or replacing a benchmark baseline is T1. A regression
>   is investigated or separately approved; the executor never blesses the
>   slower candidate merely to make the gate green.
> - **D23.5 —** `old_snapshots_open_after_format_evolution` remains ignored. Only
>   an accepted first persisted-format ADR activates its fixtures and flip; M23
>   does not infer that decision from the presence of debug JSON.
> - **D23.6 —** fuzzing and benchmarking use development/regression inputs only.
>   Existing approved black-box verifiers remain the sole interface to locked
>   acceptance inputs.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-578048a5bcc96724ef1c -->

<a id="source-6ca65c64a5b718b4c3af"></a>

Classification: `mixed-clause`. Original lines 62–115; text SHA-256: `d64f75e80635c42c0f38b47c55d86320d1c4a808679332d40719345bad9f5079`.

<!-- source-block:source-6ca65c64a5b718b4c3af -->
> ## Data schemas
> 
> `fuzz/targets.toml` contains exactly seven `[[target]]` records, sorted by `name`:
> 
> ```toml
> [[target]]
> name = "<D23.1 name>"
> family = "<cst|format|projection|incremental|render>"
> seed_dir = "fuzz/corpus/<name>"
> regression_dir = "conformance/corpora/regression/phase1/<name>"
> minimum_seed_count = 16
> ```
> 
> Each minimized regression is stored as
> `conformance/corpora/regression/phase1/<target>/<sha256>.case` plus
> `<sha256>.json`:
> 
> ```json
> {
>   "schema_version": 1,
>   "target": "<D23.1 name>",
>   "input_sha256": "<64 lowercase hex>",
>   "discovered_seed": "<recorded seed>",
>   "reproducer": "<exact cargo fuzz command>"
> }
> ```
> 
> `benches/baselines/phase1.json` is canonical UTF-8 JSON with benchmarks sorted
> by `name`:
> 
> ```json
> {
>   "schema_version": 1,
>   "artifact_kind": "<baseline|candidate>",
>   "subject_commit": "<40 lowercase hex>",
>   "compared_baseline_commit": "<null for baseline; 40 lowercase hex for candidate>",
>   "reference_environment": "<recorded environment identifier>",
>   "toolchain": "<exact rustc version>",
>   "sample_count": 30,
>   "benchmarks": [
>     {
>       "name": "<fully qualified Divan benchmark name>",
>       "unit": "<ns|bytes>",
>       "samples": ["<30 JSON u64 values>"],
>       "median": "<u64>",
>       "p95": "<u64>"
>     }
>   ]
> }
> ```
> 
> Baseline and candidate use the same schema; raw samples, not pre-rounded
> percentages, are authoritative.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-6ca65c64a5b718b4c3af -->

<a id="source-ec3bc9331e3c65100a59"></a>

Classification: `mixed-clause`. Original lines 116–144; text SHA-256: `6f4d74dc04571ce46e706e22b7d77ce22353308220a9f31721d5c26828c3e6af`.

<!-- source-block:source-ec3bc9331e3c65100a59 -->
> ## Algorithms
> 
> 1. Create one `cargo-fuzz` target for each D23.1 name. Every target treats
>    panic, timeout, invalid memory behavior, nondeterminism, or disagreement with
>    its independent/reference oracle as failure; it never filters an input after
>    observing failure.
> 2. Seed each target with at least 16 declared valid, boundary, truncated,
>    malformed, and hostile development/regression inputs. `just fuzz-smoke`
>    executes every target with its committed seeds; the qualification run
>    executes each target sanitizer-enabled for 31 minutes, exceeding ADR-0020's
>    30-minute minimum without changing that minimum.
> 3. Minimize every failure, hash the exact minimized bytes, write the `.case` and
>    metadata pair, then implement `fuzz_regressions_stay_fixed` as deterministic
>    replay through the owning API. The test fails on a missing metadata pair,
>    hash mismatch, panic, or reappearance of the recorded defect.
> 4. Run every implemented benchmark in the same recorded environment for exactly
>    30 samples and sort ascending. Median is the truncating integer mean of
>    samples 15 and 16 (one-based); nearest-rank p95 is sample 29. Avoid rounded
>    percentages: require `candidate_median * 100 <= baseline_median * 110` and
>    `candidate_p95 * 100 <= baseline_p95 * 115` with checked integer arithmetic
>    for every benchmark.
> 5. `just bench-gate` emits the baseline/candidate value and both percentages for
>    every benchmark, exits nonzero on any threshold or provenance mismatch, and
>    never rewrites the accepted baseline. Baseline creation or replacement is a
>    separate T1 step.
> 6. Leave the migration test ignored unless an accepted persisted-format ADR
>    explicitly names the format and activation fixtures. Discovering such an ADR
>    is an escalation to its owning work order, not an implicit M23 edit.
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-ec3bc9331e3c65100a59 -->

> # Phases 0–12 — work breakdown structure
> 
> Tiered-fidelity rule: Phase -1 has full mechanical work orders (`M01.md`–`M12.md`).
> The phases below are decomposed to task level — enough to size and sequence the
> work — and each phase's **mechanical work orders are authored at the preceding
> gate, using [`template.md`](template.md)**. Writing them earlier would be fiction:
> the falsification law (Law 14) means earlier phases reshape later ones.
> 
> Every phase's gating tests either already exist as phase-tagged `#[ignore]`d
> tests in `conformance/` (named below) or are authored born-ignored at the
> preceding gate. `just gates` tracks both.
> 
> Work orders authored at each gate carry executor-tier tags (`[T1]`–`[T4]`,
> defined in [`00-protocol.md`](00-protocol.md) §7) on every step, so the
> responsibility split — what demands extreme rigor vs what is delegable
> mechanics — is decided at authoring time, not rediscovered per session.
> Authoring the work orders themselves is always T1.
> 
> Pre-known ADR points come from spec v4 Part XXIII (§119–§131), pinned here to the
> phase that must decide them.
> 
> ---
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-52333e0d8527a28ae47b -->

<!-- source-block:source-f6431e75f3edb69ca27e -->
> ## Phase 0 — Constitution, profiles, corpus, conformance laws
> 
> **Inputs:** the go/no-go ADR + full ADR trail; frozen Contract types
> (`liminal-jurisdiction`); the M07 identity matrix + grade ADR; M09/M10 capability
> reports + level ADR; the M11 corpus, denominators, and scorecard pipeline;
> `template.md`.
> 
> **Tasks:**
> 1. Write the kernel spec (Node/Relation) from the live types into `spec/kernel.md`.
> 2. Freeze the interpretive Contract interpreter + Workspace Basis spec as
>    normative text.
> 3. Author the tiered-vocabulary doc (domain-native UI ceiling, R4 §3).
> 4. Extend held-out coverage per stable profile (heldout/v2 if new trace
>    categories — v1 scores retained).
> 5. Publish the mutation-local repair law + unified RepairPlan/Promotion semantics.
> 6. Publish the ILRP spec + recovery fixtures from `fixtures/ilrp-crash-matrix/`.
> 7. Publish Overlay-aging + queue rules; identity grades + dual entity/version
>    model; projection levels + lens laws.
> 8. Encode the §14 transform-contract model as data.
> 9. Publish fixture-format + torture-corpus documentation.
> 10. Write the threat model (supersedes SECURITY.md's placeholder).
> 11. Record prior-art adoption decisions (v4 §118A).
> 12. Re-measure annotated-source anchor recovery over the real CST (Phase 1
>     input); merge-class ≥95% is the L3 bar; new time-box, new report — the M09
>     L2 demotion stands until then (AM-9.2, M09.7 verdict).
> 
> **Gating tests:** all of `phase_minus_1.rs`, both
> `slo::*_graduates_on_heldout_corpus`, and `heldout_manifest_locked` stay green.
> At the M12 gate, `conformance/tests/phase0.rs` adds 18 born-ignored tests: the
> roadmap's no-new-primitive, every-example-resolves, and sound-session conjunction,
> plus strict negative-fixture, live-shape, crash-inventory, ADR, transform-schema,
> threat-model, real-CST measurement, adversarial-review-packet, and Phase 0
> go/no-go checks assigned exactly across M13–M17.

<!-- source-block:source-1b26ac4e52246127c39c -->
> # Phase 0 execution amendments
> 
> **Status:** open ledger. Created at the M12 gate; closed by the M17 Phase 0
> amendment-disposition ADR.
> 
> Each entry is `AM-<milestone>.<number> (M<nn>): <one sentence>`. Entries are
> append-only while Phase 0 is active. M17 ratifies or reverts every entry in one
> immutable ADR; absence of entries is recorded explicitly there.
> 
> AM-17.1 (M17): Phase 1 suite eligibility gains the HAQP-1 qualification profile
> from accepted ADR-0020: bidirectional traceability, 64 semantic mutants at 100%
> applicable kill rate, gate canaries, five deterministic generated/fuzz families,
> independent oracles, exhaustive registered crash boundaries, and blinded two-pass
> adversarial review; M17's five gate names and predicted counts remain unchanged.
> 
> AM-17.2 (M17): the Phase 1 crates implemented during M17 (`liminal-cst`,
> `liminal-cir`, `liminal-hir`, `liminal-format`, and the `liminal-query`
> `ParagraphCompiler`) are declared **HAQP qualification substrate**, not
> executed Phase 1 work. HAQP-1 cannot mutate, fuzz, or oracle-check code that
> does not exist, so building them under M17 was necessary; but their existence
> must not satisfy Phase 1 exit gates that M18-M24 have not executed. The seven
> Phase 1 exit-gate tests (`formatter_idempotence_law_holds`,
> `canonical_round_trip_law_holds`, `incremental_equals_full_compile_law_holds`,
> `malformed_source_never_panics_and_round_trips`, `fuzz_regressions_stay_fixed`,
> `full_document_html_matches_golden`, `incremental_patch_equals_full_render`)
> are therefore returned to their original `#[ignore = "Phase 1: ..."]` tags
> verbatim, to be un-ignored by the milestone that earns each one. Substrate
> code is retained, not reverted. Resolves M17.5 finding F-02; restores M17.8's
> predicted meter (backlog 23 now, 21 after the two Phase 0 gates flip).
> 
> AM-17.3 (M17): the `liminal_format::Formatter` seam gains
> `emit_in_dialect(&self, doc, dialect) -> Result<String, Self::Error>` with a
> default implementation delegating to `emit`, so no existing implementor changes
> behavior. `emit` remains the canonical projection (always explicit surface) and
> was NOT mutated. Rationale: `format()` is `emit(parse(x))`, so a compact
> Markdown document was lowered to `#!liminal-explicit-v1` on every format — M19
> requires the canonical round-trip law "across compact and explicit", and M20's
> `lim fmt` must not rewrite a reader's chosen surface on save. `MarkdownFormatter`
> implements the compact surface for the compact-representable subset (a
> `paragraph` node whose only child is a literal, carrying at most an `id`) and
> falls back to the explicit surface for anything richer, never emitting a lossy
> approximation. Addition over mutation, per Brian's direction 2026-07-20.
> 
> AM-17.4 (user-ratified 2026-08-08, ADR-0021): stage HAQP-1 around Phase 1
> authorization. M17.5's exit criterion becomes **HAQP-1a** — everything ADR-0020
> requires except §3's mutant clauses, which defer to **HAQP-1b** at M24.
> 
> Rationale (M17.5 finding F-28): §3 requires 64 semantic mutants at a 100% kill
> rate, and all 35 distinct killing tests backing the packet's 65 mutants were
> unrunnable — 27 did not exist and 8 are `#[ignore]`d under AM-17.2. Lifting the
> quarantine needs Phase 1 authorization, which M17.6 grants AFTER M17.5. ADR-0020
> §3 assumed the suite it mutates already exists; for Phase 1 it does not.
> 
> No threshold is reduced: every §3 clause survives verbatim into 1b, only its
> evaluation point moves. §3's gate-canary clause stays in 1a, because canaries
> run against the packet's own gates rather than against Phase 1 tests. The packet
> records `qualification_stage`, and the verifier rejects a 1a packet claiming
> mutant kills as well as a 1b packet without them.
> 
> Also reconciles M17.8's predicted counts, which were authored before the suite
> grew: it predicted 237 active / 21 backlog; the meter reads 356 active / 43
> backlog (Phase 1 deferred rose to 27 as M18–M23's 20 milestone tests were
> written and quarantined). The prediction is corrected rather than the meter.
> 
> AM-17.5 (user-approved 2026-08-14): HAQP requirement coordinates are exact
> anchors, not substring checks; gate rows use complete `## Exit gate` heading
> anchors, semantic `Dnn.n` anchors require identifier boundaries, and packet
> `kind`, `source`, `critical`, and `stateful` fields must match the closed
> authoritative M18–M24 registry in `liminal-xtask`. Blind-review findings may
> link only to `verified_defect` attempts; false-positive and caught-violation
> attempts remain attempt records without emitted findings, and malformed linkage
> blocks the pass. M10's Pandoc pin and golden move to installed 3.10.2.
> 
> AM-17.6 (user-ratified 2026-08-16): the qualification metadata child may lift
> EXACTLY ONE `#[ignore]` — the one on
> `phase1_suite_packet_is_complete_and_unratified` in
> `conformance/tests/phase0.rs` — and change nothing else in that file.
> 
> Rationale: that gate is M17.5's stated exit criterion and it asserts the packet
> is COMPLETE, so it cannot be live before the flip that completes the packet.
> Every other placement fails. Un-ignoring at the fixed base commits a red tree
> and makes the base look broken to anyone who checks it out. Un-ignoring after
> the flip moves HEAD, so `provenance.evidence_parent == HEAD^` no longer holds
> and the qualified gate refuses. The metadata child is the only position left.
> 
> Discovered by running M17.5's exit command as written: it reports
> `0 tests run: 0 passed, 18 skipped`, not the `1 passed` the work order predicts.
> The trap was an ordering constraint nobody had written down, in the same family
> as F-28 and the first ADR-0021 deadlock — no piece is defective, and the
> sequence they compose into is impossible.
> 
> No threshold is reduced and the guarantee is not widened to the file.
> `qualification_metadata_path` still refuses `conformance/tests/phase0.rs`;
> `verify_gate_unignore_only` inspects the DIFF and requires one removed line, no
> added lines, and that the removed line is that exact attribute. Gate logic
> therefore still cannot change in the child, which is what `verify_provenance`
> exists to prevent. Four canaries pin it, including one asserting the pinned
> attribute string still matches the tree — otherwise the check passes vacuously
> against a file it no longer describes.
<!-- /source-block:source-1b26ac4e52246127c39c -->

<!-- source-block:source-a17d44b84c3eb905c882 -->
> ## 1. Purpose and how to read this document
> 
> Liminal is a multi-year project. This document is the on-ramp: it says what gets built, in what order, what is deliberately **not** built, and how "done" is decided at every step.
> 
> **Every Phase -1 milestone has an execution-grade work order** in
> [`docs/execution/`](execution/00-protocol.md) — algorithms, schemas, constants,
> output formats, and step-by-step checklists, pre-decided so an executor
> implements without design work. This document stays the WHAT/WHY; the work
> orders are the HOW. Phases 0–12 are decomposed in
> [`docs/execution/phases.md`](execution/phases.md).
> 
> Three rules govern how to read it:
> 
> 1. **The tests ARE the backlog.** The entire future test surface the spec enumerates (v4 §112 laws, §113 classes, §114 conformance suite, R4 §2.3 SLOs, R4 §10 gates) already exists in `conformance/` as named, compiled tests. Tests whose subject does not exist yet are `#[ignore = "Phase N: <what must exist>"]` with the exact assertion spelled out. There is no separate issue tracker for spec work: if the spec requires it, a named test already demands it.
> 2. **A milestone is done when its named tests flip from `#[ignore]` to passing.** Nothing else counts. Each milestone below lists the exact test names that constitute its exit gate. Un-ignoring a test without making it pass is meaningless; making it pass by weakening its assertion is a spec change and requires an ADR.
> 3. **The spec-debt meter is just gates.** `just gates` parses nextest output into per-phase `passed / ignored` counts. That number is the project's only progress bar. It goes down by doing the work, never by deleting tests.
> 
> Ordering follows **Law 14 (v4 §3): risk-retirement order precedes dependency order.** The build graph may want a parser before an editor, but the research program runs the architecture-killing experiments first. Phase -1 exists to *disprove* the architecture cheaply; everything in it is interpretive reference semantics, and everything that smells like production engineering is forbidden (see §4 below).
> 
> ---
>

> ### M1 — Skeleton + honest durability substrate (1 week)
> 
> - **Goal:** everything that will later be crashed on purpose must first be honestly durable. No milestone builds on a store whose fsync discipline is untested.
> - **Builds:** `liminal-graph/src/store/` — hand-rolled append-only NDJSON log (`<crc32-hex> <canonical-json>\n` framing, fsync-before-return, recovery truncates at the first bad line = longest checksummed prefix), atomic snapshot replacement (`tmp → fsync → rename → fsync(dir)`, v4 §92), fs4 single-writer advisory lock. `liminal-daemon/src/crash.rs` — `EnvCrashInjector` (see §3 below). First slice of the `conformance` `ToyRun` harness.
> - **Exit gate:** `prop_torn_tail_truncates_cleanly` (proptest: truncate log at a random byte → reopen → exact checksummed prefix, no panic), `snapshot_replace_atomic_under_abort`, `fault_abort_exits_with_sigabrt` (proves the injector kills with a real SIGABRT, no unwinding, no flushes).
> 
<!-- /source-block:source-4ee13a2d082ddd6bcce6 -->

> ### M2 — **Killer #1**: ILRP coordinator + full crash matrix on single-step file promotion (2 weeks)
> 
> - **Goal:** falsify the Intent-Logged Repair Protocol (v4 §7.8, R4 §7) — the claim that a cross-Holder repair can be crash-resumed at *every* durable boundary and always terminate in `Committed`, `NeedsReview`, or `Aborted` with no hidden half-state, no duplication, and no lost bytes.
> - **Builds:** `liminal-jurisdiction/src/ilrp.rs` made real — `IntentState` transitions, `IlrpDriver::{prepare, run, recover_all}`, `PrestateMatch::{Prestate, Poststate, Neither}` (`Neither` → stop, **never guess**). `liminal-source` staging (`stage()/commit_if(expected_pre)` with scannable `.lim-staged` siblings). The `promote_single_step` scenario driven through `liminald exec`, killed at every registered fault point per the crash-matrix machinery of §3.
> - **Exit gate:** `crash_matrix_promote_single_step` (every `(point, occurrence)` from the baseline hit trace → crash → recover → terminal state, world digest correct, recovery idempotent), `recovery_never_guesses` (a third-party mutation between apply and recovery — the "third-state file" — must land in `NeedsReview` with zero bytes lost, never silently reconciled).
> - **Failure consequence:** revises ILRP's contract (R4 §7) before anything else is built. This is why it runs second, not last.
>

The two-step DAG scenario: source-ID insertion must precede Relation reattachment (v4 §-1.0).

> - **Failure consequence:** reshapes the repair/Promotion contract (R4 §§4–6) and possibly the Operation set, before Overlays or Bases are layered on top.

Completing M6 un-ignores the **`gate::minus1_0`** suite — the twelve R4 §10 required-result tests.

> ### M7 — **Killer #4**: persistent-identity torture corpus (2 weeks)
> 
> - **Goal:** falsify the identity-grade claims (v4 §19, Law 12, Law 13) empirically: no strategy may claim stronger continuity than the corpus demonstrates (v4 §-1.1).
> - **Builds:** the identity lab in `conformance/` — **6 strategies** (inline IDs, sidecars, immutable content hashes, structural matching, revision anchors, managed graph IDs) × **11 operations** (rename/move, split, merge, copy/paste, duplicate identical blocks, delete+recreate, formatter rewrites, arbitrary external-editor changes, git merge, git rebase, git cherry-pick with conflict resolution) × seeds → an identity guarantee matrix. Git operations use the **real `git` CLI in hermetic temp repos** (`GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null`, fixed dates/author, pinned version) — explicitly **not** git2/gitoxide, because they do not reproduce merge-ort behavior, and merge-ort is what users' files actually go through.
> - **Exit gate:** `matrix_matches_golden` (byte-exact golden of the guarantee matrix), `claims_never_exceed_evidence` (every declared `IdentityGrade` ≤ the worst demonstrated outcome for that strategy — the spec's "no strategy may claim stronger continuity than the corpus demonstrates" made executable).
> - **Failure consequence:** demotes identity grades in the standard profiles (v4 §7.6) and feeds directly into what M9 and Phase 0 may honestly promise.
>
